mr president, in december the european court of justice delivered a long-awaited judgment with worrying implications for the protection of posted workers in europe. it is a negative signal to our citizens who are concerned about the risks of social dumping. what does the court say in this so-called 'laval' judgment? that the swedish trade unions were wrong to want to impose on a latvian company the adherence to their collective agreement, especially with regard to the minimum wage. the 1996 directive requires posted workers to comply with a core of mandatory rules on minimum protection in the host member state. the court held that the swedish collective agreement system was not involved and that only the law could impose standards. the european message is therefore no longer readable: on the one hand, the commission is putting forward flexicurity and the collective bargaining system as a model, on the other hand, the court of justice is disqualifying this model. parliament and the council must therefore shed light on this matter, otherwise it would be like accepting the bolkenstein directive, which went out the door, and came back through the window, which would be completely unacceptable.

madam president, with the suicides of workers at renault and peugeot in france, the thousands of lung cancers among workers in the asbestos industries, there is obviously a problem of occupational health. the european commission presents a communication to act on the health strategy, but in reality when we read it we are faced with a walt disney resolution, written by snow white for her seven dwarfs. and it is very cute. so, in paragraph 35 of the resolution, we are told that we must have healthy lifestyles at work; in paragraph 29, medical examinations are required; in paragraph 54, fire extinguishers are required; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european parliament is not left in the lurch. fortunately, the rapporteur from the committee on industry has given us solutions, with a psychologist and a chaplain for every 500 employees. but in reality we are not told anything about the causes of occupational diseases. there are three of them. first, the ideology of lowering our border protections that puts our workers in unfair competition with slave laborers in asia. to resist, it is the race for productivity at the expense of health. secondly, the foolish policy of a strong euro deprives us of monetary competitiveness. the only adjustment variable is an increase in productivity, with health also compromised. finally, the neurotic philosophy of competitiveness is the economic war between europe, asia or latin america. but in war there are wounded and dead, as well as sick and injured workers. in other words, the european worker is in the global economic arena like a stressed and bloodied battle bull that is going to the end of its health. the solution, then, is to get our workers out of this unfair global arena, and it's called a new customs technology of deductible tariffs.

the agenda calls for the report by roberta angelilli, on behalf of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, on the european strategy on the rights of the child (2007/2093 (ini)) (a6-0520/2007).
mr president, commissioner, i am pleased that the commission is proposing the establishment of a european strategy on the rights of the child. a large part of european policies affects children and therefore specific action is needed to protect their rights and enable them to participate actively. i am particularly pleased that parliament is calling for a definition of the concept of a child in danger. this instrument will enable us to provide specialised help to children who are victims of a particular social situation, endangering their mental and physical integrity. on the other hand, we cannot abandon children in poverty to their fate. these children do not always receive the protection they need because their parents cannot afford it. they need special help so that they are not condemned to social exclusion, and states must have the responsibility to ensure access to health and education for all children, regardless of the social or legal status of their parents, in order to guarantee, in practice, equal opportunities for all. i would also like to stress the special situation of migrant children. administrative detention of children is unacceptable. we cannot understand that people fleeing war or despair are considered criminals, much less children, who should all be protected and educated according to the convention on the rights of the child.
mr president, madam commissioner, mr rapporteur, this proposal for a regulation to introduce remote sensing by satellite is an interesting one. in the 1990s, michel debatisse, the boss of french farmers, had already proposed a remote sensing project for livestock farms. the aim was to put electronic ear chips in cattle and sheep, in particular to control the allocation of premiums and to prevent fraud in certain departments in the south of france. the idea was even to have electronic capsules that the cattle would swallow, that would be attached to one of the pockets of their digestive tract and that would be sorted by satellite. today it is something different, a story that is already seven years old, with its pilot projects mars or lucas. this involves providing information on land use, soil condition or crop condition to forecast yields and, at the same time, manage agricultural markets and manufacture econometric models. this objective of collecting information, supplying statistics, making forecasts, even making a computer site obviously involves a risk - i was going to say a risk initiated by remote sensing, because it will only be accessible to large farmers or very rich regions and, at the same time, it will not allow everyone to anticipate prices, especially when the price of cereals is rising; the fact that we can anticipate prices several months in advance by predicting what the harvest will be obviously arouses great interest on the stock markets in chicago and elsewhere. it is with great interest, if i may say so, that our rapporteur, graefe zu baringdorf, raises the question of interest, especially since this position is not free. i understand that it was about 10 million, even if it is over five or six years, and that, above all, these amounts will not be taken from an autonomous line but from an agricultural guarantee fund. it is worthwhile, commissioner, to experiment or to pursue it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my polish colleague jacek saryusz-wolski which proposes a favourable opinion of the european parliament on the amendment of the 2004 council regulation on the establishment of partnerships in the framework of the stabilisation and association process. the aim is to change the name of the partnership for the former yugoslav republic of macedonia from 'european partnership' to 'accession partnership', in order to align it with the name of the partnerships established with the other two candidate countries: croatia and turkey. in addition, the independence of montenegro had to be taken into account. as i write these lines, i am thinking of kosovo and hoping for a peaceful and european solution to this difficult situation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council establishing common principles for the levying of airport charges at community airports following the report by my german colleague ulrich stockmann. at a time when european airports, which are mainly publicly owned, are being privatised, when users do not always have an accurate assessment of their consumption of services and when airlines operate in a context with many variables, it was normal to frame the setting of airport charges. i welcome the creation of independent national regulatory authorities to monitor this market and hope that european coordination will be established quickly and that an independent european regulator will eventually emerge.
in writing. i voted, in first reading under the co-decision procedure, a legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on the export and import of dangerous chemicals on the basis of the report by my dutch colleague johannes blokland. i am glad that a compromise has been reached because there is a certain urgency to regularize the legal situation resulting from the annulment of the previous 2003 regulation by the court of justice while improving this regulation to take account of developments since that date.
in writing. i welcome the agreement at first reading that has been reached on this regulation. there are 75 000 different chemicals on the market, with 1 500 more being added each year. this makes it difficult for governments to track and manage the many potentially hazardous substances that cross our borders daily. the regulation will contribute to a more rational use of these dangerous chemicals by facilitating the exchange of information on their characteristics. this will give importing countries the tools and information they need to identify potential hazards and exclude chemicals they cannot handle safely. it is true that exporting countries sometimes have difficulty in obtaining explicit consent from importing countries. but the derogations granted to exporting countries pending consent should now not be valid for more than 12 months. i am pleased that this measure has been adopted, which aims to prevent the uncontrolled import of dangerous chemicals into third countries. this regulation will thus avoid many of the mistakes that have been made in the past and which have caused damage to the environment and public health.
in writing. i voted in favour of the legislative resolution amending, at first reading by codecision, the european commission proposal amending council regulation (eec) no 1408/71 on the application of social security schemes to employed persons, to selfemployed persons and to members of their families moving within the european community, on the basis of the report by my distinguished hungarian colleague csaba ory, which makes technical amendments to the european commission proposal in order to clarify or improve the readability of the regulation. it is welcome that this regulation aims to give a correct picture of the evolution of the legal situation of national social security schemes and thus to ensure adequate coordination at community level.
in writing. on the basis of the own-initiative report of my german friend and colleague jorgo chatzimarkakis, i voted in favour of the resolution on a competitive regulatory framework for the automotive sector following the european commission's communication based on the so-called cars 21 high level group. first of all, i would like to welcome the method of carrying out a genuine industrial audit, with all the parties concerned, with a view to defining an industrial policy for the automobile sector which involves such essential parameters as the impact on purchasing power, employment, safety, mobility, the environment, the regulatory burdens on industry but also innovation, competitiveness, the problem of used cars, the deconstruction of vehicles, etc., and this in an internal market which is far from being finalised. it is imperative that the european union, after having built the internal market by taking care of consumers, should pay particular attention to producers by conducting a european industrial policy with them. the automotive sector, in which we have a long tradition, must be accompanied in the great changes of today.
in writing. the chatzimarkakis report is supposed to outline the competitiveness of the automotive sector in the future, taking into account environmental constraints, product and safety standards, the international competitive context, etc. nevertheless, the endless persecution of motorists is clearly seen. what do traffic restrictions or cross-border enforcement of traffic laws have to do with this? will europeans be forced tomorrow, under pain of sanctions or overtaxation, to buy so-called 'clean' vehicles equipped with costly safety-related technologies, when in a country like france the average age of the car fleet (8 years) is explained by the financial difficulties of citizens and their low purchasing power? why are the only private cars being criticised again, when in france, for example, they are responsible for only 13% of co2 emissions, certainly less than in countries which have not opted for nuclear power? the truth is that there is a fundamental antinomy between wanting a competitive car industry in europe, when all european policies are about raising the cost of cars and impoverishing consumers, while increasing the persecution that discourages the purchase and use of a vehicle.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report proposing the establishment of a competitive regulatory framework for the automotive sector. the roadmap will aim to make cars cleaner and safer and to simplify the legal environment in which european car manufacturers operate. the impact of road transport on air quality must be able to be reduced as the vehicle fleet is renewed. i welcome the adoption by the european parliament of the deadlines, which coincide with the date of 2015, to reach a limit of 125 g/km for cars placed on the market. this date corresponds to the entry into force of the euro vi standards. additional measures could be included in this approach (alternative fuels, eco-driving, taxation, etc.) and particular attention should be paid to biofuels and hydrogen. cars 21 recommends an integrated approach involving vehicle technology, infrastructure and road users to improve road safety (electronic stability control, seatbelt warning lights, brake assist systems, etc.). effective legislation must first be realistic, and the industry has long placed environmental issues at the heart of its policies.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the tax treatment of losses in crossborder situations, based on the own-initiative report of my distinguished colleague, ms piia-noora kauppi, in response to a communication from the european commission on the same subject. i am very concerned about the adverse effects on the functioning of the internal market of the multiplicity of schemes applied by member states in relation to crossborder losses. the timing is particularly appropriate in the context of the recent decision of the european court of justice (ecj) in the marks & spencer case, as in the absence of cross-border deduction of losses, compensation for such losses is generally limited to profits realised in the member state in which the investment was made. this distorts the decisions of companies within the internal market. it seems essential to coordinate the direct taxation systems of the member states within the internal market. but this must be a temporary solution because in the longer term we will have to adopt a common consolidated corporate tax base which is a comprehensive solution for removing the tax obstacles linked to the cross-border offsetting of losses and profits.
in writing. on the basis of the report by my british colleague glenis willmott, i voted for the european parliament resolution on the community strategy for health and safety at work 2007-2012 and in response to the european commission communication on this subject. almost 500 000 people a year die or become permanently disabled from work-related causes and the european commission's target of reducing the average number of accidents at work in the union by 25% is to be welcomed. i support the idea of better action by the european agency for safety and health at work based in bilbao, spain. in this area, and more generally in the construction of social europe, i regret that neither the report nor the european commission's communication stresses the importance of supporting the social partners, who, as we must constantly remind ourselves, have, within the framework of the current treaties with articles 137 et seq. of the treaty establishing the european community (tec) and this has been confirmed by the treaty of lisbon which is being ratified, legal instruments enabling the construction of european social law.
in writing. the objectives, although commendable in form, for health and safety at work for the 2007-2012 calendar year are unlikely to be achieved, as is the case with the lisbon strategy, which was not able to achieve its objectives by 2010. moreover, the disparities in legislation on these matters are so great in europe that it makes their management very difficult at community level, the major risk being that of a bottom-up standardization of these safety and health standards. instead of talking about the strengths and advantages it offers, europe should take concrete action and tackle the issues that really make workers vulnerable: precariousness, unemployment and poverty. only then will the issues of health and safety at work naturally find their place in the regulatory space under construction. our european leaders are wrong: it is not by encouraging immigration that poverty thresholds will be lowered, poverty reduced or growth increased. the only proof of this is that never in the last decade, when immigration has been so high, has growth been so low in relation to the rest of the world. the community strategy for health and safety at work has not taken these parameters into account. we shall therefore vote against this report.

in writing. on the basis of the excellent report by my german colleague kurt lechner, i welcome the adoption by the european parliament, at second reading under the co-decision procedure, of a legislative resolution on the council's common position with a view to adopting the directive on the harmonisation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states relating to consumer credit, replacing the community framework of 1987, as amended twice. i welcome the european commission's intention to establish the conditions for a genuine internal market in consumer credit, to guarantee a high level of consumer protection and to clarify community legislation by revising the three directives of 1987, 1990 and 1998 on consumer credit. i welcome the important work done by my french colleague, jean-paul gauzès, who, with his wisdom and conviction, has made a major contribution to this important compromise which is useful for economic growth, consumer protection and credit institutions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report proposing the harmonisation of the laws of the member states relating to consumer credit. although european households already have the right to seek out bank loans abroad to purchase consumer goods, very few take advantage of this. language barriers, distance and lack of confidence are the most powerful obstacles. the new directive will increase market transparency for the benefit of consumers for loans between eur 200 and eur 75 000. consumers will have the information they need to make informed choices if they decide to buy across borders. in the case of credit offers, the information provided to consumers will be contained in a new european credit information form. consumers will also eventually benefit from a single, comparable overall annual effective rate throughout the eu. the directive will provide consumers with basic information of good quality and easy to compare. the right of withdrawal and the right to repay in advance without paying excessive fees, together with a transparent presentation of their rights and obligations, will give them the confidence to compare prices.
in writing. i voted in favour of the compromise reached by the pse group with the council (amendment no 46), as it allows the balances reached during the german presidency last spring to be maintained. i am glad that the consumer credit as defined in this draft directive has a minimum of eur 200 and a maximum of eur 75 000. i would have preferred, however, that the ceiling had been set at eur 50 000. i am particularly pleased with the qualified majority in the plenary to ensure that the interests of consumers are clearly safeguarded in the event of early repayment of credit. the compensation that the bank may claim will be strictly limited and may be prohibited for loans of less than eur 10 000. in all cases, the fight against over-indebtedness should remain a priority and repayment should be made in a reasonable manner. it is an illusion to think that consumption can be boosted by credit to households: such an approach leads only to impoverishing the most vulnerable consumers. the aim of boosting growth through consumption is to raise wages, not increase credit!
in writing. the report by kurt lechner on the opening of the european consumer credit market was adopted on wednesday 16 january. it seems to me that the transition from a hitherto strongly national market to a european framework, while maintaining a high level of consumer protection, is a first step towards the harmonization of consumer credit rules. the risk of consumer indebtedness remains far too high. it was necessary to monitor and make the solvency of each customer transparent by setting up databases. however, i voted against amendment no 29 on article 16, as did the majority of my colleagues, and i welcome the rejection of it. in my view, this was a real penalty for the consumer who decided to pay off his credit early. the possibility for consumers to terminate credit before it expires is a good initiative. it should not be tainted by an option allowing the lender to claim compensation for any costs in the absence of justified and equitable grounds. so it was necessary to set limits. the lender will therefore not be able to claim compensation exceeding 1% of the amount of the credit.
in writing. the vote on the draft consumer credit directive marks a significant step forward for french ump meps. the final text, thanks to the contribution of the european parliament, and in particular the rapporteur, kurt lechner, favours the opening of borders in a major area of everyday life, while preserving the acquired rights of consumers, particularly the french consumer. the transposition of the directive will therefore make it possible to offer better credit conditions in the future and to limit the risks of over-indebtedness.
in writing. six years after the euro was introduced, europe still lacked a single banking market that would benefit consumers and enable them to realise the benefits of the single currency. information on rates and conditions of credit will be standardised to allow for better comparison of offers. this will enable consumers to make informed choices and obtain better loan terms. the lender should also clearly inform the customer of the advantages and disadvantages of the loan offer. the question of the right of withdrawal in the case of a tied credit (immediate delivery of the property) and the amount of penalties imposed in the case of early repayment of the loan are clearly framed. these penalties must be "fair and objectively justified". they may not exceed 1% of the amount of the credit being repaid in advance and shall not be authorized in the case of variable rate loans. i am particularly pleased that the member states will be able to provide, as is currently the case in france, that no penalty is required for appropriations of less than eur 10 000, and that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. this text, initiated by austria, provides for the possibility for a member state to request the assistance of a special intervention unit from another member state in order to control a crisis situation (hostage-taking, aircraft hijacking). such assistance could consist either in the provision of specific equipment or know-how or in the possibility of carrying out an operation in the territory of the requesting member state. we are in favour of this text for a number of reasons. firstly, because this instrument, which is intended to combat terrorism, is not binding since it does not oblige the member states either to request such assistance or to respond favourably to it. the text also provides that all practical arrangements (types of units, equipment, etc.) are to be referred to bilateral agreements between the requesting member state and the requested member state. in the fight against terrorism, which by definition knows no borders, it is very important to work for the most effective cooperation between the national police forces of the union. at a time when all matters relating to justice and the internal affairs of the states will become a matter of supranational competence with the treaty of lisbon, an intergovernmental pole of resistance seems to remain: we welcome this.
in writing. the text before us aims to provide a legal framework for operations carried out by special intervention units of one member state, sent to the territory of another, in the event of a terrorist attack. given the diversity of these interventions: exchange of equipment, know-how, active units, etc., it is left to the member states to conclude bilateral conventions for the definition of all the practical arrangements and the possibility of having the choice of accepting or refusing the request for intervention on its territory of one of these operational units. i can't believe this. finally, here is a real case of application of the controversial and complicated principle of subsidiarity! finally, there is the area of national security, which is certainly a royal domain par excellence, and which resists the supranational bulldozer of a europe which legislates on everything and everywhere. europe is therefore counting on the cooperation of national police forces to combat terrorism effectively. we support this initiative. but the key to victory over terrorism is not just in this cooperation. it requires an awareness of the revolutionary will of the islamic international which advocates the destruction of western, humanistic and christian society and its values.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we have now reached the end of three years of work and i am pleased with the progress made on the important points of this dossier. the customs union is a cornerstone of the european union and an essential element of the functioning of the internal market. the current community customs code, which was drawn up in the 1980s and came into force in the 1990s, is outdated. customs services today face new challenges. in 2007, world trade was around usd 16 trillion, or 31% of world gdp, and the european union alone accounts for 20% of the total volume of world imports and exports. customs must therefore ensure the flow of trade, while carrying out the necessary checks and ensuring the protection of the health and safety of community citizens. to achieve a good balance, control methods must be modernised and cooperation between the various departments and economic operators strengthened. the code also needs to be adapted to other radical changes in the international trade environment, in particular the increasing and irreversible use of information technology and the exchange of electronic data. this particular aspect was the subject of a report by my colleague christopher heaton-harris, which was adopted by this house last december. the first reading of the modernised customs code was adopted on 12 december 2006 and the german presidency reached a political agreement on 25 june 2007. the european parliament adopted 51 amendments at first reading, 34 of which, most of them essential, were incorporated in whole or in part in the council's common position. the thorny points of the case were the authorized economic operator, the right of customs representation, centralised customs clearance and comitology. the concept of authorised economic operator, directly linked to the events of 11 september, was introduced by the so-called 'security amendment' regulation in order to increase the facilities for operators in compensation for the new burdens linked to the consideration of the security dimension. your rapporteur is pleased that parliament has taken up the idea put forward at first reading of distinguishing between two types of authorization: customs simplification on the one hand and security and safety on the other. this pragmatic solution takes account of the different needs of economic operators. the right to be represented at customs was a matter of great concern in countries where the profession was particularly well established. if the council did not exactly take up parliament's proposals, it was nevertheless based on the idea of combining customs representative and authorized economic operator, as we wished. your rapporteur believes that the council has reached a good compromise. moreover, this solution satisfies the associations of customs representatives, which have lost their monopoly in some member states. as regards centralised customs clearance, another major innovation, the council introduced a new article, article 106, considering that it was preferable, for reasons of logic and transparency, to integrate all the provisions of the code relating to this concept into a single article. from now on, all economic operators can benefit from centralised customs clearance in the territory of the same member state. to benefit from it in several member states, they will have to meet the criteria of the status of authorised economic operator. finally, among the major advances in this area, we can also welcome the extension of the comitology procedure with scrutiny to 44 provisions of the modernised customs code. i therefore ask the european parliament to support the council's common position without any amendments.
the rapporteur. - mr president, i thank the speakers and all those who have contributed to the preparation of this report. since mr medina ortega has mentioned contraband, i cannot resist the urge to talk to you about counterfeiting. between 1998 and 2004, the number of counterfeit seizures increased by 1000%. this means that the specific controls and a new approach to the customs function needed to be modernised. i would also like to pay tribute to the professionals, who have shown a great deal of openness, and i would like to tell them that i do not feel at ease with them. this will no doubt answer mrs mcguinness' concerns. as regards implementing measures, i will endeavour to encourage dialogue between them and the community institutions, including the commission, with which cooperation has always been close and fruitful. i therefore ask you to vote in favour of the common position and thank you for your attention.
in writing. the competitiveness of european industry must be at the heart of the community agenda as it is the only way to create skilled jobs, ensure europe's economic growth, ensure the survival of the european social system and ensure that the eu can remain a major trading power in the 21st century. in order to ensure this competitiveness, we must therefore move towards fair and reciprocal market access conditions. the european market is one of the most open and competitive in the world, thanks in particular to competition law, which guarantees open and fair competition in the eu. however, on the external side, the eu faces many trade barriers. the markets of europe's main trading partners are not as open and transparent as the community market. it is therefore more than necessary to restore reciprocal conditions of market access at the level of third countries and more particularly emerging countries and to combat unfair trade practices. we must act swiftly and decisively to ensure that our smes in particular have unhindered access to markets, and in particular to public procurement.
mr president, the commission has decided to postpone the draft reform of the trade defence instruments and i welcome, mr commissioner, this wise decision, which will help to preserve the effectiveness of the fight against unfair competition. these instruments are essential to the international trading system, since they ensure fair and sustainable conditions of competition for companies, and in particular for smes, which are the first victims of dumping, and thus guarantee a healthy economy. i would therefore like to quote mr verheugen's words at a textile conference in milan at the end of last week: 'trade defence instruments are useful for the competitiveness of our industries and are in no way instruments of protectionism'. i think that says it all. these instruments do not constitute a disguised protection of the community industry against the free play of international competition, but on the contrary make it possible to improve its competitiveness by restoring, where necessary, the conditions of normal competition. the weakening of the implementation of these instruments would not have made the eu's trade policy more adapted to the changing global economic context. on the contrary, the interests of industry would have been diluted and the measures taken might have indirectly encouraged relocations and the flight of our research and innovation centres. europe must play a protective role in globalisation. to be competitive, we must not let our guard down in relation to our partners and enforce the rules of fair international trade.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the debate we are continuing tonight has been open in this chamber for some years. it will not be closed with the adoption of this report, which leaves some questions open, to which we will probably have to return in the near future. i would like to thank the commission for the quality of its communication, which has enriched the debate and which we have taken advantage of in the committee on employment. i shall be dealing with the consequences of demographic changes in my report, i.e. the decline in the working population, the increasing number of elderly people and the demographic imbalances in the regions of europe. does that mean that it is impossible to act on the causes? i would like to remind you that the 20th century has seen two major developments. first, women have access to education and training on an equal basis with men. then women gained control of their fertility by contraception. these are two factors in women's emancipation. this is a great advance for mankind and, i hope, irreversible. however, in order to have all the elements of analysis in hand, two things must be added at the same time. all the studies show that european citizens want more children than they actually have, and secondly, in the member states where the employment rate of women is high, the birth rate is also high. so having an active working life does not prevent having children, provided that it allows a good balance between work and family life for all men and women. much progress remains to be made in this area, and this in all member states. another point has emerged in the course of our discussions, which no one disputes. economic insecurity, fear of the future are important factors in the decline in birth rates. when it's hard to plan for the future, you hesitate to have children. this is a crucial point and i believe that the fall in birth rates in the european union is a serious warning in this respect. the citizens of europe need to regain confidence in the future by regaining job security and decent living conditions. that's the cause, what about the effect? the main consequence is the decline in the working population, which is expected to fall from 331 million in 2010 to around 268 million in 2050. how can europe maintain its growth and competitiveness with a reduced working population? in this area, the title of the communication, commissioner, is quite meaningful and powerful: turning a challenge into an opportunity. europe today suffers from still very high unemployment rates and there is still considerable scope for progress in the employment of women, young people and the elderly, for whom the employment rate falls dramatically from 52 to 55 years of age. the real opportunity of this demographic challenge is the goal of full employment, which is at last realistic, at last achievable, and at last necessary. we must therefore implement a real human resource management policy and a real lifelong learning policy. i say lifelong, and that also means for employees over 50, who are discriminated against in vocational training and promotion. in my report i propose the concept of the working life cycle to emphasize the need to consider the period of working life, which is about 40 years, but it is up to the member states to define it as a continuous chain of employment, training, retraining and possible promotion from the beginning to the end of working life. and before we consider lowering the retirement age, we must ensure that all those who have not yet reached that age have the opportunity to work, to use their skills and professional experience. it is because there is a legal retirement age that it can be considered to go beyond it, according to modalities which each member state defines in accordance with its traditions of dialogue and consultation. the debate on this point remains open. the last point i would like to make quickly is, of course, the use of immigration. there's a lot of talk about compensating for the decline in the working population, and you know that immigration also causes a lot of tension. that is why i am advocating a calm and reasoned approach to this issue. immigration into the european union is not a new phenomenon and, with a positive balance of two million immigrants per year - a figure that has remained stable for several years - legal immigration contributes to the composition of the european union's labour force, as it also contributes to the composition of european societies. we must maintain this flow of immigrants and guarantee legal status in our member states to those we receive, in particular by fighting against the illegal channels and the exploitation of illegal labour. the human dimension of immigration must be the guiding principle of our immigration policies and family integration must not be left out of our guidelines. in the interim conclusion of this presentation, i would like to remind you that behind the birth rates, the age pyramids, the ratios, there are the questions of birth, motherhood, the place of women in our societies, the care we give to our elders and how we ourselves hope to end our lives. that is why this debate is as exciting as it is passionate, and i thank all the shadow rapporteurs for being as passionate as i am.

the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we are debating two reports of our own initiative this morning, but i think they are very important for several reasons. first of all, we are relying on the commission's fourth report on cohesion. it is a truly remarkable document, much better than the previous ones and a very solid basis for any reflection on the future of cohesion in europe. secondly, because the new treaty of lisbon enshrines territorial cohesion as a major objective of the union. finally, we know this because new and formidable challenges are added to those we already know and cohesion policy must make a strong and useful contribution to addressing them in order to move towards the europe we want, that is to say, a europe that is effective and supportive. what does the fourth report tell us? that economic and social convergence between member states is on track, with some reduction in income and employment disparities over the past decade, but also that disparities between, and sometimes within, regions remain strong and often tend to worsen. the development is real but it is far too much imbalanced. this is where the new concept of territorial cohesion comes into its own and where it must, alongside economic and social cohesion, play a central role in pursuing regional development at union level. it will involve an integrated approach between sectoral policies and the actual practice of multi-level governance for its implementation. in this respect, we look forward - and i must say eagerly - to the commission's green paper for next september. the need for a common language on this subject is obvious and this has been well highlighted in our discussions in the regional committee. the lessons of the fourth report lead us to look beyond 2013, since operational programmes for 2007-13 are now in place almost everywhere. they are characterised, in particular, for the first time, by a system of 'split' appropriations, designed to channel the bulk of resources towards the objectives of the lisbon agenda. while emphasising the close relationship in terms of priorities between the lisbon strategy and cohesion policy, we believe that cohesion policy must go beyond this framework and be placed in a broader perspective. our report strongly affirms that convergence at different levels is a prerequisite for the long-term competitiveness of the regions and that in the future the complementarity of the two policies is necessary in order to reconcile performance and solidarity. a periodic evaluation over the period 2007-2013, which we are requesting, should make it possible to confirm the merits of the approach or to make any changes that may be necessary in full knowledge of the facts. the dissociation between rural development and regional policy in the current programming period will also have to be examined. its relevance does not seem to be proven on the ground and the maintenance of this separation after 2013 seems problematic to us. finally, our report puts particular emphasis on the new challenges facing the union and their strong territorial impact - of course, there is the ageing population, climate change, energy, urban concentration, etc. we believe that the urgent need for convergence and the appropriate territorial response to these challenges call for a reinforced cohesion policy in both political and financial terms for the period after 2013. in this context, parliament will - in writing. europeans are becoming an endangered species. with an average fertility rate of less than 1.5, the eu-27 will have lost some 20 million inhabitants by 2050, and those over 65 will make up 30% of its population. the measures proposed by mrs castex to improve the birth rate in europe are ridiculous because, like all the europeans in power, our colleague does not want the demographic renewal of the european peoples, but their replacement by immigration from africa and asia. that is why it devotes fifteen articles of its report to calling for facilities for family reunification, civil rights for immigrants, an increased effort to integrate them... this policy, recommended in france by mr attali and led by mr sarkozy, will bring 80 million more immigrants to europe by 2050 and, in the long run, the disappearance of our peoples. to ensure the survival of the peoples of europe, we must, on the contrary, reverse the migratory flows and implement a great natalist policy based on the family and the welcome of life. to achieve this, our nations must, in a new europe, that of the homelands, regain their sovereignty and their identity.
in writing. the castex report on the demographic future of europe is a sadly banal statement, repeating all the punchlines found in studies on the subject. mrs castex forgets, among other things, to mention the methods of birth control which have largely contributed to reducing the birth rate in europe, which is now only 1.5 children per woman, far from the replacement of generations. the favourable demographic environment means that women who wish to do so can raise their children for a shorter or longer period. this investment is a priority for society and would significantly reduce school failure and juvenile delinquency. as for the use of immigration to compensate for empty cribs, it is a dangerous idea which, in addition to destabilizing our western societies, risks being a time bomb with all the consequences one can imagine. to justify immigration by a lack of skilled or unskilled labour when there are more than 20 million unemployed in europe is to penalise european workers, who will certainly welcome the proposals of the commission or the european parliament. for these reasons we shall vote against the castex report.

member of the commission. − mr president, the commission has condemned the attacks against president ramos-horta and prime minister xanana gusmao in the strongest terms. the young democracy of east timor is still extremely vulnerable in its political, judicial and security institutions. the country is confronted with poverty and high unemployment, especially among the young people who have so far little expectations for a prosperous future and are amenable to violent groups. in its meetings with the leaders of the country, the commission has supported a peaceful settlement of the conflict, including the eventual disbanding and disarmament of any paramilitary group. following the 2006 violence, the european commission has reacted quickly: firstly, with humanitarian assistance to the internally displaced persons; secondly, by supporting dialogue among the leaders; and thirdly, in implementing a cash-for-work programme for unemployed youth. the european commission also decided to open a fully-fledged delegation in dili, and the new head of delegation is expected to start work in march 2008. the delegation will become fully operational towards the second half of 2008. this will create the opportunity for a formal political dialogue with the government and a faster assessment of support to the country. the strategy of the european commission for east timor under the 10th european development fund has recently been approved. it aims to support the still weak judicial sector, the parliament and other institutions, thereby assisting in building up a democratic culture. support to rural development will help to alleviate poverty and to improve infrastructure. health-related activities will contribute to tackling poverty-related diseases and reducing alarmingly high mother and child mortality rates. addressing the root causes of the present conflict and providing support for their solution will be as important as the longer term programmes. the east timorese government has submitted a comprehensive governance action plan, which will be the subject of political dialogue between the delegation and the government, supported by the commission. in a mission during the next weeks, the commission will assess the situation and the possibility of assisting with further measures addressing some of the root causes of the conflict. this may include requests of the government to support some labour-intensive programmes to combat unemployment. in a joint commission-council paper of december 2007, both the commission and the eu member states supported the central role of the united nations in coordinating the assistance to the security sector. in summary, the envisaged support under the commission programme, more than eur 80 million, is comprehensive and will help to address many of the present problems of the country.

member of the commission. − mr president, the commission remains very concerned about the dire humanitarian situation in the kivus, and north kivu in particular, where the number of internally displaced people – currently exceeding 800 000 in north kivu alone – has as much as doubled in the course of 2007, thus alarmingly increasing the vulnerability of the population already suffering hardship. at the same time, we are aware of, and condemn, the severe human rights abuses – including recruitment of child soldiers and widespread sexual violence – taking place in the region. yet, in this context, it is important to remember that today’s critical situation in north kivu, while exacerbated by the fighting taking place in the second half of 2007, is a result of years of war in the region. the root causes of the kivu conflict can be traced all the way to the rwandan genocide at the beginning of the 1990s, while also bearing in mind that there are several local components – such as insufficient political representation of ethnic minorities, pillaging of natural resources and land tenure issues – that significantly contribute to the instability and insecurity in eastern democratic republic of congo. that is why the commission welcomes the recent goma peace conference and the following cease-fire as positive steps towards solving the enduring conflict in eastern democratic republic of congo. the conference restored president kabila’s credibility after the army’s defeat against general nkunda’s troops at the end of 2007, and launched an inter-provincial dialogue process – something that the commission has always advocated. moreover, along the lines of the commitments made by the democratic republic of congo and rwanda in their nairobi joint communiqué in november 2007, the goma conference also re-emphasised the need to tackle the problem of the ex-far as a priority. at the same time, it was made clear that there is a need to address the root causes of the conflict, while restoring the state authority in the east. that said, it should not be forgotten that nothing was definitively solved at goma or nairobi. finding a permanent solution to the root causes of the kivu crisis, and thus a sustainable restoration of peace in the region, will take time. indeed, while complementing each other, the nairobi joint communiqué and the goma conference represent an encouraging start – but only a start – of a difficult and lengthy process. the main challenge ahead is now an effective implementation of the nairobi and goma commitments. it ought to be assured that all the concerned stakeholders stand by their commitments. the eu will continue to follow closely and participate actively in this process. in this context, international action in support of the congolese is very much needed. the commission, together with the member states, is ready to continue to play an important role in the kivus. we have traditionally been one of the most important donors in the east, via our humanitarian assistance and our rehabilitation and capacity-building programmes. we are willing to further increase our support for the region, especially through european initiatives, as well as in close collaboration with the united nations.
the debate is closed.

madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in this own-initiative report, mr albertini has stressed the need for a comprehensive policy which takes account of all aspects: transport, energy and the environment. human mobility, which is a source of wealth for society in various ways - economic, social and cultural - cannot be achieved without energy and often has negative consequences for the environment. every society - and the european union in particular - must seek a balance. a difficult task! it is in this context that the european union makes its full sense by playing a decisive role in the harmonious development of transport: the single european railway market, the single european sky, the trans-european transport networks, the european port policy. by setting ambitious targets with the energy-climate package, action must now relay the discourse, the discourses on these shared goals. and as plato said, "it is only up to us to take the road that goes up and avoid the road that goes down". coordination and cooperation are the keywords of this policy. coordination of infrastructure at european level to benefit from a global vision of transport networks, cooperation with local actors who are best able to provide a practical and realistic vision of the issues at stake, because this is europe. the aim is to achieve harmony by pooling efforts, by exchanging good practice in the interests of citizens and the environment, and, not forgetting the prevert inventory, by providing significant additional financial support to complete the priority transeuropean transport projects as soon as possible. but, above all, if we focus on the local, it seems to me that the integrated approach can only be efficient through an intermodal approach supported financially by europe, especially in the congested metropolitan and urban areas, for guaranteed, safe and affordable mobility, in short, ecological and sustainable mobility.
mr president, most of our countries have in their budgetary law credit lines to deal with disasters. for example, french budgetary law has global appropriations which allow, by advance decree, the commitment of appropriations in case of emergency. since november 2002, european budgetary law has been endowed with this financial right for disasters with this solidarity fund. we have also created the globalisation injury compensation fund for economic disasters. as far as natural disasters are concerned, we are asked to contribute less than 4% to the repair of the damage of over 4 billion suffered in britain in june 2007 as a result of floods. nine months to commit appropriations is a long time, since by definition these are emergency situations. that means that the amending budget technique for authorizing commitment is not operational. the amending budget should be used earlier to ratify the commitment which will have to be made in advance by means of provisional and non-limiting appropriations for disasters, floods or fires. this is a good example of pragmatism, given that the 162 million euros in solidarity for britain from adam smith, ricardo and mrs thatcher, who believe only in the market, darwinism and natural selection, is a good example. the lion that roars in the economic jungle discovers, when it is wet, the virtues of solidarity. as has happened three times before - mad cow disease, foot-and-mouth disease and floods - our british colleagues will also have the opportunity tomorrow to show solidarity with the european farmers who are suffering from the effects of imports.
mr president, commissioner, we are now at last at the start of the procedure for the political priorities for 2009. it is a major step forward, since there will be many changes - new mandate, the introduction of the treaty - and it is also a new response from parliament to the commission on its spa, since we have chosen to have the political groups speak rather than the committee on budgets. the political choices of the socialist group are clear and have been reiterated: this is social europe. it is europe for this priority in the fight against climate change; it is also europe for common external action. and, you see, when i see that the commission wants the eu's contribution to international security and stability to be increased, i wonder where the money is going to come from. how can we fulfill this godly desire? if we continue in this way, we will be put, as we are every year, by the council in an untenable position: to choose which part of the world to sacrifice. a fourth priority for us is the citizen; the commission is telling us that we must put the citizen first in 2009. it is high time, because our political project, far from the people, cannot continue. so we need to strengthen all exchanges, all information, all communication, but with what money? the budget is clearly not adequate. the available margins are already pre-empted and we in the committee on budgets do not know how to finance these priorities. we do not want to sacrifice old priorities to implement new ones. how are you going to do that? there is a great urgency to get europe out of its budgetary and management magma. the political world is changing very rapidly and we in europe are producing ideas, but we have never been able to adopt our means of implementing them in a pragmatic way to meet the political expectations which are certainly those of parliament, but also those of the citizens.
mr president, we are now in the final phase of the creation of the eit. i welcome the negotiating work between the various institutions to reach a balanced solution to make this institute the symbol of innovation in line with our great ambitions. the emphasis is therefore on innovation, a fundamental value in europe. the first kics will focus on key areas such as climate change and renewable energy, not to mention nanotechnologies which need real support. the european union will be firmly committed to innovation. the europe of innovation, the innovation of europe, the eit is the missing link between these two concepts, the missing link which, as it will be voted on tomorrow, will enable the european union to move forward. it is by believing in roses that we make them bloom, anatole france reminded us. the eit is like a rose in our european garden. all the climatic conditions must be present for the tie to flower. i regretted, at first reading, the low financial resources allocated to the eti, the insufficiency of this support: 308 million euros is not a sufficient response to meet our ambitions. we must therefore, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, change the financial climate and provide the means to achieve our real ambitions.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report on sustainable transport policy. it takes account of european energy and environmental policies. a proportion of 70% of oil demand in the eu is attributable to the transport sector. the almost total dependence on fossil fuels must be ended by combining the different policies that cover all modes of transport. this approach must meet the necessary conditions to be realistic, such as technological innovation to reduce co2 emissions from cars and the development of biofuels, the reform of the taxation system to take account of the impact on the environment, accompanying measures to optimise the use of infrastructure and to encourage citizens to change their habits. each citizen can be a player in sustainable transport by favouring public transport over private cars when this alternative is possible. to facilitate the mobility of people and goods by means of low-emission transport modes such as rail, inland waterway, maritime transport and public transport, new services will have to be offered, the sector will have to be organised in a more competitive way and certain infrastructures will have to be used differently.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text which makes it compulsory for member states to participate in the collection of data necessary for efficient energy statistics. this is a prerequisite for the eu to live up to its stated ambition of building a coherent european energy policy and speaking with one voice on the international stage. the commission will have to ensure that these statistics are comparable, transparent, detailed and flexible. the eu has committed to reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 20% by 2020 and to achieving a 20% share of renewable energy in the eu's total energy consumption by 2020, with a 10% target for biofuels. the energy statistics system must adapt to these commitments and take account of the growing importance of energy efficiency, renewable energies, the greenhouse effect, the development of nuclear energy and the emergence of biofuels. greater attention will also have to be paid to the security of supply of the main fuels. more up-to-date and accurate data at eu level will be needed to anticipate and coordinate eu responses to possible supply crises.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my belgian colleague bart staes on the relevant statistics on pesticides. i welcome the action of the european commission, which, as early as the sixth community environment action programme in 2002, recognised that the use of pesticides has a significant impact on human health and the environment. their use must therefore be approached in a sustainable development logic and be the subject of harmonised and comparable community statistics on production, import, export and marketing in order to develop and monitor community legislation in this field. it is important to note that pesticides are used not only in agricultural activities but also in green space maintenance services, road services and rail transport companies. finally, i support the idea of clarifying the terminology plant protection products by replacing it with the term pesticides in the regulation while clearly specifying what it is.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. the long-term, worrying consequences of the ubiquitous presence of pesticide residues are only beginning to be seen: cancer, endocrine disruption, reduced male fertility, weakened immune defenses, and behavioral disorders. exposure to pesticides may increase the risk of asthma in children. monitoring the risks associated with pesticide use therefore requires appropriate indicators. those indicators should provide available, transparent, relevant and reliable data to reduce the risks and harm to the environment and human health arising from their use. the active components of biocides are also used as plant protection products and produce almost the same effects on health and the environment. therefore, this category must be clearly defined and taken into account by these statistics. to make the figures as realistic as possible, statistics should cover not only the use of plant protection products in agricultural activities but also in non-agricultural activities such as green space maintenance services, road services or railway transport undertakings. in the long term, a quantitative and quantified reduction in the use of these products will have to be implemented.
in writing. i voted in favour of the advisory report by my german colleague elisabeth jeggle on the increase in milk quotas from 1 april 2008. this is to meet the growing demand for milk within the european union itself and also on world markets. i welcome the compromise to allow member states to increase their production quotas by 2% by 1 april 2008 with possibilities for rebalancing between countries that exceed and those that under-use their quotas to limit the penalties for exceeding at european level.
in writing. there were, they said, streams of milk, mountains of butter, and frosty chests of meat. brussels then invented the malthusian instruments to sell off production. there were the headquarters, the farm, the slaughter premiums and the quotas... for milk. thousands of dairy farmers have disappeared. new zealand has dominated the milk market. then things changed. we ran out of milk. prices have skyrocketed. and brussels is discovering the folly of its policy of stifling production. so we decide to increase the quotas by 2%. in the name of a "soft landing" since in 2015 quotas would be abolished and the market would be left to full liberalism, with the risk for our mountain farmers. so we destroyed some ranchers in the '80s and prevented young people from settling. the quota was not available for the installation licence. and now we are heading for more desertification of mountain farming areas if quotas are no longer there to provide the safety net.
in writing. it was important that parliament give its opinion on the broad guidelines for the future health check-up. the pse group has won some important victories, such as the criticism of the decoupling of aid (livestock and small crops), the objectives of the cap in terms of food security, ecosystem preservation, territorial development, the redistributive effect of the degressive ceiling, modulation, safety nets, the recognition of the role of inter-professional, the contribution of agriculture to climate change... however, i was keen to support several points, unlike the pse group: the partial decoupling of direct aid must be maintained for animal premiums, but it is necessary to ensure that not only intensive or large-scale farming (§26, §32) is taken into account, the references do not allow to value the respect by farmers of certain high environmental standards (§16) of the milk market, the redistributive effect of the decreasing ceiling, modulation, safety nets, the recognition of the role of inter-professional, the contribution of agriculture to climate change... however, i was keen to support several points, unlike the pse group: the partial decoupling of direct aid must be maintained for animal premiums, but care must be taken not to take into account only intensive or large-scale farming (§26, §32) the references do not allow to the historical value of the respect by farmers of high environmental standards (§16) of the land, the redistributive effect of the reduction of direct support of the reduction of the reduction of the aid (§6)
in writing. the commission's cap health check is not a check, it is a new unspoken reform. and another step towards the economic reorganization of the world which brussels europe has been working on for years, in the wake of washington. in the south and the united states, agriculture. in the north, services and industry, in fierce competition with emerging countries. european agriculture is being sacrificed and will soon be left to market forces alone. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. agriculture is not a sector like any other. because it is used to feed men, it contributes to national independence and sovereignty. because the quality of food determines public health. because farming determines land use, environmental protection, biodiversity, water management, the animation and settlement of rural areas - but it is still a productive act. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. and it is a pity that despite some good things, the rapporteur has not challenged this logic.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which calls in particular for taking into account the specificities of regions in difficulty and sensitive sectors such as livestock farming and for further simplifying the rules for farmers. the aim is to improve the functioning of the common agricultural policy on the basis of the experience gained since 2003 and to adapt it to the new challenges and opportunities that will arise in 2007 in a european union of 27 member states. the report estimates that direct support will remain necessary after 2013, not only in the event of market problems, but also to compensate for the services farmers render to society and the very high environmental, health and animal welfare standards. finally, as regards risk management, the commission must be able to hear the message of parliament in this report in the light of the future reform of the cap. private or mixed insurance schemes should be developed as a matter of urgency with the support of public funding, ensuring that member states remain on an equal footing. the commission should be able to envisage the future introduction of a european reinsurance system for climate or environmental disasters and risk prevention measures should be financed under the first pillar (support for agricultural markets).
in writing. gender equality in rural areas needs more attention from the european union. the situation of women's rights and their place in rural life requires greater determination on the part of the member states and the commission. on the one hand, women suffer from a particularly unfavourable legal status when they work in the agricultural sector as a caring spouse. the european commission must break with this legal inequality, which deprives some european women of their access to social security, maternity and sick leave or pensions in the event of divorce. on the other hand, there is insufficient support for women's economic initiatives and entrepreneurship. the member states must, for example, financially support enterprises that diversify women's work and, more generally, support the development of infrastructure and new technologies in rural areas. finally, the commission must analyse rural development programmes more closely in the light of the situation of women. rural areas account for 56% of the population of the european union. because women can bring dynamism and creativity to the process, i fully support the proposals in mrs klass' report.
in writing. the issue of the status of women in rural areas has been addressed many times at the world conferences on women (1975, 1980, 1985 and 1995), on land reform and rural development (1979) and on population (1994), as well as by the european commission and parliament. but the texts may be accumulated, but the findings are always the same: an increase in the "masculinization" of the rural population and no improvement in the status of the assistant spouse on an agricultural holding. it is high time to develop strategies to curb the rural exodus of women, especially those with a university degree. to take account of the development of the main global trends, in particular the liberalisation of trade and finance and the privatisation of agriculture into a strictly regulated and quota-based commercial sector. times are changing, but not the attitudes and customs that have meant that the role of women in agriculture is far too often reduced to being co-farmers or unpaid workers on farms that are often family-run. does this report propose any changes to the statute? we will vote in favour.
in writing. i would like to congratulate csaba tabajdi on his excellent report and on all the research and synthesis work he has carried out perfectly. however, i would like to point out that i voted against paragraph 27:27. notes that the court of auditors' audit findings on the annual accounts of the european food safety authority (efsa) for the financial year 2012 were based on the information provided by the court of auditors in its annual accounts for the financial year 2012; in my view, biogas must be fed primarily from agricultural waste. there can be no question of developing gm seeds and pesticides in order to promote even more intensive agriculture. that would be bad for the environment, and it would negate all the benefits of agrofuels. as the title of the report indicates, we must first of all promote sustainable agriculture. i will be responsible for the opinion of the committee on agriculture on the draft directive on the promotion of renewable energy sources.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i too would like to congratulate mrs gomes on the quality of her work on a very sensitive and complex subject. we all know how deeply divided our member states were over the iraq conflict. we know that today our duty is to help build a secure, united, prosperous and democratic iraq. i would like to emphasize a major drama, largely overlooked by our governments. i am talking about the iraq conflict, which has left nearly 4.5 million people on the roads, the largest displacement in the middle east since 1948. concerted action is urgently needed at european level. my main concern is the immediate and long-term fate of the iraqis who have had to flee their country. some 2.3 million people have found refuge in neighbouring countries, mainly syria and jordan, but also in egypt, lebanon, turkey and the gulf states. by welcoming almost 2 million people, syria and jordan have made a very worthwhile effort. the role of the union and the international community is of course to enable all these refugees to return home eventually, but at this stage it is not possible for many of them to return. some of these particularly vulnerable refugees require transfer to a western country. according to unhcr, 6.6% of iraqis residing in syria, or 100,000 people, need to be resettled. i therefore call on my colleagues to support the amendment in favour of resettlement programmes which provide for the union to take in some of the most vulnerable refugees selected by the unhcr in 2008. in conclusion, let us not turn our backs on our values. we must fully respect the 1951 geneva convention and refuse any forced return to iraq.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, for fernand braudel, history began in sumer, but today the long history of the christian minorities in iraq seems to be coming to an end. we, the nations of europe, cannot condone this great injustice by our inaction. these people welcomed islam with hospitality and together they built this country that was prosperous before it was ravaged by fanaticism and wars. today, these minorities have to resign themselves to running away. the future of iraq cannot be achieved without their presence and their skills. the future does not lie in partitioning the country, but in rebuilding the economy, in mutual recognition between different communities and cultures, and in the promotion of the rule of law. if the european union decides to intervene in iraq, it must always bear in mind, in the context of its project, the tragic reality of all these minority communities. their future must be the basis of its intervention, and the reality of mutual respect between the communities the criterion for allocating its aid. this action will then be the honor of our nations.
the chairman of the council. - as you are aware, the situation in chad has deteriorated in recent weeks. in early february, chadian rebels approached and captured most of the capital city of n'djamena, but after a few days they retreated or were driven eastward to the chad-sudan border. the attacks by rebel groups on the chadian government in early february not only ignited a simmering internal crisis, but also revealed its regional dimension. the rebels came from darfur with the support of the sudanese side. the situation in chad must therefore be considered from two interrelated perspectives: domestic and regional. in february, the council of the european union condemned the rebel attacks on the chadian government, calling for a political dialogue between the government, the opposition and the rebels, and stressing the need for a political dialogue between the chadian and sudanese governments. we believe that pressure should be increased on the governments of chad and sudan to fulfil the commitments they have made in the various agreements. the council called on both governments to immediately cease supporting and supplying armed groups and to improve relations between them. as regards the internal political situation in chad, a political solution to the conflict is the only way to peace and stability in that country. the inclusive political process indicated by the agreement between the ruling party of chad and the parties of the legal opposition in august 2007 should continue. in this regard, the union supports the efforts of the african union to find a peaceful solution to the disputes. the european union therefore joins the calls of both the african union and the united nations, which have very clearly condemned the rebel attacks. we share their concern about the danger of further escalation of the conflict. we are also concerned about the deteriorating humanitarian situation. the growing hostilities have deepened the humanitarian tragedy and increased the already high number of refugees and displaced persons. more than 160 people were killed and about a thousand were wounded. tens of thousands of refugees have fled to neighboring cameroon and nigeria. the humanitarian situation is very poor, with approximately 250 000 refugees from the darfur region of sudan also present in eastern chad, and calls for the full deployment of the european union mission eufor chad-central african republic as soon as possible. the security situation in the capital n'djamena and in most of the country, except the east, is currently calming down and normalizing following the recent clashes. however, the state of emergency declared on 15 february was extended for 15 days until the middle of this month. in this context, the eu expresses concern at the restrictions on civil liberties and media freedom in chad. activities related to the deployment of eufor shall continue after the suspension. the operation's commander, general nash, has decided to suspend operations following the rebel attacks, allowing an assessment of the new political and security situation. the guidance then continued without any consequences for the entire timeframe of the operation. it is planned to reach initial operating capacity by mid-march. the worrying situation in the region has made the importance of the mandate of eufor and the united nations mission all the more apparent. the deployment of eufor demonstrates the union's commitment to contribute to the stabilisation of the region. to achieve the objectives we have set ourselves, two things are needed: we need the security provided by military units, and this is another aspect, and the willingness of the parties to dialogue and negotiate is important.
