in writing. a few remarks on the gill report, which is really about the organisation of research programmes to improve the autonomy of older people through information and communication technologies. the first is the substance: the added value of the european union in a project initiated, as they are entitled to do, by some member states, is not clearly seen, except for the bureaucratization of the process and the creation of a new community body. the union's financial surplus of eur 150 million over several years, minus the operating costs of the aforementioned body, does not appear to be a decisive advantage. secondly, as regards the form: increasingly, this house is presenting legislative reports in the form of a compromise between parliament and the council, which is supposed to allow rapid adoption of dossiers at first reading. but the legislator is now held hostage by a handful of expert negotiators. the extension of this practice seems to me dangerous for democracy.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report proposing the participation of the european union in the research and development programme on home-based assistance (hsa) undertaken jointly by several member states and third countries. the ageing population is a challenge for european society and the economy. the average life expectancy is now 80 years and the number of people aged 65 to 80 will increase by around 40% between 2010 and 2030. innovative solutions are emerging to help with the memory, vision, hearing, mobility, and autonomy impairments that occur more frequently with age. the european union's participation in this programme is based on the seventh framework programme of the european commission for research and development. the projects will be co-financed by the european union to the tune of eur 150 million and will have a leverage effect of at least eur 600 million between 2008 and 2013. the countries participating in the aad programme should also contribute to its financing by allocating funds equal to or greater than the aad programme, which would mean that each country would devote at least 20% of the funds allocated to national research on this topic.
in writing. brussels' europe means more taxes and more constraints! the harmonization of excise duties and vat by fixing compulsory minimum rates of taxation, as it has been for the past 15 years, has proved ineffective, totally useless and sometimes harmful. it is worth recalling that this prevents member states from reducing vat on, for example, catering, which is certainly the activity for which a possible distortion of cross-border competition is least credible and which could create thousands of jobs! or that the new member states are forced to raise their taxes to an extent that is shocking to their citizens in order to comply with community regulations, even though other european regulations require them to control inflation! today we are being asked to raise the tax on diesel fuel to the same level as that on unleaded petrol, both under the pretext of protecting the environment and of combating 'tax tourism', that is to say the use of competition by citizens for their own benefit! this is all the more scandalous because motorists in france, for example, have been encouraged to buy diesel cars in order to be able to beat them better now.
in writing. the aim of the commission's proposal was to establish measures to reduce co2 emissions under the ambitions set out in the energy-climate package. however, neither the commission proposal nor the report adopted today responds to the urgent need to develop a fuel which is effective in combating co2 emissions. the disparity of the proposed adjustments and their dilution over time and the geographical area of the european union render the proposed measures ineffective. to change the air in a changing era, we should be more imaginative in terms of the environment by voting for measures that effectively combat climate drift. the commission's proposed taxation amendment and ms schmidt's report do not encourage research into or substitution by a new fuel with lower co2 emissions. today i would like to express my clear opposition to the logic of this report by refusing to vote for this compromise which distorts the stated objective.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report because there is an urgent need to adapt conditions of detention to take account of the specific needs of women. to date, prison conditions in many member states remain very poor and in no way can provide the specific support needed for women. the women prisoners have specificities that require special attention, especially with regard to access to health care. that is why i supported an amendment by the socialist group which calls for women in prison to have access to the same prevention campaigns for breast and cervical cancer screening. this type of early detection increases the chances of recovery. the lack of access to such care for women in prison can be a form of double punishment. women also continue to play a central role in the family unit. it is therefore appropriate to facilitate, as far as possible, alternative sentences to imprisonment for mothers if they do not constitute a threat to public policy.
in writing. although the european union has been integrating gender equality into its development cooperation programmes for many years, progress in this area is still too limited. the european commission must therefore set itself quantified and timed objectives to make development the main factor in improving women's living conditions. to this end, the european union should make clear in the partnerships it leads three priorities: fundamental freedoms, the place in the city and access to care for women. on the one hand, the commission must be more vigilant than ever in the face of attacks on the physical integrity and dignity of women (torture, traditional mutilation, forced marriages). on the other hand, cooperation must lead to the recognition of women's place in society, from access to knowledge to financial autonomy. finally, commitments should be made by 2010 to make hiv prevention and treatment a reality in developing countries. european development policy will be a bitter failure if it does not bring about real changes in the situation of women.

the rapporteur. - mr president, the report i am presenting to you follows up the request we made, which mrs trüpel, who is here, and whom i welcome, and myself, in the culture 2007 report three years ago, to see greater recognition given to the cultural industries, which, i remind you, with 3.1% of the european union's working population and 2.6% of gdp, today weigh more than the automotive industry in the european union. i have therefore drawn up this report in the spirit of maximum consultation with all the players in the sector. i would like to thank the experts and professionals in the sector, the internet users' and consumers' associations and, finally, my colleagues in the committee on culture for all the discussions we have had on these crucial issues. the report starts from the assumption that culture and the economy have become inseparable. the economy needs culture and culture needs the economy. in this context, it is urgent to give culture back its rightful place on the lisbon agenda. i am therefore making a number of proposals in this report. the first would be to create a task force to explore the relationship between culture, creativity and innovation in the context of community policies. secondly, it is essential to give more space in our community financing to the cultural industries. in this report, i advocate, at member state level, private/public funding methods, as well as the promotion of a regulatory and fiscal framework favourable to cultural industries and more specifically the application of tax credits and reduced vat rates to all cultural products, including online works. i would also like to invite the commission to consider the possibility of setting up a programme similar to the media programme for all cultural industries. thirdly, this report proposes that culture be better integrated into the external policies of the european union because - and i stress this - what makes europe rich is first of all its culture, or rather, i was going to say, the diversity of its culture. i therefore also call on the commission and the member states to increase the amount of aid for translation. finally, if i may, mr president, i would like to return to the question of copyright, which has been the subject of many amendments in this report. on this subject i strongly oppose the position of certain member states whose repressive measures are dictated by industries which have not been able to change their economic model in the face of the requirements of the information society. cutting off internet access is a disproportionate measure in relation to the objectives. this is a powerful sanction, which could have serious repercussions in a society where access to the internet is an imperative right for social inclusion. i think we must distinguish between mass piracy and consumers who are not acting for commercial purposes. rather than criminalising consumers, we need to develop new economic models that strike a balance between access to cultural activities and content, cultural diversity and genuine remuneration for rights holders. it seems to me that only then will europe's culture truly enter the 21st century.
the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, i think we must not be mistaken about the objective. despite what some subjective studies would have us believe, it is not the 13% of europeans who illegally download cultural content that threatens our culture, but it seems to me that it is the concentration of our culture in the hands of a few large groups that is damaging our diversity and, by the same token, the richness of our cultural heritage. i will take only one example, the one of the disc. today, 95 percent of what is broadcast comes from the four major discs. i believe it is important to ensure that consumers have a real choice and it is necessary to ensure content pluralism in a highly concentrated market where the key players in innovation and creativity are the small and not the big. and from this point of view, mr commissioner, you spoke of smes, advocating a study, which i think is very interesting. the commission's approval of the sony/bmg merger is in total contradiction to the european policy of supporting smes in the music sector, which create more jobs than the majors and account for 99% of market players and 80% of innovation in this sector. i therefore believe that there is an urgent need to support diversity in the cultural sector, which is a real engine of growth and a real means of personal fulfilment. in conclusion, i would say that it is the diversity of culture that makes it rich, not the other way around.

the rapporteur. - madam president, nothing surprises me, and in particular nothing in the commissioner's communication. commissioner, thank you for this very detailed report. i would simply like to point out that the stated objective of the proposal for a council regulation is to simplify and improve the procedures for managing fishing authorizations. the aim was to establish general provisions applicable to all applications for authorization, as you have said, commissioner. a single procedure for the management of all fishing authorisations has been proposed. the division of responsibilities between the commission and the member states is defined. new eligibility criteria, penalties for infringements and information provisions are also proposed. compliance with international obligations under the various agreements is reinforced by introducing measures requiring member states to prohibit a vessel from fishing if it has been found to be involved in a serious infringement or has been included on a list of participation in illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing activities. mrs catherine stihler was appointed rapporteur for this report but, as her opinion was not followed by the majority of the members of the committee on fisheries on two points which she considered essential, she preferred to withdraw her name from the report. it is therefore my duty to present this draft to you as chairman of the committee. but i would like to welcome his work in passing and i will leave it to him, representing his amendments, to give us the reasons for his decision. on its report, which is now mine, the committee on fisheries has proposed, in the context of the consultation procedure, several amendments, the full list of which you have given - not the list but the numbers, commissioner - to the proposal for a council regulation. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a new regulation on the protection of the environment. i shall present only the main ones. firstly, the regulation should not apply to the overseas territories of the member states of the european union. secondly, a serious infringement should only be considered to have been committed if it has been confirmed following prosecution in accordance with the applicable national law. thirdly, the iuu list is the list of fishing vessels identified by the regional fisheries organisations or by the commission, pursuant to the council regulation establishing a community system to prevent, deter and eradicate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, which is such an important task, commissioner, and to which you have personally committed yourself. fourth, the commission should forward applications to the authority empowered to issue authorisations only after giving the member states the opportunity to submit their comments. fifthly, the commission may refuse to act on requests only where it has knowledge, through duly established facts, that a member state has not complied with obligations under a particular agreement. sixthly, community fishing vessels for which an authorization has been issued must communicate to their national competent authority information on catches and fishing effort at a frequency appropriate to the agreement and the fisheries concerned. this obligation shall be compatible with those contained in the regulation on the electronic flight recorder. i leave it to my colleagues to elaborate, because some of them are the authors of some of the amendments.

generations. to be more specific, in my region, the south-west of france, the old farms are facing south. the reason for this is that the inhabitants had perceived that the orientation of the house in writing i voted in favour of the report by my italian colleague luciana sbarbati in the consultation procedure on the proposal for a council decision establishing a european migration network. the need to monitor migration flows dates back to the commission's first communication in 1994 and led to the experimental creation of the european migration network (emn) in 2003. in order to maintain this indispensable tool, it became necessary to set up a legal instrument. indeed, despite the enormous amount of information produced on many aspects of international migration, this data is not easily accessible. in addition, there is a lack of reliable, comparable and up-to-date information and analysis of the evolving legal and political situation of immigration and asylum at both national and eu level. i support the initiatives to extend this scheme to asylum and to provide for an extension of the mandate of this network.
in writing. the report before us is nothing more than a statement of the failure of the various european policies pursued and the european bodies created so far. what exactly is this? the aim is to create a further european structure responsible for collecting, exchanging and using up-to-date data on migratory trends. it seems that a central source of information is missing. but what about the activities of the dozens of other national, international or intergovernmental bodies, the european observatory on migration, the international organisation for migration, the fundamental rights agency, whose tasks include the collection of information on migration, eurostat, europol, the raxen network, cirefi ... would they be ineffective, outdated? if so, why do we spend more and more money on them each year? the rapporteur is rightly concerned about the risk of duplication of the european migration network with all the existing structures. it should be concerned above all about the dangerous drift of the european institutions which, instead of solving the problems of immigration, are only masking the sad reality by the limitless multiplication of the practice of comitology and the creation of bodies of all kinds.
in writing. cooperation between member states and exchange of information are certainly necessary when it comes to immigration policies. the schengen agreements, which abolish all internal border controls in the union, mean that decisions taken in a member state, particularly those concerning the legalisation of illegal immigrants, necessarily have consequences for and in neighbouring countries. if there is one area in which europe is prolific, it is in the creation of agencies, bodies or any other structures, with staff and budget, which can both justify the union's action and give the appearance of wanting to solve problems. obviously, it's not. this is particularly the case in the field of migration, where existing structures, whether governmental, non-governmental or intergovernmental, are juxtaposed to excess, with no clear results. research centres, professional associations, the european migration observatory, eurostat, europol, the agency for fundamental rights, the centre for the study and research of border crossing and immigration (cirefi)... the list is not exhaustive in this area. the report adds yet another: a european migration network, the first step before the creation of a new european observatory or agency. it is time to put a stop to this europe of hypocrisy and false appearances.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to mention one important aspect of discharge, namely the measurement of actions by sampling. during the preparation of my working document on the commission's management of the cards programme for the balkans, only 2.32% of the operations under discharge were audited by the court of auditors in order to assess the management of the external actions of the european union in this region of europe. the small sample did not allow the court of auditors to analyse the impact of actions outside montenegro, since none of the 256 actions financed were examined. in this situation, how can such impacts be measured seriously? how scientifically and financially reliable should such evaluation reports be? although from a statistical point of view small samples make it possible to estimate the behaviour of systems, the sample still needs to be representative, which was not the case for the appropriations financing actions in montenegro for the cards programme. collectively, european taxpayers would benefit from improved methods of analysis of samples by the court of auditors to better identify the efficiency of our budget appropriations.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my spanish colleague, bárbara dührkop dührkop, which approved, subject to amendments, the initiative of the federal republic of germany with a view to adopting a council decision on the implementation of the decision on the deepening of crossborder cooperation, in particular with a view to combating terrorism and crossborder crime. i welcome germany's initiative to ensure that member states comply with the common technical specifications in all requests and responses relating to the consultation and comparison of dna profiles, dactyloscopic data (e.g. fingerprints, handprints, etc.) and vehicle registration data. i support the report's assertions that the processing of particular categories of data concerning racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, party or trade union membership, sexual orientation or health status should only be possible if it is strictly necessary and proportionate in the context of a specific case and with specific safeguards.
in writing. in the face of insecurity and crime, the european union must set itself two major objectives. the first is to strengthen the fight against terrorism, which knows no borders and no limits to the violence of its acts and the threat it poses. the second objective is still the protection of the fundamental rights which are the foundation of the european construction. the adoption by all member states of the prüm treaty proposed by germany in 2007 is part of the necessary improvement of police cooperation within the european union. the exchange of dna data and vital information such as fingerprints or vehicle registration between the different national systems has already enabled many investigations to be completed. from the fight against kidnapping to international terrorism to the organisation of transnational events, these measures are becoming indispensable. however, european policy must combat crime and delinquency and not build a system which will undermine the rule of law and dangerously weaken democracy. the accessibility and use of personal data must be governed by european rules, the rapid adoption of which is to be hoped. this report illustrates the importance of a balance between data use and data protection.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my finnish colleague anneli jäätteenmäki on a proposal for a european parliament decision amending the european parliament's decision on the ombudsman's statute and general conditions of performance of his duties, which itself called for these matters to be changed. i support the report in that it proposes to adapt the ombudsman's statute so as to remove any uncertainty about the ombudsman's ability to conduct thorough and impartial investigations into alleged cases of maladministration. subject to the application of professional secrecy, i welcome the obligation of officials to give evidence. i also support the idea that access to classified information or documents, especially sensitive documents, should be subject to the ombudsman's compliance with rules strictly equivalent to those in force in the institution or body in question. i congratulate the rapporteur for pointing out that the ombudsman and his staff will be required not to disclose any sensitive information or any document falling within the scope of community legislation on the protection of personal data. it will be difficult to monitor the application of these rules.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my cypriot colleague, adamos adamou, which welcomes the european commission's communication on eu policy action on organ donation and transplantation and proposes an integrated approach to ensure the quality and safety of organs, increase their availability and combat organ trafficking. i welcome the areas of intervention identified, namely: improving quality and safety, increasing the availability of organs and making transplant systems more efficient and accessible, and the mechanisms for action aimed at strengthening cooperation between member states and implementing a community legal instrument which would set the quality and safety requirements for the donation, procurement, verification, preservation, transport and distribution of organs in the european union while providing the resources to meet these requirements.
in writing. i would like to take this opportunity of voting on this report to underline the constant discrepancy between the european union's words and deeds in certain areas. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services. but what is to be expected when the commission and several of those same member states now recognise kosovo and its leaders, some of whom are personally involved in trafficking in organs taken from serb prisoners murdered for that purpose, according to carla del ponte, former president of the international criminal tribunal for the former yugoslavia? what should we think when no state takes sanctions against china, nor protests, while consistent testimonies and investigations have tended to show that executions are scheduled according to the needs of organs, sometimes for foreign patients. what is the plan for the rich europeans who bypass the shortage by engaging in the morbid tourism that encourages these practices? mr adamou's report is strangely elliptical on these subjects. wishing well inside, silence outside... it's a given when certain countries are involved.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. organ donation is a life-giving gesture, a self-giving that is the ultimate and strong act of solidarity. unfortunately, the shortage of organs is still widespread, and nearly ten people die every day in europe waiting for a transplant. the eu must facilitate the rapprochement of national transplantation bodies. increased cooperation would provide safeguards for patients who donate or receive organs outside their member state. some new member states with less well-equipped health systems could benefit. the shortage of organs is also all too often linked to organ trafficking. forms of 'transplant tourism' are emerging which exploit poverty outside the eu's borders. this 'trafficking' in human beings risks undermining the confidence of citizens and exacerbating the shortage of voluntary organ and tissue donations. free of charge is also a fundamental principle. however, the living donor must be reimbursed for the costs of the withdrawals. finally, we must promote research in biotechnology which will provide researchers with the means to reconstitute organs from tissues, either from patients themselves or from other tissue donors.
in writing. organ donation in the european union will face three major challenges in the coming years. firstly, there is a lack of available bodies in the eu. this shortage causes the death of nearly ten patients every day waiting for a donation. secondly, the risks of organ transplantation remain a major concern. the transmission of serious diseases such as hiv, certain hepatitis and cancer remains a reality affecting european citizens. finally, the eu member states will have to deal in a serious and coordinated manner with the issue of organ trafficking, which, although it remains relatively limited within the community, nevertheless raises political and above all ethical concerns. the recommendations in the adamou report are in the right direction: exchange of best practice, enhanced cooperation, increased exchanges of organs between member states, better public information and the need to preserve the voluntary and non-commercial nature of organ donation. these proposals, if implemented, will make it possible to improve substantially and rapidly the conditions for organ donation and transplantation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report 'organ donation and transplantation: political action at eu level', presented by my cypriot colleague adamou adamos. as we all know, organ transplants save lives and improve the daily lives of many of our citizens. nevertheless, the union is currently suffering from a real shortage of donated organs: 40 000 patients are currently waiting for a transplant and it is estimated that 10 of them die every day. this is the problem we have been looking at, with measures such as the creation of a european donor card, increased cooperation between member states, raising awareness among citizens, the introduction of a single number for organ transplants and the promotion of biotechnology research which would make it possible in the future to reconstitute organs without the need for donation. the need to make up for this shortage of organs should not, however, lead us to renounce our values. i am therefore pleased that this text emphasizes the voluntary, unpaid and, as far as possible, anonymous nature of the donation; the european parliament also called on the member states to combat organ trafficking and transplant tourism more effectively.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my irish colleague marian harkin on the contribution of volunteering to economic and social cohesion. i welcome the quality of its research, which aims to place volunteering as a major element that nourishes civil society and strengthens solidarity - one of the core values of our european union. recognising the usefulness of volunteering in all its components, public and private, is essential to its development and to the search for the great balances between the economic, social and environmental aspects; the commission's proposal is to set up a european network of experts in the field of sustainable development. i regret that the report does not address the question of the evaluation of volunteering without also dealing with the fact that volunteering can be defined as a kind of compensated volunteering because the rapporteur considered, in the definition, that volunteering is unpaid. this report is an important step in the recognition of the essential role of non-profit institutions (npi).
in writing. i voted for the discharge for the general budget of the european union for 2006 and for the report by my danish colleague dan jørgensen recommending that the commission be given discharge. the report recalls that 80% of community expenditure is administered by the member states under 'shared management' and that each member state must be able, under the current organisation, to assume responsibility for the management of the community funds received. at present, this reporting must be done in the form of a single national management declaration or in the form of several declarations within a national framework. it is becoming urgent to have an agreement between the commission and the member states on the arrangements for the handover of shared management in the context of future landfills, since it is regrettable that for structural actions, internal policies and external actions, payments are still significantly affected by errors at the level of the bodies responsible for implementation. i regret that the commission is tacitly accepting the collective irresponsibility of the majority of member states with regard to the financial management of the eu. finally, i support the idea of a european authority for the real estate function.
in writing. i voted for the discharge to the president of parliament for the implementation of the 2006 budget and for the report by my spanish colleague josé javier pomés ruiz recommending that parliament vote for the discharge. i support the idea that the new status of assistants should come into force at the same time as that of meps. as regards parliamentary assistance allowances, i believe that the contractual freedom of members, which is a condition of their independence, should be maintained and that this should be subject to the control of the national administrations within the framework of a logic of subsidiarity. i am therefore opposed to any measure restricting the free will of members, including the employment of related persons, subject, of course, to actual work normally paid. as regards the voluntary pension fund, which is a supplementary pension scheme co-financed by the member and the employer, i agree with the publication of the names of the beneficiaries and with the reform of this pension scheme taking place alongside the reform of the members' statute. finally, i support the evaluation of its staffing needs to find out how many staff will be needed to help parliamentarians carry out their work after the entry into force of the lisbon treaty.
in writing. the 30 or so reports voted on today, which give discharge to the management of community funds by the various institutions and agencies of the european union, show that there is control over expenditure. and it is precisely this control that makes it possible to highlight the malfunctions, the errors, the abuses in the management of the structural funds, in that of external aid, etc. some of them, anyway. but they also show that parliament has chosen to approve the management of european finances, despite everything. it is therefore a political act of support for the brussels machine of which it is a cog, rather than a critical exercise. it is true that it is particularly concerned, after an audit report on the cost of parliamentary assistance has been drawn up, which highlights its own shortcomings. and it is symptomatic that the transparency which this parliament is so quick to ask of others, of all the others - council, commission, member states, agencies... - is clearly not for it. because this explosive report for the reputation of this house is not available to the public, not even to the whole house. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. keeping these facts secret won't make them go away.
in writing. i voted to give the council discharge in respect of the implementation of the 2006 budget on the basis of the report by my swedish colleague nils lundgren recommending that the european parliament give the secretary-general of the council a discharge. i regret that, unlike the other institutions, the council does not publish an annual activity report. the council is based on an informal agreement of 1970, but it seems essential that the council should be accountable to the european citizens. under this agreement, the council undertook not to alter the estimates of the european parliament's expenditure. this undertaking shall apply only if the estimates do not affect community provisions, in particular those relating to the staff regulations of officials and the conditions of employment of other servants and the seat of the institutions. as regards the common european security policy (cfsp), i support the request for maximum transparency and for ensuring that, in accordance with the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006, no operational expenditure in the field of the cfsp is included in the council's budget. nevertheless, i believe that the council should have a discretionary budget under the cfsp.
in writing. i voted the discharge on the implementation of the 2006 budget of the european court of justice (ecj) on the basis of the report by my swedish colleague nils lundgren recommending that parliament give the court's registrar a discharge. i welcome the adoption by the court of a code of conduct applicable to members and former members of the court of justice, the court of first instance and the civil service tribunal, including an obligation to submit a declaration of financial interests, but i regret that this information is not published on the court's website. i note that the real estate issues (problem of appointing an independent expert for the extension of the main building; lease-purchase agreement signed between the grand duchy of luxembourg and the court to complete the 2001 framework contract providing for the sale to the court of the land on which the complex is located for the symbolic price of eur 1 once the court of justice has become the owner of the buildings; lack of competition) confirm the need to create a european authority for all real estate issues of our institutions.
in writing. i voted the discharge on the implementation of the court of auditors' 2006 budget on the basis of the report by my swedish colleague nils lundgren recommending that the european parliament give the secretary-general of the court of auditors a discharge. i welcome the quality of the accounts produced which are supervised by an external auditor and the internal auditor with favourable conclusions. as regards declarations of financial interests, like my colleagues, i note that, in accordance with its code of conduct, the members of the court declare their financial interests and other assets (including shares, convertible bonds and investment certificates, as well as land and real estate property, plus the professional activities of their spouses). i agree with my colleagues that members of all the institutions of the union should submit a declaration of financial interests and publish this information on the internet via a public register. but a distinction must be made between enrichment, which must measure amounts, and the issue of conflicts of interest, which must show the nature of assets owned directly or indirectly and relationship links.
in writing. i voted the discharge for the implementation of the 2006 budget of the european economic and social committee (eesc) on the basis of the report by my swedish colleague nils lundgren recommending that parliament give the discharge to the secretary-general of the eesc. like many colleagues, i welcome the signing in december 2007 of a new administrative cooperation agreement between the eesc and the committee of the regions (cor) for the period 2008-2014, knowing that this cooperation will be financially beneficial for the european taxpayer. as regards controls, the eesc considered in its annual activity report that the number of ex-post controls carried out in 2006 was insufficient. however, this situation seems to have improved. it is crucial that the checks carried out are rigorous and the personal assurance given by the eesc secretary-general that the eesc's ex-ante and ex-post checks are effective and regular is welcome. at the same time, like many colleagues, i congratulate the eesc on the establishment of an audit committee of three eesc members, whose tasks will be to verify the independence of the internal audit unit and to evaluate the measures taken in response to the recommendations made in the audit reports.
in writing. i voted to give the secretary-general of the committee of the regions (cor) discharge for the implementation of the 2008 budget on the basis of the report by my swedish colleague, nils lundgren, which recommends that parliament give discharge. like many colleagues, i welcome the signing in december 2007 of a new administrative cooperation agreement between the european economic and social committee (eesc) and the committee of the regions (cor) for the period 2008-2014, in the knowledge that this cooperation will be financially beneficial for the european taxpayer. under the new agreement, the most important sectors (infrastructure, it and telecommunications, and translation, including document production) remain in the remit of the two institutions' joint services, while a limited number of services will be decoupled (internal services, social and medical services, library and prepress). i welcome the outcome of the unfortunate cases of travel expenses for members of the committee of the regions and of the transfer of salaries of certain civil servants. finally, i welcome the strengthening of the independence of the audit service and the increase in its resources.
in writing. i voted to discharge the european ombudsman for the implementation of his budget for the financial year 2006 on the basis of the report by my swedish colleague nils lundgren. like many colleagues, i am surprised that during the period 2003-2006 the ombudsman's commitment appropriations have increased steadily (from eur 4 438 653 to eur 7 682 538 in 3 years (+73%), the number of posts increased from 31 to 57 (+84%) while complaints increased by 57% and newly opened inquiries increased from 253 to 258, +2%). on the operational side, i welcome the conclusion of the new framework cooperation agreement with parliament for the provision of administrative services and the appointment of the first secretary-general of the ombudsman with effect from 1 august 2006. it appears that the effectiveness of controls could be improved in some areas. i am also surprised by the difficulties in recruitment mentioned by the ombudsman in his 2006 annual report, particularly as regards qualified lawyers, due to the two successive waves of enlargement (2004 and 2007), staff movements and the difficulty in attracting and retaining candidates in strasbourg by offering them temporary contracts.

for the gue/ngl group commissioner, first of all, i would like to point out that my colleagues in the conference of presidents who decided against my wishes to have this debate at a late hour are all absent this evening. but even in the night session, i am glad that we have finally had a first debate on this serious matter of the european court of justice's legitimization of wage dumping, a matter which you, commissioner, have just discussed in twenty seconds with a singular ease. i shall therefore briefly recall the three stages of this new departure from european law. 11 december 2007: the court condemns a trade union action against the finnish shipowner viking line for re-registering its ferry in estonia to undercut the salary of the seamen. 18 december 2007: the court again condemns trade unions, this time in sweden, in vaxholm, for blocking the work of a latvian company which refused to apply the collective agreement in force in this sector. 3 april 2008: the court finds the land of lower saxony, germany, guilty of having imposed a minimum wage on all construction companies winning a public contract. the court thus upheld the case of a polish subcontractor of a german company which paid its workers wages more than half the current rate. this is the rüffert decision. in all three cases, the court's basic reason for its decision encouraging wage dumping was the same: community law prohibits any measure which - listen carefully - is likely to make the conditions imposed on an undertaking in another member state less attractive because it constitutes - i quote again - a restriction on the freedom to provide services or the freedom of establishment, which are among the fundamental freedoms guaranteed by the treaty. this is simply unacceptable. where is the social element in such a liberal logic? indeed, any social advance in a country makes a market in some way less attractive - to use the court's expression - for competing firms. i would add that in all three cases the famous directive on the posting of workers did not provide any protection for the workers concerned. the court of justice has also stated, and i quote, that 'the purpose of this directive is to achieve freedom to provide services'. it doesn't talk about protecting workers. finally, in all three cases the court has taken its decision in the light of specific articles of the treaty and not just the text of the directive. in the light of specific articles of the treaty, article 43 in the first case, article 49 in the other two, both of which are reproduced as they stand in the draft treaty of lisbon in the process of ratification. so my conclusion is clear. amending a directive will not be enough to overcome the problem posed by these judgments. the european parliament has been a party to the maastricht treaty and has been a party to the treaty of rome. it is difficult, but i think it is necessary, because otherwise we can expect a serious crisis of legitimacy in the future for the current european economic and social model.
it is true, commissioner, that we are very disappointed to see the way in which the freedom to provide services is applied, according to the case law. it may be assumed that, in certain interpretations, the court of justice wishes to establish the primacy of articles 43 and 49 over all other considerations. but i am wary of manichean analyses of case law which, as you all know, are first and foremost cases in point. i think the question we need to ask ourselves is how to guarantee the social acquis and how, in particular, to answer two questions. what is the minimum wage level to which a company must be subject under the national law of the host country? and secondly, how far can the collective action of the trade unions to ensure equal treatment between national workers and posted workers be limited? to answer these questions, i do not believe that the secondment directive should be changed. i think we would be taking a big risk to do that. i find the proposal of the european trade union confederation for a social clause more interesting. i believe that it is simply a matter of applying, as elmar brok has said, the old and new treaties, article 3.3, article 6.1 and the charter of fundamental rights, which is now positive law. it is also a question of enforcing - and national parliaments will be able to ensure - the principle of subsidiarity in all matters relating to labour law, workers' rights and the right to strike, in particular. the french presidency must now, in the near future, activate the social agenda and for you, commissioner, the commission must go beyond the simple observation you have made, and beyond the purely administrative and minimal recommendation, to move towards a more political text which takes full account of the uncertainties arising from the case law.

in writing. the 10th edf is the eu's multiannual framework for cooperation and development with the acp countries. it is worth €22.7 billion for the period 2008-2013 and is designed to help some of the world's poorest and most vulnerable countries. the effectiveness of this fund, the financial arm of european development policy, requires that it be integrated into the general budget of the community, rather than the asymmetric contribution of the member states. budgeting european aid would have certain advantages, since aid to the acp would be subject to the same programming and management rules as other eu external action instruments, thus enhancing the coherence, transparency, efficiency and democratic control of development cooperation. the notion of 'historical links' between some member states and overseas countries and territories must be overcome and africa and development made a priority for the eu as a whole. if the eu is concerned about the efficiency of these policies and programmes, then it must continue to modernise its external aid by integrating the edf into the community budget as from 2009.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my polish colleague lidia joanna geringer of oedenberg, which proposes to approve, at first reading by the codecision procedure, the proposal for a codified version of the council regulation on the application of article 81 (3) of the treaty to certain categories of agreements, decisions and concerted practices between liner shipping companies ( consortia ). as this was a codification procedure, the proposal did not need to be formally amended by the parliamentary committee and the latter did not do so. nevertheless, i take this opportunity to express my surprise at the delay with which the european union codifies texts which have been amended several times and whose reading and application become more complex over time. the procedure for codification is provided for in an interinstitutional agreement of 20 december 1994, which was the result of the political will of the european council of december 1992 and which provides for an accelerated procedure for the rapid adoption of codified acts. i strongly support the need to codify community legislation: it is an imperative for democracy, the rule of law, the training of students, the proper application by citizens and legal professionals, etc.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the common position to emerge from a very old case on civil and commercial mediation even if this directive will be limited to crossborder cases, based on a restrictive interpretation of article 65 ec but with a broader definition of disputes. however, i regret that the common position does not allow the implementation of the directive by means of voluntary agreements between the parties, even though it is true that the rules of the member states relating to judicial procedures cannot still be amended by agreements between the parties. overall, this common position is to be welcomed, as it remains true to the original objective of facilitating access to dispute resolution procedures and promoting the amicable settlement of disputes by encouraging the use of mediation and ensuring a satisfactory link between mediation and judicial proceedings.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my distinguished hungarian colleague, mrs etelka barsi-pataky, which proposes to approve, subject to amendments, the amended proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the further implementation of the european satellite radio navigation programmes (egnos and galileo). on this occasion, i commend the determined action of jacques barrot, vice-president of the european commission responsible for transport, for his determination, his lucidity and his capacity for political discernment and conviction in this difficult matter where the public sphere has taken the industrialists out of the impasse as to the strategy to be adopted in terms, in particular, of financial risks. the 100% public funding, amounting to €3.4 billion, was made possible thanks to the will of all, in particular that of the european parliament: it is therefore also the representatives of the citizens who are at the origin of this way out of the crisis with a commissioning in 2014 and a deployment of satellites until 2013. this dossier shows the need to think quickly about the european means to be put in place to finance public investment operations when there is a failure of the private market.
in writing. it took eleven years of painful hesitation and political and administrative connivance to reach a solution for the creation of an independent european satellite radio navigation system. the delay is estimated at 5 years, due to the method chosen: public-private partnership, international cooperation beyond the european union, mandatory participation of all member states, imposed role of the european commission... if these principles and methods had been applied to technological and industrial ventures such as airbus or ariane, europe would probably not have its own aircraft manufacturer or space launcher today. the final result may not be entirely satisfactory, but it is nevertheless instructive. the launch of major strategic projects in new areas where the private sector cannot or will not take risks can only be achieved if the public authorities are the decision-makers and the exclusive financiers. because these are projects that are based on a political vision and not on pure economic logic. secondly, in this type of project, the mandatory passage through the community institutions and procedures has proved to be a brake and a negative factor, multiplying the ideological constraints, where intergovernmental cooperation has proved its effectiveness. let us hope that these lessons will be learned.
in writing. the roure report, like the directive it proposes to amend, is unacceptable. it is unconscionable to allow beneficiaries of international protection to be granted long-term resident status, even if only temporarily, without requiring them to meet any resource requirements or to integrate minimally, when this status can only be granted after 5 years of residence. the provisions also guarantee that such persons will not be expelled, including to another member state, unless they have committed a serious crime. the right of such persons to reside in the member state of their choice would thus become irrevocable, whatever their situation and social status. this prerogative was based on the right of the states to choose sovereignly who can live on their territory, under what status, and under what conditions compatible with public order and security. finally, as you all know, the application for international protection is being used to circumvent the already weak controls or restrictions on purely economic immigration. you know that subsidiary protection, in these circumstances, is often preferred to refugee status, because it is shorter and more flexible. if its beneficiaries can become long-term residents, it will be a new call to immigration.
in writing. while it is true that information, prevention and awareness-raising are essential in the fight against drug use to prevent the dangers of drug addiction to the physical and psychological health of users, unfortunately this is not enough. according to the monitoring centre for drugs and drug addiction, more than 70 million europeans have already smoked cannabis and 60% of nightclub goers in france, italy and britain have used cocaine. it is therefore clear that the european information and communication strategies are totally ineffective, because, unfortunately, the supply and demand of drugs is increasing everywhere in france and in europe. no compromise is acceptable when it comes to drug use and sale. zero tolerance is the only effective policy. the disasters caused to thousands of victims by experimental drug liberalization policies will not be able to undermine this evidence.
in writing. as a fictitious socialist rapporteur, i have devoted a great deal of time and energy to this dossier in order to arrive at the substance, to explain the need for a deeper dialogue with civil society in the field of the fight against drugs, and to propose a text that is readable and understandable by all. i believe that civil society actors, with their experience on the ground and their capacity for innovation, can bring real added value to national and european policies, both in terms of prevention and information, and in terms of ending addiction and social reintegration. all these actions need to be taken at different levels: in the workplace, in schools, on the streets and even in prisons. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report, which welcomes the creation of the civil society forum on drugs and stresses the importance of enhanced cooperation between civil society and all the union institutions and bodies. the fight against drugs concerns us all, and those who are on the front lines of this fight, who work every day to help addicts and prevent more people from falling into addiction, must be privileged interlocutors.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council amending the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 on budgetary discipline and sound financial management as regards the adaptation of the multiannual financial framework on the basis of the report by my distinguished german colleague, mr reimer böge. this adjustment had become unavoidable due to the delay in the adoption of certain operational programmes under heading 1b and 2, eur 2 034 million in current prices of appropriations for the structural funds, the cohesion fund, rural development and the european fisheries fund which could not be committed in 2007 or carried over to 2008. it was therefore logical that, in accordance with point 48 of the interinstitutional agreement on budgetary discipline and sound financial management, this amount should be carried over to subsequent years by increasing the corresponding expenditure ceilings for commitment appropriations.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my french colleague marie-arlette carlotti on the programming of the 10th european development fund (edf) and, as the report states, i regret that this fund is not budgeted in the union budget, thus allowing for democratic control. it is hoped that the edf budgeting issue will be brought up again in the context of the mid-term review of the financial perspective in 2009. as regards the edf and its contribution to poverty eradication and the achievement of the millennium development goals (mdgs), it is urgent to programme it and, therefore, to finalise the political agreements enabling its implementation. priority should be given to strengthening health care and basic education and, in addition, subsistence farming. at a time when the doha agenda is being driven by the world trade organisation (wto), it is becoming urgent for the european union to use its development instruments to participate in this ambitious, equitable and laudable drive to eradicate poverty in the world.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report by my socialist colleague marie-arlette carlotti on the implementation of the 10th european development fund (edf) programming. the edf is the main community instrument for development cooperation assistance to the acp states (africa, caribbean and pacific). it is particularly active in the achievement of the millennium development goals, which were set in 2000 by the united nations. however, the 10th edf (2008-2013) is currently at an impasse: the revised cotonou agreement has not been ratified by some acp countries, and the €22.7 million available since 1 january 2008 has still not been used. the text adopted by parliament therefore urges the unblocking of the situation and sets out a number of complaints: priority should be given to poverty reduction (in particular health and education), specific consideration should be given to gender issues and a sustainable development strategy should be drawn up for the countries concerned. parliament also called for the edf to be integrated into the general budget of the union in order to strengthen the coherence of european policies and to guarantee democratic control of its management.
in writing. i voted in favour of the good own-initiative report by my portuguese colleague ana maria gomès on china policy and its effects on africa. while it is welcome that china is willing to provide concrete and pragmatic cooperation to african countries, there are many areas of concern such as china's cooperation with repressive regimes in africa, non-compliance with social and environmental standards, arms deliveries to repressive and undemocratic regimes etc. i support the proposal that the african union, china and the eu should set up a permanent consultative body to ensure the coherence and smooth functioning of the various cooperation actions and to define a general framework for the implementation of concrete operational projects on common challenges such as adaptation to climate change, renewable energy, agriculture, water or health issues. i also support the idea of initiating a dialogue between the chinese national people's congress, the pan-african parliament and the african national parliaments and our european parliament to promote sustainable development and to strengthen their capacity to scrutinise the executives in peace and democracy.

the agenda calls for the report by mrs cristiana muscardini, on behalf of the committee on international trade, on the way forward for reform of the world trade organisation (2007/2184 (ini)) (a6-0104/2008).
on behalf of the pse group. madam president, madam commissioner, the doha round must be completed, but we must also start thinking again about how the wto works. it is faced with problems of efficiency, legitimacy and interaction with the other organisations in the multilateral system. in some respects it was inevitable that, a little over ten years after its creation, the mechanisms of its operation would have to be re-examined. the transition from gatt to the wto has not merely changed the dimensions of the multilateral trading system but, in some respects, its nature. trade rules have been extended to a considerable number of new areas: services, intellectual property, investment, rules on non-tariff barriers. new member states have joined those which were created, and this enlargement has introduced diversity, disparity of situations, of member states with different resources, with different problems, and so all this really requires that, in parallel with the efforts to complete the development round, the necessary reforms be discussed again. i would therefore like to welcome the work done with our rapporteur, mrs muscardini, the cooperation that has been possible with her and with the other groups, and i would like to stress several points in this report, which i consider extremely important and which i hope will be adopted very broadly by our assembly tomorrow. first, the balancing of international standards and the establishment of new relations between the wto and other international organizations. you will see that in this report we obviously mention the interaction with environmental issues, with health issues - as we have seen in the case of generic medicines and intellectual property, this is obviously decisive - but also the treatment of social issues. we cannot afford to ignore the wto debate on this subject. cooperation between the ilo and the wto, which has been re-engaged by the directors-general of these two organizations, must go much further and the european union must give an impetus to this end, and we propose two very concrete things: firstly, that the ilo be granted observer status in the wto, as is the case with the international monetary fund; secondly, that a committee on trade and decent work be set up within the wto - and the union should propose this - just as there is a committee on trade and the environment, which has made a great deal of progress on the interaction between environmental and trade rules. secondly, i would like to emphasize the aspects of the report which call for the wto to give the weakest member states, the least developed countries, more means to have an equal, effective and efficient participation in all the negotiations, in all the committees in which future agreements and trade policies are being drawn up. thirdly, we also insist on external transparency, on the possibility for civil society, for parliamentarians, for a truly living parliamentary dimension to develop within the wto. we are asking for a genuine parliamentary assembly. today there is an assembly of parliamentarians which meets next to the wto. the director-general comes to him and talks to him like the trade ministers, but we would like to see this recognised, and then we make very concrete proposals, for example on the appeal body and dispute settlement. we think that, as it is a court, a tribunal, well, these sessions should be public. documents should be publicly accessible. and i think it would also help to dispel some of the fantasies and make this organization more transparent. finally, we also insist on the secretariat's resources. that has been emphasized. the wto's budget is now $135 million. it is six times smaller than the imf, almost ten times smaller than the world bank. it has about 600 employees. this is still far less important than that of the other multilateral organizations. so i believe that strengthening the means of a wto that is better integrated into all the other multilateral organizations, more efficient for fairer trade, more transparent to be more legitimate, is also one of the conditions for better trade rules for development.
for the gue/ngl group madam president, the only thing we will agree on is the urgent need to revolutionize the wto. the wto, like the imf, is an illegitimate, undemocratic and dangerous organization for the interests of the people. it was founded in its time to ensure the financial and industrial hegemony of the united states and the large transnational groups. the union has, of course, slavishly served this system, hoping to collect a few crumbs from the american master's feast. the unbridled free trade has now backfired on its promoters and the centre of gravity of the world economy has shifted from the west to asia, producing the worst financial and food crisis our planet has ever known. it is not often that countries which were yesterday classed as emerging economies, and which have now become predators, give up their predatory strategy in the name of some kind of benevolence, the entire international trade organization built around the wto encouraging them to persevere in this course. the rule known to all gamblers is to get rich as quickly as possible, by any means necessary, including speculating on medicines or foodstuffs of primary necessity. inequality has exploded in the union and the working and middle classes are becoming poorer. the food crisis affecting the poorest populations is a direct consequence of the wto's policy of destroying food crops in favour of export crops. biofuels are the easy scapegoat for a market system that must be revolutionised as soon as possible. i would like to denounce mr mandelson's irresponsible remarks calling for further deregulation of agricultural markets at a time when the world food programme is pointing to soaring food prices and saying that this is, i quote, a 'silent tsunami that threatens to drive tens of millions more people into hunger'. so does mr. mandelson want to go down in history books as the infamous "hungry man"? yes, the wto must be transformed to curb speculative behaviour, to favour producers rather than a minority of profiteers in the service of global finance, to encourage food and industrial sovereignty of the peoples and to encourage nations to cooperate rather than compete.
madam president, at a time when the doha round of negotiations is falling apart and getting bogged down, the question of how the wto should function is more important than ever. is it not possible to break the deadlock by reforming the wto? in the absence of agreement on the substance, can the process leading to such an agreement be encouraged? this revival of the wto seems possible and requires the strengthening of its functional and decision-making efficiency. two levels of reform are possible: those aimed at improving the negotiating procedure and those aimed at strengthening the legitimacy of the organisation, a key factor in its organisation. to do this, we must insist on the parliamentary dimension within the wto and give thanks to the legitimate representatives of the citizens that we are, and make the issues of globalisation more transparent and democratic. a great deal of work is also needed to ensure consistency between international policies. it is no use removing barriers at the frontiers if behind them there are still barriers to investment, social rights being flouted and environmental standards being ignored. an effective wto is therefore essential to guarantee the objective of increased trade and market-driven opening-up. and by rule i do not mean protectionist measures. indeed, unchecked liberalisation is not the solution to all the ills, especially those we are experiencing today, through the rise in the prices of agricultural raw materials and the resulting hunger riots. the falconer proposal to lower customs duties is unacceptable for our european agriculture and would have an underestimated impact on agricultural production in the poorest countries. the conclusion of the doha round therefore requires a rebalancing of the negotiations and a genuine reciprocity of market access commitments. we are not yet ready to sacrifice our agriculture and our role as contributors to food security in order to get a few industrial tariff cuts.
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i welcome the debate this evening on the report by mrs muscardini on the reform of the world trade organisation. the food crisis that is now hitting developing countries hard is a perfect example of the urgency of better regulation of world trade. it must be supported by a reformed wto, capable of controlling the course of globalisation and promoting fairer trade rules. this crisis is not cyclical but structural. it is a sign that serious malfunctions are diverting world trade from what should be its primary objective, namely trade for the development of all, and particularly the poorest countries of the world. many elements have been put forward in an attempt to explain the origin of this crisis, and i do not doubt their relevance. but i think we should collectively ask ourselves a few questions. would this crisis have been as serious if the priorities of developing countries had been better addressed at the wto, if there had been better coordination between the wto and other international organisations such as unced and fao, if our free trade agreements had not encouraged developing countries to specialise in export monocultures at the expense of traditional food crops and their food self-sufficiency, if we had heard and supported african countries at the wto when they asked to include a commodity price action in the current round of negotiations? i would remind you that article 38 of gatt requires all wto members to stabilize and improve the situation on the markets for primary products, which are of particular interest to developing countries. in order to address the current dysfunction and to increase the effectiveness and legitimacy of the wto, this report proposes several ways forward. the council also called for the establishment of a european union-wide network of experts in the field of human rights, including the european ombudsman, and for the establishment of a european union-wide network of experts in the field of human rights. in order to ensure greater transparency of the debates and organisational work, better information, dialogue with the organisation and representatives of civil society, and the opening of the proceedings of the meetings to the public, in particular for the dispute settlement procedure, should be considered. finally, the parliamentary dimension of the wto, which guarantees democratic legitimacy and transparency in negotiations, must be strengthened. this includes the creation of a wto parliamentary assembly with consultative powers. beyond these measures, the very aims of the multilateral trading system need to be reviewed in order to ensure consistency with other international organisations. only reform undertaken in this direction will be able to conclude a doha round that is genuinely working towards development and the achievement of the millennium development goals. i would remind you that the first of these objectives is the eradication of poverty and hunger. but unfortunately, the news reminds us of our broken promises.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, trade between nations is a good thing. free trade is desirable, but today the world has changed and the wto rules are inadequate and often need to be changed. the nature of international trade has indeed changed. yesterday, trade was based on complementarities, we sought what we did not have, exported what we had left over. this order has brought prosperity to the nations. but today, social dumping is the priority. we abandon what we know how to make in order to import what the other does cheaper, not because he is more productive but because he is less burdened, less taxed, less socially constrained. this wto order allows poor countries, poor countries in rich countries, to enrich rich countries in poor countries. it is less and less a system of solidarity, of mutualisms organized in nations, but an order that upsets nations and creates a conflict between the caste of the winners and that of the losers. so the rules of the wto must be changed. they must restore community preference and reconnect with the spirit of the treaty of rome, which established the common external tariff. it was not a protection for the frivolous, but a fair compensation for social dumping. the founding fathers weren't always wrong. the wto must take account of the erratic development of exchange rates in its assessment of trade constraints. it is unacceptable that the yuan remains low despite a very high external trade surplus. it is scandalous that eads loses a billion every time the dollar drops 10 cents against an ideological euro. in conclusion, the future of genuinely free trade reminds us that much more must be done before we can let go. on the one hand, we must restore the frontier as a condition for politics and therefore for the freedom of peoples, and on the other hand, we must subordinate the monetary and financial economy to the real economy, the productive economy which alone enables people to live here, now and freely.

the european parliament has a duty to protect the environment. madam president, the conclusion of a free trade agreement between the european community and the gulf cooperation council has been the subject of negotiations since 1988 and it would appear that a final conclusion is approaching. i welcome the latest progress, because the conclusion of a free trade agreement is essential to intensify and regulate trade relations between the european union and the gulf states. they would thus open a new and more dynamic era of cooperation in many strategic areas between two regions of mutual vital importance, but whose relations suffer from a lack of substance. the free trade agreement should contribute to the dismantling of non-tariff barriers and the elimination of all public subsidies and compensation, in particular for access to raw materials, in accordance with current wto rules. the opportunities and challenges of the expansion of sovereign wealth funds should be the subject of substantive work, dialogue and constructive cooperation between the european parliament and the gulf states in particular. the aim is to maintain an open environment for investment while improving its transparency. this means that the managers of these funds must be able to increase the information they provide to the market on the origin of their resources, their investment objectives and their strategies. but europe must also be able to attract these funds, which are the vectors of growth, innovation and job creation, not forgetting the strong international competition for productive capital. the signing of the free trade agreement will encourage the gulf countries to be more receptive to the views of their european partners and will thus diversify and accelerate our exchanges and convergences.
madam president, the european union has been negotiating for almost 20 years now, as has been mentioned, the conclusion of a free trade agreement with the gulf cooperation council. since then, the commission's negotiating mandate has been only very slightly amended, without any real updating. the result is an astonishing situation, to say the least, where the union does not negotiate with the gulf countries on the basis of the same criteria as with its other trading partners, such as korea or the asean countries. in particular, the negotiating mandate does not provide for the inclusion in the future agreement of a clause on social standards or an ambitious chapter on sustainable development. the question of respect for human rights is hardly mentioned. since these elements must be among the priorities of european action, they should not only be fully integrated into the future free trade agreement, but also be the subject of suspensive clauses in the event of non-compliance with the commitments made. it is the responsibility of the union to ensure that democratic principles of human rights, international labour organisation conventions and environmental standards are promoted and respected in all trade agreements it negotiates. in the case of the gulf countries, special attention - as david martin has just pointed out - must be paid to the living conditions and rights of migrant workers, who are present in very large numbers in the region to support rapid growth, but often work in undignified and unacceptable conditions. more generally, beyond economic exchanges, which must be developed within the framework of harmonious trade relations, europe and its countries must strengthen their political and social dialogue. we must therefore implement a free trade agreement which not only does not have a negative impact on the people of this region but, on the contrary, strengthens their political, economic and social rights. this is why it is, for example, essential that in the negotiations on services, the need to guarantee a universal, accessible and sustainable public service at reasonable prices and meeting high quality standards for all is respected.

the agenda calls for the report by anne ferreira, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, on the green paper on market-based instruments for the environment and related objectives (2007/2203 (ini)) (a6-0040/2008).
the rapporteur. - mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking the fictitious rapporteurs and the opinion rapporteurs in particular for their very good cooperation. we can be satisfied today with the balanced report adopted by the committee on the environment, which is the result of a joint effort. the european union's commitment to the environment, both internally and internationally, is unquestionable. having set a number of objectives to respond to the environmental emergency we are facing, the european union must develop the means to achieve them. to this end, it has developed legislation which has been regularly revised over the years and which is applicable in its territory. it invests in research, raises public awareness and encourages good practice in the member states. today we are proposing to explore another avenue, that of market instruments. the report is based on the commission's book, which contains a number of proposals and reflections which i welcome. firstly, it seeks to enrich a text which is, in my opinion, a little too focused on climate change. the subject is certainly essential, but we must not neglect all the areas of human activity whose impacts on the environment are also very important. i also regret that i did not have the information from the consultation which could have helped us to complete our work. in the green paper, the commission proposes to achieve environmental objectives at a lower and more reasonable cost. this should be possible through economic instruments, which are also a flexible means of achieving the objectives set. the report also proposes that the commission draw up an action plan or other instrument for a market instrument for the environment. i would ask the commission to tell us how far it has come in its thinking and whether the results of the consultation it has had so far will confirm or alter the proposals contained in the green paper. i think that is a very important question. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, including the creation of a european environment agency, the establishment of a european
