european environment agency, the establishment of a european environment agency, the establishment of a european environment agency, the establishment of a european environment agency, the establishment of a european environment agency, the establishment of a european environment agency, the establishment of a european environment agency, and the establishment of a european environment agency. in other words, we must avoid being systematic and show a great deal of ingenuity. as regards specific instruments, which i do not have time to deal with here, i would like to stress the scepticism of our assembly regarding the proposal on biodiversity. the reason is simple. it seems to us difficult, if not impossible, to make a real contribution to a more or less rare ecosystem in another territory. secondly, as regards the internalisation of costs, this is a principle which we must support and take action on. at present, the environmental costs of human activities, especially industrial and economic, i.e. in more technical terms, the external costs, are only little or not taken into account. the transport sector is a good example of this. i have noted that the commission is due to propose in june a proposal for a revision of the so-called 'euro-vignette' directive, in particular by making the road transport charge variable. this principle of variability must be increasingly taken into account in the development of market instruments for the environment; the commission is also proposing the same thing in the field of energy taxation, namely a division into two components: one energy and the other environmental. the revision of this directive, if it achieves its aim, should also make it possible to restore the competitiveness of other modes of transport and to use less co2-emitting modes. finally, i would like to stress one point in particular: the question of the competitiveness of the european economy. we are of course in agreement, but the question that we can ask ourselves in this context is whether the cost of inaction would also be a social, economic, environmental and also a political cost.
mr president, yesterday in this parliament i was asked by a 16-year-old high school student: 'is europe prepared to make great sacrifices to save the planet?' this young high school student was very concerned about climate change and asked us how far we were willing to go. it was a reflection of anxiety, too, of a youth that carries an ideal and expects much from us. so we have market-based instruments that have been put in place: the community scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading, or, in the field of transport, the 'eurovignette' directive. these instruments have advantages because they add value to environmental costs and contribute to the achievement of environmental objectives, at lower cost, and encourage companies to commit to longer-term, and this ultimately supports employment. these instruments can help to reduce the adverse effects that environmental taxes could have on the competitiveness of certain sectors. the approach to promoting sustainable development and combating climate change must not only be a deterrent, through taxes and fees, but an incentive by facilitating a faster transition to virtuous behaviour, behaviour that is environmentally compatible. the effort must be made by all, hence the need to internalize environmental costs. it is important to emphasize that environmental taxes should not be seen as a means of increasing tax revenue but as a means of preventing harmful pollution or environmental degradation at a reasonable cost. finally, in the future discussions in the european parliament on the energy-climate package, the introduction of a border adjustment instrument, in particular to avoid possible carbon leakage, will have to be seriously considered. the obligation to reduce co2 emissions while preserving economic competitiveness must be ensured, and in this way i stress the importance of the carbon tax. it is often a taboo subject, but i still find it interesting and worth studying.

in writing. it proposes nothing more or less than the transformation of the wto into a new centre of global governance, with a secretariat whose role and prerogatives would be strengthened on the model of the brussels commission (staff, right of initiative, etc.), a parliamentary assembly, etc., all in coordination with the other bodies that claim to manage the world. paradoxically, it advocates consensus, i.e. unanimity, which, i quote, "guarantees, in contrast to the majority or qualified majority, the equality of all members". but this equality is being trampled underfoot in the european union. paradoxically, he is asking that trade negotiations and dispute settlement should clearly include social, environmental and 'humanitarian' considerations, but that accession requests should be examined only from a commercial point of view! a kind of a posteriori justification of this parliament's massive approval of china's entry into the wto, while it is now complaining about the social dumping practiced by that country, not to mention its repeated violations of human rights.
in writing. the issues raised by mr radwan's report seem very technical but they are crucial. yes, public authorities must have a say in the definition of accounting standards, since they have an impact on all economic actors and even on the tax revenues of the states. it is not healthy for a private body to be established as a de facto legislator, without any political control. the iasb's technical legitimacy is increasingly being called into question because of its more theoretical than professional approach to the issues it deals with. on the other hand, its geographical and occupational composition is not very good. yes, new standards should only be adopted if they are useful, necessary and after a rigorous cost-benefit analysis. yes, the iasb's role should be limited to listed companies and should spare smes. the principle of fair value, on the other hand, favours a short-term approach and gives financial results a predominant role in the management of companies. it aggravates the financialisation of the economy and the volatility of markets. the european union must refuse to apply this standard. but the rapporteur's position on this subject is not very clear. that is why we abstain on his report.

madam president, commissioner, the transatlantic economic dialogue is taking place in the context of a triple crisis: the global banking and financial crisis, which is still not over, the food price crisis and, finally, the persistent crisis in the price of oil. the whole of these shocks are part of a global context of global warming and climate change which calls for a reversal of cycles and a questioning of certain dogmas on which we have based the prosperity of western societies. can the strengthening of transatlantic relations serve such an objective? i believe that, even if it's difficult, complex and conflicting. and this resolution outlines some answers that resonate with the demands and aspirations of european and american public opinion. the first is not to reduce our ambition to the creation of a transatlantic free trade area, but to work concretely to ensure that the development of our trade serves other, more virtuous objectives, in favour of social and environmental standards. in this respect, the resolution which will be put to the vote tomorrow is balanced. it recalls that so-called barriers to trade between the eu and the us are often laws that have a specific social, environmental, cultural or public health purpose, and that these barriers cannot be removed without democratic decision-making and positive legislative action that safeguards these objectives. the text also encourages the european union to draw inspiration from certain bilateral trade agreements signed by the usa, which contain specific specifications on labour law. it is for these reasons, among others, that i believe this resolution is useful for the transatlantic dialogue.
on behalf of the pse group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the directive on european works councils was a pioneering one when it was adopted in 1994. although it only laid down minimum requirements, it paved the way for the right to information and consultation of workers at the level of european-sized groups and was one of the founding elements of a european labour law. but today it has fallen behind the developments in the reality of the enterprise, the financialisation of their governance, and it is even behind the other directives on information and consultation of workers which have been adopted since then. it is therefore absolutely necessary to revise it, to ensure that, in groups of european size, timely information and quality consultation make it possible to find alternatives when workers are faced with decisions on restructuring, closures of sites and massive job cuts. we have seen too many abrupt decisions on collective redundancies in recent years without workers being consulted, without their representatives having a say. sometimes employees hear on the radio that they are going to be fired. their representatives are informed only a few minutes before the decision is made public, usually at the opening hours of the stock exchanges. all of this therefore underlines the urgency of a revision. moreover, this revision was foreseen in the text of the original directive itself, and in the year 2000 there was to be an update of the mechanisms of this directive. since then, however, businesseurope - which was then unice - has tried everything possible to block this revision, to ensure that the consultation does not lead to anything. that is why, ladies and gentlemen, mr bushill-matthews, i, who was rapporteur for the european parliament with others here in 2001, who helped to get an ambitious request for revision of this directive adopted by an overwhelming majority in our assembly, as was the case again in 2007, cannot accept that the european trade union confederation should be called into question. she's in good faith, she's willing to negotiate. and if this consultation and negotiation does not lead to anything, it is up to the commission to exercise its right of initiative. the commission has a monopoly on the right of initiative. we respect that. but it also creates a responsibility for the european union to defend the general european interest, to not allow it to be held hostage by particular interests, to ensure that the workers of our continent can rely on the european commission to defend the right to consultation, to information, in good time, so that a real european social dialogue can take place in the large european groups.

in writing. i am pleased that the european parliament has approved the amendments to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the seychelles for the period 2005 to 2011. the amendments introduced do not alter the basic elements of the agreement. they merely reflect the successes achieved and allow for practical adaptation to real needs. therefore, taking into account the average level of catches over the last three years, the reference tonnage has been increased from 55 000 tonnes to 63 000 tonnes. in addition, in order to balance the situation, the payment to shipowners was increased to eur 35 per tonne in order to harmonize with the other tuna agreements. as a corollary, the community counterpart was reduced from eur 75 to eur 65 per tonne. the total financial contribution thus rises from eur 4 125 000 to eur 5 355 000 a year. the success of this agreement shows the clear and mutual interest of the european union in concluding partnership agreements, particularly in the fisheries sector. the reunion fleet has benefited from these fishing opportunities and i hope that today's vote will help to strengthen and stimulate the strength of our maritime economy.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my italian colleague monica frassoni on the conclusion of an interinstitutional agreement between the european parliament and the commission on the detailed rules for the application of the council decision laying down the procedures for the exercise of implementing powers conferred on the commission, as amended by decision no 2006/512/ec of 17 july 2006. unfortunately, the comitology procedure does not work well and it is urgent to put in place the means to allow both the commission to exercise its implementing powers and the european parliament to exercise control. the reference in the texts to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny, where applicable, shall be mandatory for the three institutions. i am glad that the new agreement defines more precisely the commission's obligation to inform parliament in a manner that ensures the transparency and efficiency of the transmission system and an identification of the information transmitted and the different stages of the procedure. i welcome the establishment of an 'early warning system' to inform parliament of draft implementing measures. i support the idea that the commission should be required to publish all draft implementing measures as soon as they are formally proposed.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my italian colleague monica frassoni on the amendment of article 81 of the european parliament's rules of procedure on the so-called comitology implementing measures. article 81 (4) (a) of parliament's rules of procedure provides that if the implementing measures envisaged by the commission fall under the regulatory procedure with scrutiny, the scrutiny period shall begin to run when the draft measures have been submitted to parliament in all the official languages. i support the proposal to add that in the event of a shorter period provided for in article 5a (5) (b) and in the event of urgency provided for in article 5a (6) of decision 1999/468/ec, and unless the chair of the parliamentary committee objects, the time limit for scrutiny will run from the date of adoption by parliament of the final draft implementing measures in the language versions provided to the members of the committee set up pursuant to decision 1999/468/ec.

in writing. i abstained from the final vote on this resolution for the following reasons in particular. the resolution contains positive points, such as the reference to the precautionary principle. however, i cannot support certain proposals and objectives. while i can accept the principle of a transatlantic market, it is not possible, much less desirable, to complete it by 2015. this completion is in fact a further step towards the elimination of non-tariff barriers (paragraph 17), i.e. social, health, environmental standards, etc. the provisions adopted by the eu through legislation in this area provide satisfactory protection for european consumers and citizens, and they need to be maintained or improved. nor can the labelling and traceability of products be relied upon to ensure consumer choice (para. 28). a consumer protection policy cannot be reduced to this type of measure. it is also necessary to ensure the choice of agricultural products by preventing contamination of conventional and organic crops by gmos. finally, as regards the import of american chicken treated with bleach, the wording used is too ambiguous. imports must be banned if we are to preserve the community's food security policy.
in writing. i voted in favour of my italian colleague marco cappato's own-initiative report on human rights in the world in 2007. i support the view that the commission and the council should, following the example of what they did in establishing the international criminal court, take priority action in support of international tribunals for the protection of human rights. the new united nations human rights council (unhrc) should be seen as a viable framework for improving the human rights situation in the world. i support the promotion of non-violence as a fundamental instrument for respect for fundamental human rights and the fight against the death penalty. like my colleagues, i am surprised that many european countries have still not ratified the optional protocol to the convention against torture and other inhuman or degrading treatment. i welcome the effectiveness of the european instrument for democracy and human rights (eidhr) but its budget remains drastically below expectations and i support an increase in the eidhr budget as from 2009.
in writing. i welcome the adoption today of mr cappato's motion for a resolution on the 2007 annual report on human rights in the world and the eu's human rights policy. this report examines the progress made in all parts of the world in the field of human rights and assesses the efforts made by the eu to promote human rights through its actions and policies. the report rightly stresses the need to improve the coherence of internal and external policies in this area. the report focuses in particular on the issue of the death penalty, the fight against all forms of torture, discrimination and violence against women and the need to strengthen the protection of children's rights. it stressed the eu's responsibility to promote the role of civil society in order to make the fight more effective and relevant and to strengthen the means available to this end.
in writing. i voted in favour of the joint own-initiative report by my belgian colleague, veronique de keyser, and my spanish colleague, josé ignacio salafranca sanchez-neyra, on the european union's election observation missions (eoms). election observation, especially in new democracies, must remain a priority for the eu because while elections do not constitute democracy, they are an essential component of it and therefore a fundamental right of the people. like my colleagues, i regret that the union still lacks a common and comprehensive strategy for the promotion of democracy and that post-electoral operations should be monitored, as it is not satisfactory to have, in some cases, a passive attitude towards countries whose electoral process has been severely criticised by observers.
in writing. i voted in favour of the very good own-initiative report by my excellent british colleague glyn ford on trade and economic relations with the association of south east asian nations (asean) which is part of a broader strategy of bilateral and interregional negotiations with trade partners. in any event, a partnership and cooperation agreement (pca), containing enforceable human rights clauses, is a precondition for the union to conclude a free trade agreement (fta). a solution to the banking secrecy problem in singapore is essential if there is to be any real prospect of an interregional free trade agreement. like my colleagues, i attach particular importance to the fight against counterfeit medicines, which give rise to unfair competition and are a danger to consumers. i regret the adoption of the principle of maximum use of the flexibilities recognised in the declaration on the agreement on trade-related aspects of intellectual property rights (trips agreement) and access to medicines, and this in the absence of a serious evaluation of these arrangements.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is perfectly normal to consult the parties concerned about legislation that is being prepared or adopted. we are the first to recognise, as parliamentarians called upon to give their opinion on sometimes highly technical subjects, the very important information role played by what are commonly called lobbies. their work is useful, but it must be firmly and consistently framed in their relations with all the institutions, and that is why we shall vote in favour of this report. a few remarks, though. we must not confuse all interest groups: we cannot treat representatives of multinational firms or ngos in the same way as representatives of democratic local or national authorities. in our view, the 'legislative footprint', i.e. the mention of the groups consulted, must be mandatory, especially at commission level. we know how much influence these groups have on the drawing up of legislative proposals or the orientation of european policy, and how difficult it is for the legislator to make fundamental changes to these proposals and orientations. finally, the financial information requested from lobbies must be sufficiently detailed to allow the financial interests involved and their holders to be clearly identified.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which brings more transparency. lobbyists are important players who can provide useful expertise. however, it is essential to be able to identify the organisations represented by the pressure groups. a mandatory public register for lobbyists, shared by the council, the commission and parliament, and including all their sources of funding, is a good initiative that will help to bring about greater clarity. the opening of a 'one-stop shop' where lobbyists would only have to register once to gain access to parliament, the commission and the council will also bring more simplification. it is also normal that there should be penalties for lobbyists who do not comply with the code of conduct.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which proposes to better regulate the activities of interest representatives in the eu institutions. in brussels, the 'lobbyists' are legion: their number is generally estimated at more than 15 000, for 2500 pressure groups. their main objective is to influence community decisions, and their activities - which inspire suspicion and mistrust in many citizens - are a full part of democratic life. a member of parliament, for example, will always understand better the issues involved in a draft legislation after having heard the views of professional associations, ngos, trade unions or regions. however, lobbying can only be such a tool in the service of democracy if it is carried out in a transparent manner. meps, like citizens, need to be able to know precisely who these actors are: who is funding them? what interests do they really represent ? the text thus fulfils this requirement by requiring lobbyists to register in a public register common to all the community institutions and to indicate the details of their funding; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my polish colleague lidia joanna geringer from oedenberg approving, at first reading under the co-decision procedure, the proposal for a european parliament and council directive codifying council directive 93/7/eec of 15 march 1993 on the return of cultural objects unlawfully removed from the territory of a member state, as amended by directives 96/100/ec (oj l 1, 1.3.1997) and 2001/38/ec (oj l 10, 1.7.2001). i regret that the process of codification is so slow and it should be remembered that on 1 april 1987 the commission decided to instruct its departments to codify all legislative acts at the latest after their tenth amendment, stressing that this was a minimum rule and that the departments should endeavour to codify the texts for which they are responsible at even shorter intervals. the presidency of the european council (edinburgh, december 1992) confirmed these imperatives. finally, the european parliament, the council and the commission agreed, by an interinstitutional agreement of 20 december 1994, that an accelerated procedure could be used.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my italian colleague pia elda locatelli, drawn up in the context of the consultation procedure, on the proposal for a council regulation establishing the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking. it is a good policy to put europe at the global forefront of fuel cell and hydrogen technologies. fuel cells are discrete and efficient energy converters, which can significantly reduce the production of greenhouse gases. they allow for a great deal of flexibility, as they can consume hydrogen and other fuels such as natural gas, ethanol and methanol. it was therefore essential to set up a community instrument with this joint technical initiative (jti) to create public-private partnerships in research under the seventh framework programme for research and development (fp7). the itcs, which are mainly the result of the work of the european technology platforms (etps), reflect the eu's strong commitment to coordinate research efforts in order to strengthen the european research area and achieve european competitiveness objectives. i support the idea of giving more help to smes.
in writing. the community tobacco fund, financed by the transfer of a certain amount of tobacco aid for the years 2006 and 2007, promotes public awareness campaigns on the harmful effects of tobacco consumption. the committee on agriculture and rural development proposed to extend its funding until the end of the financial perspective and raised the percentage to 6%. tobacco consumption in europe has not changed and the gradual decline in european production is being replaced by tobacco imports. the parallel issue of maintaining the tobacco cmo and thus postponing the 2004 reform which was to apply from 2010 will have to be addressed in the cap health check as decoupling causes almost total abandonment of production without any sustainable alternative from the point of view of the economy and employment, which has had very serious consequences for the rural area concerned but no impact on public health. i think that the fight against smoking and the extension of a transitional period to allow european tobacco producers to find alternatives to this crop and to mitigate the negative impact on our regions are not antinomic.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my british colleague, mr bairbre de brun, on the evaluation of the peace programme (the eu programme for peace and reconciliation in northern ireland), which stresses that strengthening local self-government has been an essential element in peacebuilding in northern ireland and that the involvement of civil society in this process has made a significant contribution to improving the development and implementation of local policies. i support the idea that cooperation between participants in programmes funded by peace and the fii (international fund for ireland) does not end when the programmes expire.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my german colleague, mr friedrich-wilhelm graeffe zu baringdorf, which proposes to amend the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on statistics on meat and livestock, but in a way that should allow for agreement at first reading in the codecision procedure. livestock statistics (twice a year for pigs and cattle and once a year for sheep and goats), monthly statistics on slaughter (heads and carcass weights of pigs, cattle, sheep, goats and poultry) and forecasts of meat production (meat of pigs, cattle, sheep and goats). the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment and the environment from the adverse effects of certain substances and mixtures is a step in the right direction. it seems appropriate to include, in addition to the statistics on pigmeat, beef, sheepmeat and goatmeat, poultrymeat.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my belgian colleague anne van lancker, drawn up in the context of the consultation procedure, on the proposal for a council decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the member states. i welcome the excellent work done by my colleague and friend elisabeth morin, rapporteur for our political group, particularly on flexicurity. at the risk of being off-topic since, in substance, this council decision is only intended to make recommendations to the member states on the basis of article 128 of the treaty establishing the european community (tec), i regret that the commission, while it is its duty under article 138 of the same treaty, does not put the social partners first by stating that the time has come to create a european social law on the basis of the same social partners on the basis of the procedure provided for in article 139 of the tec. we cannot have an ambitious employment policy if we do not put in place a european labour law with the support of the social partners.
in writing. the employment situation in the european union is poor. the average unemployment rate - 7.3% in 2007 - excluding supported jobs, is higher than in other major economies. for example, in north america, it is less than 5%. the guidelines presented to us will make matters worse than better. the lisbon strategy, which the rapporteur welcomes, exposes our economies to unfair competition, particularly from communist china, which is practicing genuine social dumping. in addition, by calling for a reduction in the 'inequalities between third country nationals and citizens of the european union', the report is part of the immigration policy pursued for decades in our countries, which, by bringing in more than one and a half million extra-european immigrants every year, is making our nations third world. the main measures to be taken to develop employment in europe are to restore national preference, which is fair positive discrimination, to reduce the burden of immigration and thus reduce the tax burden on our companies and our workers, and to implement the principle of community preference in order to protect the european market.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my polish colleague janusz lewandowski on the estimated state of the european parliament's revenue and expenditure for 2009. this budget will have to meet major challenges such as the entry into force of the lisbon treaty if it is ratified by the member states, the fact that 2009 is an election year for parliament and the entry into force of the new statute for members. while i obviously agree that we must be vigilant about the quality of budgetary expenditure, i think we must be uncompromising about expenditure on multilingualism (translation and interpretation), which is a condition for the political success of the union. we also need to develop the capacity of meps to receive visitors, as these visits are very popular and help citizens to get to know the union. finally, i believe that the staffing of meps and committees of the european parliament should be increased in order to ensure their independence and the quality of their work; the european parliament has a duty to respect the rights of citizens and to respect the rights of the citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my swedish colleague, mr jens holm, on trade in raw materials and basic products. i agree with the idea of the need to secure the eu's supply of raw materials and to ensure security of access to these materials on world markets, while noting that the eu does not currently propose a coherent policy to enable its economy to meet the competitiveness challenges of increased competition in access to raw materials. i regret that the report does not address the issues of monetary manipulation in the world, which distorts fair competition by means of short-term exchange rates. among the raw materials, oil would have deserved special consideration and i reiterate my proposal for the creation of a european instrument for the annual regulation of the price of crude oil which would at least deserve to be studied - not to combat the laws of the market which are imposed on us - but to regulate the brutality of their application in the internal market and to allow a better impact of the increases in crude oil in the cost price chain of the sectors concerned (fisheries, transport, etc.).
in writing. mr holm's report seems to identify quite clearly the problems facing the world today due to the unprecedented rise in the price of raw materials. for european countries deprived of natural resources, these are problems of competitiveness, hence of employment, security of supply, increased dependence... and, for poor countries, of questioning their development, hunger riots... but if some causes are mentioned, notably the predatory behaviour of certain emerging countries such as china, or the liberalisation of agricultural exchanges, others are hidden or almost, such as speculation, the malthusian agricultural policy of brussels europe, the very principle of global ultra-changeism... as for the solutions, it is clear that this parliament believes essentially in the regulatory virtues of the free and competitive market. the market is now showing its limits. energy, food and raw materials are not products like any other: the survival of peoples depends on them. it is time for europe based in brussels to put its own interests and those of its members first in its international trade relations, rather than the realisation of the globalist utopia at any human and social cost.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my french colleague and friend, margie sudre, which she drew up in response to the commission's communication on the strategy for the outermost regions (orr). i am of the opinion that the fact that measures are justified by increasingly arithmetical means should not be used as a pretext for calling into question part of the union's policy towards its ors, or for discouraging the actors by requiring them to meet conditions that are too difficult to meet. community interventions should act as a catalyst for the spirit of initiative to develop, from the ors, centres of excellence, drawing on sectors that value their assets and know-how, such as waste management, renewable energy, energy self-sufficiency, biodiversity, student mobility, climate research and crisis management. finally, i support the fact that the future common immigration policy pays special attention to the situation in the overseas territories, which are all external borders of the union. i commend the work of margie sudre, who has worked tirelessly, with great skill, determination and heart for the outermost regions.
in writing. france is very concerned about the european union's policy in favour of peripheral regions. the specific nature of these territories must be taken into account, much more and much better than it is today, by the policies of brussels, in particular: - by trade policy, the production of the ors being in competition with those of neighbouring countries benefiting from ultra-preferential conditions from the eu; - by immigration policy, these territories being particularly vulnerable and the influx of illegal immigrants creating economic and social difficulties without common measure with the local capacities to overcome them; - by the provisions concerning state aid and especially by maintaining the tax exemptions enjoyed by these territories, periodically called into question by european law. i am particularly concerned about the legal ambiguity surrounding saint barthélemy: a territorial authority since 2007, this small french island has, by changing its status, wanted to retain the tax exemption which is the condition for its economic survival. but the eu seems to consider it part of the ors, i.e. a territory of the union subject to community law. it would be unacceptable if this ambiguity were to call into question the desire for autonomy clearly expressed by 95% of the population.
in writing. i abstained on the own-initiative report by my finnish colleague lasse lehtinen in response to the commission's communication on the community strategy on consumer policy for 2007-13. i naturally agree that europe's 493 million consumers must be at the heart of the three main challenges facing the union: growth, jobs and the need to strengthen ties with citizens, and that they are the lifeblood of the economy, with their consumption accounting for 58% of eu gdp. i am convinced, however, that if we have achieved the internal market through competition; i believe that in the face of today's global challenges, we must put the producer at the heart of our concerns. furthermore, i am very concerned, in the absence of any serious legal study, about the hasty way in which the report tackles the issue of consumer collective action against producers by asking the commission to come up with a coherent solution at european level offering all consumers access to collective redress mechanisms to settle cross-border disputes.
in writing. i abstained on the own-initiative report by my british colleague elisabeth lynne on the progress made in the eu on equal opportunities and non-discrimination since the transposition of the 2000 directives. i agree with the main principles set out in the report, including non-discrimination in areas such as education, lifelong learning, employment, social protection, housing and healthcare, images of discriminated groups in the media and advertising, physical access of disabled people to information, telecommunications, electronic communications, different modes of transport and public spaces, social benefits and access to them, and goods and services made available to the public, etc. however, i am not convinced that a new directive based on article 13 of the treaty establishing the european community is necessary. the political debate must continue. follow ...
in writing. the lynne report on combating discrimination in the member states, particularly in employment, is in line with the texts adopted by this parliament on this subject. behind the general terms and the few mentions about women or the disabled, it is not difficult to distinguish the real, and obsessive, object of your attention: the immigrant populations. to drown the fish, everything is deliberately mixed up: discrimination against women, young people, the elderly, on the basis of ethnic origin, etc., but also on the basis of national origin. if there is any discrimination which is perfectly justified, morally, legally and politically, it is national and european preference in employment and social benefits. correspondingly, your proposals for 'positive action', since you do not dare to use the real terms, are indeed reverse discrimination, the first victims of which would be, and already are, the europeans themselves in their own countries. but this discrimination seems normal to you.
in writing. there are currently no less than five directives on equal opportunities and non-discrimination in the european union. twenty-eight infringement actions are pending against member states which have not transposed them. we can only regret it. but should gender equality be systematically enforced through coercion and repression? i don't think so, on the contrary. let us stop stigmatising this discourse on discrimination by calling minority groups and populations, and immigrants in particular, 'gentiles' and by blaming europeans who continue to discriminate. we must put an end to these leftist slogans which do not help the cause of people who are discriminated against, but who are instead stigmatised. instead, we should emphasise the individual responsibility to end all forms of discrimination and the need for immigrants in particular to adapt to our rules, laws and values.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my german colleague willi piecyk on an integrated maritime policy for the european union, drawn up in response to a commission communication on the same subject. europe's maritime spaces (two oceans - the atlantic and the arctic - and four seas - the baltic, north sea, mediterranean and black sea) and coastlines (70,000 km) are essential to its well-being and prosperity; they are the trade routes, the climate regulators, the sources of food, energy and resources, and the places where europeans live and play. i'd add that they're a reservoir of water that will be a scarce commodity. in a context of globalisation and rapid climate change, there is an urgent need to act by establishing an integrated maritime policy for the european union, based on the recognition that all issues relating to europe's oceans and seas are interlinked. maritime surveillance, which is essential to ensure safety and security in the use of maritime space, maritime spatial planning, which is a fundamental planning tool for environmentally sustainable decision-making, and a source of comprehensive and accessible data and information are all very interesting avenues.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because i consider it essential for the european union to have an integrated maritime policy as soon as possible. the eu would have much to gain from adopting a coherent strategy in the implementation of the various sectoral policies which have an impact on the maritime sector, such as certain social, industrial or environmental policies, and thus fostering the establishment of a genuine 'network of solidarity'. i also welcome the desire to strengthen the fight against global warming and pollution by creating genuine innovation hubs which can also be a source of competitiveness and social welfare for the union's coastal regions. finally, i support the proposals in the report on the safety aspect of maritime policy, and in particular the idea of drawing up common rules in this area and of sharing the means of surveillance within the community's maritime area. this would make it possible both to combat maritime piracy, which has been on the rise in recent years, and to protect the natural and archaeological heritage of these areas in order to prevent possible disasters with disastrous effects on the development of the union's coastline.
mr president, we cannot seriously consider the question of the transport of goods by road without addressing the problem of dangerous goods. however, in the texts before us today, as in all european legislation, this problem is either underestimated or badly dealt with. but if there is one area where more europe is needed, where more binding community rules are needed, it is this area. as many companies put their dangerous goods on the roads to avoid a seveso site classification of their establishments, the flows of dangerous goods moving through the union are continuing to increase, increasing the risks of major disasters. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the safety of the road transport of dangerous goods is not compromised. the danger of composite charges is grossly underestimated. harmless cargo taken apart can become dangerous if they coexist in the same parking lot. this danger is simply being ignored at the moment. i am advocating the creation of a european agency for the safety of the inland transport of dangerous goods to promote a genuine comprehensive safety policy at union level.
mr president, i would first of all like to thank our two rapporteurs for the excellent work they have done and then to express the hope that under the french presidency this very important road package will of course have a future and a conclusion. i would like to focus on two issues first. the first is that of cabotage and the date which the european parliament has decided to set, i.e. automatic liberalisation in 2014. from this point of view, there is a natural distortion between the countries which are peripheral and the countries of transit. a country like france, a country like germany, probably, a country like austria are by nature the most corrupt countries. and the fact that we have just adopted a definition of cabotage, which is called cabotage following an international journey, is a good thing at the same time, but it assures us that the social question will create considerable distortions, since in road transport the principle of the country of origin is the one that is required. and so i think it would have been much wiser to wait - as was originally planned - for a commission report to enable us to take stock of the social distortions before deciding on automatic liberalisation. secondly, there is the matter of the derogation for bus driving times. i have already said that i think this procedure is abhorrent, without going into the substance of the matter. it is a question, under the influence of pressure groups, of putting forward an amendment which is an amendment to a text which is not the original text. this question should be settled by a new commission proposal amending what was called the markov report. i would also remind you that we are proposing an amendment to the markov report in the form of a regulation, whereas the markov report was a directive. i am not saying that this was a regulation, you are right, it was a regulation, but in any case i think that parallelism of forms is necessary and we must not make a habit of tabled amendments to texts other than the original texts under pressure from pressure groups.
mr president, i am not saying that i give preference to mr grosch or to mrs ţicău but i will speak about cabotage like my honourable colleague mr savary did. this cabotage discussion has been going on for many years. as one of the stakeholders said, ‘the behaviour of the council can be compared to the behaviour of a snail’; that is how slowly the council has been moving on this subject whereas parliament has finally got its act together. cabotage is more important than we realise and i have to say that i cannot agree with my dear friend, mr savary, when he expresses fear that the social market will be distorted. if you do not allow cabotage to happen, what does it mean? it means unnecessarily high transport costs; that means unladen, empty lorries going here and there. what is the eu all about? the eu is all about an open market, and we have to care for eu citizens. if we get the transport costs down that means that the eu citizens will benefit and therefore we are giving them added value in their daily lives. at this point in time people everywhere are asking: ‘what is the eu doing?’ ordinary people are literally running after the money as the prizes are getting higher. well, at the same time we cannot apply protectionism. we must allow people to have a better life and, if we can lower the costs, our economy will improve and the ordinary people will benefit from it. just to give an example, on trade between finland and russia all the transport has been taken over by russian lorry drivers and the finnish citizens are benefiting from it. i cannot see why french citizens – i have my feet in both camps – would not benefit from cabotage. so we have to say ‘yes’ to the future.
the joint discussion is closed. the vote will take place tomorrow at noon.

thank you very much, mr dover. i thank you all the more because, apart from commissioner dimas, you are the only man registered for this debate tonight. i only have female speakers.
the european parliament has a duty to protect the environment. mr president, commissioner, can we accept that our scrapping vessels are going to pollute the beaches of south asia because we refuse to take responsibility for their dismantling? south asia, which receives most of our ships, unfortunately collects pollutants such as asbestos, pyralenes, oils, hydrocarbon sludge, which also end up in the soil, the sand, the sea. if only that were all there was! children are the ones who work on this dismantling, because they can easily get into small spaces and, unfortunately, remove toxic materials without any protection. it's a low-cost labor force, victims of chronic and incurable diseases. from an ethical point of view, this is unacceptable, especially when ships come from europe and end up on the shores of india, pakistan and bangladesh. the european union, which is partly responsible for these social and environmental problems, must take the right measures, in cooperation with the imo, to put an end to social and environmental dumping due to economic incentives. there are urgent measures to be taken, to put constraints on ship recycling, and this must include certification and notification requirements. the future recycling perspective must be taken into account in the design and construction of ships, and the ship recycling facilities must also be planned. there is an urgent need to establish a list of facilities which would be considered the best for this, in terms of human rights, health and safety. and then, of course, without wanting to deprive south asia of this great market, we must also provide for installations in european shipyards so that we can recover what is waste ourselves and then develop what could be called an ecologically rational dismantling, all of which serves as the basis for an international agreement.
the european parliament has a duty to protect the environment. mr president, commissioner, i apologize for the delay, but i tried to respect the speed to respect the climate. our main debate today is about the scientific evidence on climate change. and i would first like to thank my colleague karl-heinz florenz for his remarkable work and also his constant commitment to this issue. my dear colleagues, the scientific knowledge on climate change is now established. the majority of experts now believe that we can no longer doubt that global warming is real and that it is largely caused by human activities. some disagreeing voices are raised to question the reality of this phenomenon, but without any real evidence. the interim report by the european parliament's temporary committee on climate change is the first phase of a process that will lead to the search for solutions. we almost all agree that the global temperature increase should be limited to two degrees above pre-industrial values, keeping in mind the fact that we should, in fact, aim for a target of less than two degrees. but the debate on change cannot be reduced to a battle of numbers. when we talk about climate, we talk about the melting of the arctic ice sheet, desertification, global warming, the movement of animal species, but above all the phenomena that could have catastrophic consequences for the movement of human beings. this is a major challenge for all of humanity. the regions most seriously affected will be the poorest countries in africa, asia and central and latin america, where environmental migration is expected. with the increase in extreme weather events, a new kind of refugee is about to emerge. it's not going to be political refugees, it's not going to be economic migrants, it's going to be climate refugees. and with the reduction in the area of arable land, the food crisis threatens. with the decline of fresh water resources, tensions could increase, wars could break out, with control of resources at stake. our responsibility is immense. it is no longer about questioning the fact of climate change, but about working together to find solutions and to put those solutions into practice. and the climate-energy package tabled by the commission in january is currently being discussed in parliament's environment and industry committees: emissions trading scheme, climate burden sharing, carbon capture and storage and renewable energy. the members of our epp-ed group in these committees and the epp group as a whole are working actively. we expect a lot from these discussions and are determined to join our efforts so that a compromise can be found at the first reading. it is essential that an agreement be reached between parliament and the council before the european elections. ladies and gentlemen, the european union has assumed the role of global leader in the fight against climate change vis-à-vis its global partners and it is essential that it remains so. if we do not take our role seriously and urge the united states on the one hand and the powers, as you have mentioned, commissioner, china and india on the other, to join us in the fight against climate change, who will? europe must present itself united, in order of march, at the international conference in poznań in december 2008, which will foreshadow the agreement we hope to sign in copenhagen in december 2009. the challenge is global, but europe is the power capable of pushing its partners to join it in this fight and we must prepare the future for our children and grandchildren.
madam president, the report by our colleague, mrs ria oomen-ruijten, is thorough, honest and courageous at a crucial moment for turkey, and i pay tribute to her. but this relationship is one of a kind that, in my opinion, is becoming increasingly unreal. the european parliament and many others with it continue to pretend that our tireless teaching can change turkey! because that's what this is about: the contradiction between this country, this nation, this great people, its evolution and the project that we want to lead together. turkey is a nation state, one of the last, one of the strongest, one of the most conscious. the unity of the armenian people is nationalist, and this is evident in the recognition of the armenian genocide. its politics are increasingly inspired by a single religion, while it is moving away from the secularism which was the very basis of its constitution. it is a desire for independence, whereas we here want to implement a principle of integration, delegation of powers and sovereignty. there's a fundamental head-on collision between the two. we must stop deluding ourselves, we must stop telling the turks everything and everything else, and making them believe that we are ready either to accept their accession without really fulfilling the copenhagen criteria or to refuse it because of them, when it is basically about us, what we want the european project to become. and let us define a sustainable partnership structure which, in a win-win spirit, allows turkey to assume its role as a regional power and the european union to continue to build its identity in the world.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report to bring forward the mercury export ban to 15 march 2011, three months before the date proposed by the council. mercury can be obtained from the recycling of waste (e.g. fluorescent bulbs, batteries), from the purification of natural gas or from the industrial processing of non-ferrous metals. i welcome the fact that this ban covers, in addition to metallic mercury, mercury-containing products which cannot be sold or marketed in the european union, cinnabar ore or mercury compounds. it is also very important that compounds used in research and development, medicine or analysis are not covered by the ban, as the report stresses. finally, as regards storage, it is essential that it be secure, as the report and the council suggest. mercury waste should be temporarily stored for more than one year in deep, underground and rock salt mines or in surface facilities, in such a way as to exclude any risk to human health and the environment, before being treated.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my excellent german colleague, mr hartmut nassauer, drawn up at first reading under the codecision procedure, on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the protection of the environment through criminal law. i support the position to reinsert the scheme in the strict field of community law by limiting the effect of the directive to cases of infringement of community environmental law only and, therefore, leaving it to the member states to determine the penalties to be applied in the event of infringement of that law. this is the wise position of the court of justice of the european communities which held that the eu has the power to adopt criminal measures only in cases where there is a 'justified need'; the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area. it is useful to point out that the directive aims to oblige the member states to provide for criminal penalties in their national legislation for serious infringements of the provisions of community law relating to the protection of the environment, without creating any obligations relating to the application of such penalties which may be invoked in individual cases.
in writing. the adoption of a common criminal law within the european union, thus depriving member states of their sovereign and exclusive right to determine independently what types of behaviour they consider to be a criminal offence, as well as the possibility of defining the qualifications and limits of criminal sanctions, is underway. the court of justice of the european communities, by a coup de force, with its judgment of 13 september 2005 in the so-called "environmental protection" case, granted itself a right to intervene in the criminal law of the member states in cases of infringement of environmental legislation. the new stage is now to establish a harmonised set of offences which should be punishable by criminal law in all member states, and to harmonise these criminal sanctions in the case of environmental offences. the court has taken power and handed it over to the commission, in defiance of the peoples, the national constitutions, the parliaments and the proper application of the law. we are sovereignists and are committed to defending the freedoms and the right of peoples to self-determination, and we reject these methods.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my hungarian colleague, gábor harangozo, which amends, at first reading by codecision, the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on farm structure surveys and the survey on agricultural production methods. i support the idea of allowing derogations for member states that would like to carry out the survey on the structure of agricultural holdings in 2009 rather than in 2010 because of the decennial population census in 2011. i am also in favour of all the simplifications proposed.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my romanian colleague, silvia adriana ticau, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing common rules on the conditions for the exercise of the occupation of road haulage operator. the former directive 96/26/ec on access to the occupation of road haulage operator and its four regulations on access to the transport market, together with the deregulation of international road transport prices a few years earlier, shaped the internal road transport market but with a minimum degree of road transport quality, while the market opening organised by the regulations encouraged more competition. experience has shown that these measures are poorly or unevenly applied because they are ambiguous, incomplete or have become unsuitable for the development of the sector. companies remain subject to unequal supervision and controls across member states with very different levels of professional qualification and financial soundness. it was therefore urgent to legislate requiring the conditions of good repute, financial and professional capacity and establishing mutual recognition of some of the documents required for the authorisation to practise.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my excellent colleague mathieu grosch on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing common rules for access to the international road haulage market which aims to merge the texts regulating access to the international road haulage and cabotage market is currently governed by old regulations and directive. in the internal market, international transport between member states is fully liberalized, but certain restrictions on cabotage still exist. i welcome these clarifications and simplifications and the fact that the framework for sanctions for offences committed in member states other than the member state of establishment is being strengthened.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my british colleague fiona hall, who did an excellent job and amended, at first reading under the co-decision procedure, the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the selection and authorisation of systems providing mobile satellite services (mss). as rapporteur for my political group, the epp-ed, i have fought for the best possible geographical coverage of services throughout the union. i am pleased to have been able to help to require that applications should include a commitment that the proposed system will provide coverage of at least 60% of the territory of a single member state at the time the service is set up. in addition, the proposed system must provide coverage of all member states and at least 50% of the population and at least 60% of a single link in each member state by the date set by the applicant but no later than seven years after the publication of the text. finally, applications must include a commitment to allow the use of the proposed mobile satellite services by civil protection and disaster relief services.
in writing. the adoption of this decision is a decisive step towards strengthening the internal market for electronic communications. the goal is simple: to provide broadband internet access for all and to provide mobile multimedia and civil protection services in the event of natural or man-made disasters. the measures taken are in line with the expectations of our citizens, particularly as regards access to the internet: coverage of 50% of the population and at least 60% of each member state is a guarantee that the digital divide will be effectively reduced, including for the benefit of rural areas. this decision is all the more successful as it contributes to greater harmonisation of the management of radio spectrum at european level, which, it should be remembered, is an increasingly scarce resource. it is also the result of the desire of all the member states to provide the telecommunications industries with the means to build a market for services at european level, a market which has hitherto been too fragmented. in the end, mss should be a success both at the industrial level and in terms of strengthening cultural diversity and media pluralism.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my german colleague klaus-heiner lehne on simplifying the legal, accounting and auditing environment for companies, in response to the european commission's communication on the same subject. like my colleagues, i welcome the commission's general objective of reducing the administrative burden on european businesses. but this reduction must not come at the cost of legal or accounting uncertainty at the moment when small and mediumsized enterprises begin to penetrate the internal market. i am glad that parliament did not consider raising the thresholds set by the communication for micro-entities below which they are exempt from the obligation under european law to submit accounts, to have their accounts audited annually and to publish them. finally, i welcome the fact that parliament voted on an amendment which i had proposed in committee and which was not voted on and which recommends that a consultation be organised to examine the need and the possibility of creating a european regulator in the accounting and auditing services.
in writing. false truths, erroneous statements, sexist remarks and stigmatising of men in a primary way - in a few words, although brutal - this is the substance of the report presented to us. equality between men and women and better integration of women into the working environment cannot be conceived in an authoritarian and repressive way. the results can only be negative and counterproductive. it is true that delays in integration, pay gaps and lack of career profiles are a problem for women, particularly in the specific case of the science and research sector. but once again, it is through consultation, the introduction of non-binding measures to encourage long and scientific studies for young girls and the active support of women throughout their careers that the place of women in society will finally change.
in writing. i voted in favour of the interim report by my german colleague karl-heinz florenz on the scientific evidence on climate change in the european parliament's temporary committee. scientific consensus on the origins and causes of climate change is well established and globally recognised. scientific evidence from all continents and most oceans shows that many natural ecosystems are already affected by regional climate change due to historical carbon emissions from industrialized countries. it has also been scientifically proven that the underlying causes of global warming are largely man-made. i am pleased that the report stresses the need for further analysis and research on the consequences of climate change such as the impact on economic competitiveness, energy costs and social change in europe, the role of land use, the role of forests and deforestation, the role of the marine environment and the calculation of the external costs of climate change from industry, and in particular transport, including quantification of the impacts of air pollution.
in writing. in the 1960s, the french parliament, having benefited from planning, voted each year on a growth rate for the economy and thought of deciding on it, because it happened that for several years in a row the real growth was the one it had voted for. i have the same impression reading mr florenz's report: that this parliament intends to vote on the global temperature! let us be clear: what i am criticizing is not the need for man to take care of his environment, to preserve the immense diversity of nature or, for economies, to find ways of using natural resources better and saving them. it's the ritual sacrifice to the new climate religion and its new gurus, these mind-oriented scientists who cast anathema on anyone whose work goes against their untouchable conclusions. it is the systematic stigmatization of man, as evil, and especially of western and european man. it's institutionalized repentance. it is the industrial and economic suicide of europe alone on the altar of so-called global warming, with no benefit for the environment at world level, but with the worst human and social consequences for the european populations. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. i abstained on my dutch colleague ria oomen-ruijten's own-initiative report on the 2007 report on turkey's progress towards accession, although, like our committee on foreign affairs, i welcome prime minister erdogan's commitment to make 2008 the year of reforms and for turkey to transform into a modern and prosperous democracy, based on a secular state, and a pluralistic society. but it is worth recalling turkey's commitment to good neighbourly relations with greece and bulgaria and the need to achieve a comprehensive settlement of the cyprus question on the basis of the principles on which the eu is founded. turkey has also failed to respond to calls for an end to the economic blockade against armenia and for a reconciliation process with armenia, allowing for a frank and open debate on past events. these negotiations are important for the eu and turkey as the latter is acquiring the acquis communautaire. however, these negotiations must in no case prejudge the final political decision on turkey's accession to the union.

in writing. the report by mrs oomen-ruijten illustrates the autism of the leaders of europe in brussels, denying the obvious: turkey is an asian country. this blindness leads them to deny the foreseeable consequences of such adherence. turkey, with more than 100 million inhabitants in 2020, will be the most populous state in the european union and, therefore, the most important in the european institutions. our assembly is thus in danger of being dominated not by the epp or the socialists but by the islamists of the akp. turkey will also be the most assisted country: its regions will absorb the bulk of the structural funds and its ten million farmers will complete the destruction of the common agricultural policy. the rejection of reality also leads our governments to ignore the will of the peoples of europe. thus, after imposing on the french the european constitutional treaty they had rejected in 2005, sarkozy is preparing to delete article 88.5 of the constitution, subjecting the entry of a new state into the european union to a referendum. if brussels succeeds in forcing turkey to join, then we should propose to our nations that they leave this whole thing, which would have nothing european but the name, in order to build another europe, a european europe: the europe of the homelands.

the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in turin i was able to appreciate the excellent work of the foundation, which is an indispensable and very effective instrument for the development of vocational training systems in the union's partner countries. the commission's draft updates its tasks and governance so that its action is based on a sound legal basis. the compromise reached with the council brings two essential advances in my view. firstly, the new regulation will enable the foundation to intervene in all the union's partner countries, including beyond the framework of the neighbourhood policy or pre-accession programmes. this is a crucial point. the union takes decisions, for example, which have a direct impact on the economies of its acp partners. i shall not learn from commissioner louis michel that this is what has recently happened with the reform of the sugar cmo, which has forced these countries to undertake a thorough diversification of their industrial activity. the training foundation could have usefully contributed to this development and will be able to do so in the future in cases of a similar nature. the second contribution of the compromise, which i particularly welcome, is a genuine involvement of members in the monitoring of the foundation's activities. this is a matter that is beyond the scope of this agency. parliament has only one occasion, often a very poor one, to look at the functioning of the agencies when it votes on the budget and on discharge. however, i think it is no longer possible, especially with the forthcoming entry into force of the lisbon treaty, for parliament not to be more involved in the substance of the matters dealt with by the agencies. that is why, in the specific case of the foundation, parliament will now appoint three representatives, without voting rights, but three representatives on the board of directors, provided that they are particularly competent in the areas of activity of the foundation. parliament is free to appoint either outside figures or members. he will be responsible for choosing the level of representation he intends to promote on the management board. the main thing at this stage is that the choice is now open and that the debate on parliament's involvement is launched. the multiplication of agencies must necessarily lead all the european institutions to eliminate the means of controlling their action. in this context, i am convinced of the need to create a real link between parliament and the agencies. in the same spirit, the new regulation aims to formalise the hearings of the foundation director before parliamentary committees. for several years now, this director has been speaking once a year in parliament at the invitation of the employment committee, but this invitation has not been formalised until now. finally, the director will be appointed for five years by the management board on the basis of a list of at least three candidates submitted by the commission and, before being appointed, the candidate selected by the management board will have to make a statement before the competent committees of the european parliament and answer questions put by the members of those committees. let's be honest with each other. the compromise we have reached on parliament's involvement is not what i would have liked. but you have to face the facts. at the present stage of the debate, the minds are not yet ready to go any further. it is therefore reasonable to support the negotiated package to enable the foundation to operate as quickly as possible on a sound basis. i therefore ask you, ladies and gentlemen, to adopt compromise amendment no 11, the result of the trilogue to which commissioner michel referred earlier, to adopt it as a whole, and not to give in to the temptation that an amendment might call into question the balance achieved. i would like to thank the slovenian presidency and the commission for the quality of the dialogue we have had on these issues and, of course, all my fictitious colleagues for their support.

on behalf of the pse group. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, our discussions on aid effectiveness have been marked in recent weeks by the dramatic news of the world food crisis. this crisis is a stark reminder that if we are not able to ensure the most basic right of all, that of living and eating properly, then our development aid efforts will be in vain. in this report, mr van hecke, whose work i welcome, points out that only a long-term strategy will make it possible to give real support to the development of our partner countries. in the field of food, public health and education, only sustainable solutions can address the root causes of the current crisis. the many amendments tabled by the pse have supported the rapporteur's position and strengthened it on certain points. we have thus reiterated that our priority objective must be the achievement of the millennium development goals, the first of which is the eradication of poverty and hunger. to do this, and to make aid more effective, it must be better adapted to the local context, as close as possible to the terrain and to the needs of the local population. this is why i recalled the need to better consult national parliaments, civil society and local authorities in the formulation, implementation and evaluation of development policies. it is also essential to combat corruption effectively and to make aid more transparent. in concrete terms, we ask the commission to produce a matrix of all funds allocated to local governance in order to verify policy coherence and the proper management of these funds. finally, because the debate on the best effectiveness of aid is inseparable from the debate on the amount, i would like to recall - as was said earlier - and condemn the unjustifiable reduction in official development aid between 2006 and 2007, from 0.41% to 0.38% in europe. the accra summit, commissioner, will be political. it will be a unique opportunity for donor countries to reaffirm their commitment. it's our responsibility to be on time and not disappoint our partners.
, in writing. in 2005, the paris declaration set out specific commitments to promote greater effectiveness of development aid, based on dialogue and mutual accountability. this international framework is essential for the eu, which provides over 55% of total global development aid. the ep also calls for simplification of procedures, the fight against corruption and the disbursement of aid according to the partners' own priorities, in order to further improve the quality and effectiveness of this aid. these measures are more than necessary even though member states' development aid has been somewhat reduced from 0.41% to 0.38% of eu gni between 2006 and 2007. with the food crisis affecting the most vulnerable in developing countries and access to water and education remaining limited, it is understandable that the eu needs to redouble its efforts to meet the mdg target of devoting 0.7% of its gni to development aid by 2015. similarly, for aid to take the form of long-term and predictable financing, it is vital to provide additional resources through innovative financing and to mobilise sovereign funds for productive investment.
