before proceeding to the explanations of vote, i would like to inform you that the conference of presidents has decided, in accordance with rule 127 (3), to change the calendar of sittings for this year and to convene an extraordinary plenary session on tuesday 24 june from 9 a.m. to 11 a.m. the council will be discussing the results of the european council on 19 and 20 june and the results of the six-month slovenian presidency.
in writing. the global food crisis (83% price increase) which is currently translating into hunger riots in developing countries and a reduction in the purchasing power of the most modest european consumers is, in my view, linked to: - unprecedented stock market speculation on the prices of basic food products, which unacceptably takes advantage of tensions and high volatility in agricultural markets; - the development of energy crops at the expense of essential food crops; - the shortcomings of european development policy; - the fact that support for export crops in developing countries has come at the expense of food crops and food self-sufficiency; and - the current rules of world trade which create particularly unfair conditions for small farmers, especially in developing countries. beyond emergency action, we must, in the context of the cap health check, redefine our means of intervention on world markets (infrastructure, intervention stocks, risk management, prospects and economic modelling of price developments, etc.), reverse the decoupling of aid and rethink our agricultural production models globally so that they are productive and sustainable.
in writing. at a time when food price rises are of the greatest concern, a european parliament resolution is needed more than ever. on the one hand, the food shortages that are occurring in many parts of the world are simply unacceptable. urgent measures must be proposed to put an end to the famine which is afflicting the most vulnerable people in developing countries at this very moment. in addition to these emergency measures, which will not provide a long-term solution to the problem, the eu must put in place a strategy, in agreement with international organisations (including the world bank, the imf, fao and the wto). a comprehensive strategy that will have to take account of all the causes of the crisis: changing eating habits in asia, the rapid growth of biofuel crops, etc. on the other hand, the worrying rise in the price of the consumer basket within the european union provides an opportunity for a thorough reflection on the reform of the common agricultural policy. at the time of the health check, concrete proposals must be made to stop this inflation within the internal market itself, but also to ensure the eu's food self-sufficiency.
in writing. i supported the wojciechowski report on a new animal health strategy. as the member for massif central-centre, i am particularly concerned about the current outbreak of bluetongue in europe, which is very serious because of its duration, its spread, the spread of the various serotypes of the disease in previously free areas and the serious socioeconomic consequences of restrictions on the movement of livestock and trade. i think that the commission, as part of an animal health action plan, must improve its capacity to respond to such serious animal diseases by means of research funding, compensation for losses, advance payments, etc. i voted against amendment no 12 which mentions that the transport of live animals over long distances is likely to increase the risks and that the transport time for animals destined for slaughter should be capped at nine hours. on the other hand, i voted for amendment no 3, which states that the quality of transport is more important than the duration of the transport for the welfare of animals. there is a specific regulation on this matter, and we must monitor its application.
in writing. after extensive debate and numerous amendments tabled in comagri, the wojciechowski report, as adopted, proposes substantial changes to the european commission's proposals. these amendments bring a certain balance to the report and will make it possible to modify and improve effectively the legislative framework governing animal health in the european union. on the question of high concentrations of animals in intensive farming systems, the comagri vote moderated the rapporteur's initial position, recognising that they can be problematic when inappropriate disease control measures are implemented. the amendment tabled in plenary on behalf of the epp-ed, concerning the transport of animals over long distances, should also allow the eu to limit the unnecessary suffering of animals destined for slaughter, while maintaining excellent health conditions. the other measures proposed in the report, such as encouraging the use of emergency vaccination, increasing the sense of responsibility of farmers or clarifying the role of each individual in financing the future strategy, are in the right direction and are likely to strengthen eu legislation on animal health.

member of the commission. − madam president, first of all allow me to thank the rapporteur for her work on this report. i am pleased to note the strong support of the committee on fisheries on this important proposal to prevent, deter and eliminate iuu fishing. as you know, iuu fishing constitutes a major threat to the sustainability of fish stocks and marine biodiversity, which undermines the very essence of the common fisheries policy. i do not believe that it is necessary to expand any further on the disastrous global environmental and economic consequences of iuu fishing, as you are well aware of that. however, it is important to bear in mind that iuu fishing is a worldwide phenomenon, affecting in particular developing countries. this is why the proposal is a non-discriminatory instrument, applying to all community trade of fishery products deriving from iuu fishing, in all waters, and to all community nationals engaging in or supporting iuu fishing activities conducted under any flag. international cooperation is the key to the efficient elimination of iuu fishing. this is why the commission has already commenced bilateral contacts with third countries. the commission has also defined a working programme, in close cooperation with the development dg and europeaid, to support developing countries, in order to assist them with a smooth and successful implementation of the regulation, in particular with regard to the catch certification scheme. this working programme includes seminars and workshops in a large number of third countries. the commission can agree with nearly all amendments proposed, which are either covered by the proposal or which are incorporated in the presidency compromise text. i am extremely happy that the report supports, in particular, the implementation of the regulation to all vessels, its catch certification scheme and the harmonisation of sanctions. the inclusion of community vessels is an important feature which will ensure non-discrimination and consistency with wto rules. it is also important that the community demonstrates its seriousness in fighting iuu fishing activities, by including all vessels infringing conservation and management rules. the catch certification scheme is the instrument which will ensure the control of traceability of fishery products. inspired by current practices in regional fisheries management organisations and customs regulations, it must apply to all fishery products, including processed products, in order to be efficient. aquaculture products and products with marginal community trade will, however, be excluded from its scope. we can do this during final negotiations in council. harmonised sanctions will strengthen the ability of member states to take measures to prevent iuu activities and to ensure that any economic advantage will be more than offset by the fines imposed. the commission strongly believes that a system of dissuasive, proportionate and harmonised sanctions and accompanying measures is the key to compliance with the regulation. i would once again like to thank mrs aubert for the report and the committee for its attention on this very important issue. this report is a significant contribution to a truly efficient fight against iuu fishing.
the rapporteur. - madam president, the events taking place in brussels today show us how much the future of european fisheries is threatened if the european union is not able to implement sustainable management of fisheries resources and a fundamental reorientation of the policies pursued so far. the fight against iuu fishing is a major element of this more demanding and more coherent policy. however, the globalisation of trade, the free flow of financial flows and the development of transport and communications have led to a significant increase in illegal fishing activities in recent years. today the situation is no longer sustainable and european fishermen, as well as all the players in the sector, such as ngos, are unanimously calling for a more effective fight against this phenomenon, which accelerates the degradation of resources and is totally unfair competition compared to those who respect the rules. but it is little wonder that the member states have not been able, up to now, to monitor and punish illegal practices as they should have done, and the court of auditors' report published a few months ago is, in this respect, overwhelming. that is why the european commission's ambitious proposal, which was presented last october, was particularly well received by our committee, which had already adopted by an overwhelming majority an own-initiative report on the european union action plan to combat iuu fishing in february 2007. in fact, the commission's legislative proposal takes up the bulk of our recommendations and we welcome that. blacklists and the publication of these lists, reinforced control measures in port states, compulsory catch certificates for the flag state and thus refusal to import products from illegal fishing into the european community market, reinforced and harmonised sanctions, alert system, etc. the commission's proposal is therefore not lacking in much. but as you know, three points were the subject of intense debate in the council, particularly as regards the scope of application. i am glad that we have finally succeeded in maintaining the scope of application that you proposed, which applies to both community vessels and third country vessels. the catch certificate was also considered too burdensome or complex, and the level and nature of the penalties were also hotly debated. these questions have also been raised in our committee. but in the end, i think our amendments have made it possible to clarify the text while preserving the ambition and the main objectives of this new regulation. the report was voted unanimously and i would like to thank my colleagues for their excellent contribution to this result. this is a very strong signal that the european parliament wants to send today, in the midst of the crisis in the sector, and that it is particularly directed at the council, which has been too late in taking on responsibilities in this area. the fight against iuu fishing is only one part of a wider policy, which includes the control regulation and the regulation on serious infringements. this division has not helped to clarify the debate, to say the least. and we are still waiting for your clarification on how these three new regulations will be structured. similarly, concerns about the complexity of the capture certificate have not been just bad excuses to weaken the text or delay it. we need procedures that are understandable to all, that can be used by a sufficient number of competent staff, that are reliable and efficient, and that are also accessible to developing countries, which are the first victims of illegal fishing. we are also waiting for clarifications and commitments from you. finally, we count on your full determination, mr commissioner, and we know that it is strong, to bring an end to illegal fishing, particularly for bluefin tuna and cod, which are highly prized but are currently being overexploited. that is at least a concrete response, starting tonight, to the serious problems facing the fisheries sector at the moment. there is still a lot of work to be done, as you know, to ensure a sustainable future for european fisheries, but an important step will be taken in the coming weeks and i am delighted with you.
member of the commission. − madam president, first of all, the level of the debate on this important subject demonstrates that we share a strong commitment to address the issue of iuu in an effective and comprehensive manner. the truth of the matter is not only that iuu is an activity that threatens the sustainability of fish stocks, but it is also an activity that threatens the future of honest fishermen within and outside the european union. in order for us to be successful in our efforts, we must ensure three crucial principles. the first is that the scope of the proposal remains comprehensive. secondly, the certification scheme put in place must be effective yet ensure that there are no unnecessary burdens imposed as a result. and the sanctions scheme we proposed must be such that these can serve as effective punitive measures and, therefore, be dissuasive by their very nature. with regard to these three principles, i have heard confirmation that you have managed to sort out various issues with member states concerning the scope, the certification scheme and the sanctions. you have done so without diluting or diminishing the effectiveness of the proposal. specifically on the sanctions, let me say that one of the major problems with control is the fact that the range of sanctions applied by member states is so diverse that it is the sector itself which has consistently and constantly called for a level playing field in this area. it is for this reason that, at the very least, we have proposed levels which should be applied in a proportionate and in an effective manner. on the wider issue regarding the reform of the common fisheries policy, i can confirm that we have started reflecting on this and will be having an orientation debate in council in the coming months. in fact the idea is to have an informal ministerial meeting in september. we are also dealing with over-regulation, with a view to simplifying the regulatory regime that is in place. let me also say that i cannot agree more with the comment made by mrs aubert that the fight against iuu, if effective, will help fishermen to better face up to the problems and the difficulties they are now facing, and this point was made by certain other members who intervened. i also, however, agree that it is not sufficient. on the issue of developing countries, we are committed to addressing this issue effectively, as i said in my opening remarks. taking measures to assist developing countries is key if we are to solve the problem and not simply to displace it. as regards control issues, let me assure the rapporteur that the commission is coming up with a strong proposal during the third quarter of this year which will also be merged, or harmonised, with the iuu proposal that we have before us. in that way, both will be convergent and attain the same results. as regards the fuel crisis, we already have the possibility of medium- to long-term measures that are in place, and this would be in combination with the restructuring of the sector. we will be looking at the market measures in place – this point was raised by some members who intervened – which work in such a way that increased costs are borne by the fishermen and are not passed on to the consumer, as happens in other sectors. we therefore need to look into this in order to find out why. there are systems in place which bring about a situation whereby it is the fisherman who ends up suffering, who ends up having to bear the increased costs himself, rather than those being passed on to the consumers. we also offer fishermen some possibilities for providing immediate assistance, if this is linked to restructuring in the form of rescue and restructuring aid. however, i need to say here that i am also looking at this and am discussing it with my colleagues, with a view to trying to identify other ways and means whereby we can help fishermen face up to this new reality in the very short term. but i need to underline that we can only do this if there is a firm and a fixed-term commitment to restructuring, because the problem is also that of over-capacity. therefore, unless we tackle the problem of over-capacity, we will have a recurring problem for as long as fuel prices remain as they are, or – worse still – if they continue rising, as the indications suggest. this is what we have done with france, where agreement was reached between the commission and france on a package of measures which are intended to help the french fisheries sector to restructure. i have to admit that this was not enough and did not satisfy the french fishermen. i need to underline that, for the commission to respond, we also need the cooperation and active engagement of member states. we cannot act on our own. in this regard i understand that this crisis will be raised and discussed at the forthcoming june council, and i personally welcome it. on the question raised at the very end by mrs doyle concerning the application of subsidies by some member states and not others, the information that the commission has is that these subsidies that have been granted by different member states either fall within the parameters of the de minimis (and any member state can grant subsidies as long as they fall within the threshold of de minimis) or are under restructuring programmes to which i made reference before. there is the communication with regard to rescue and restructuring aid and, if agreement is reached – if the commission gives the green light to a restructuring programme – then there are certain possibilities with regard to subsidies, with regard to state assistance, which would not otherwise be possible. where we have had information with regard to other subsidies which are not covered either by de minimis or under restructuring programmes, we are investigating them. there has just been, for example, a notification to france that the amount which was paid in the form of an insurance scheme has to be re-collected. so we do take action in order to see to it that the european rules with regard to competition are properly observed. however, i would end by saying that the immediate crisis is such that we need to address it very carefully in order to find ways and means whereby we try to find solutions of an immediate nature but which would also have the conditionality that there is a firm commitment within the short term for the fisheries sector to restructure in order to bring about capacity levels to match what can sustainably be fished out of the seas.
the rapporteur. - madam president, i should like to begin by thanking all the members who took part in the debate, and the commissioner. of course, we also discussed the serious crisis the sector is currently facing, which is quite normal, and i thank the commissioner for answering the questions that have been asked about this as precisely as possible, although of course it is difficult to go into detail in some respects. in any case, in this context, it is regrettable that the european union - brussels, as they say - is systematically blamed for all the ills and i think that we have a good opportunity here to show that the european union, brussels, is not part of the problem, but above all part of the solution. it is true that when we see the resentment that can be felt towards the european union, we realise how the member states and many players in the sector have for years evaded their responsibilities by favouring very short-term interests, thinking that they will benefit for a while, but refusing to see that in doing so they were driving an entire sector to the edge of the abyss. now we're here. how can we find immediate solutions to a problem that has persisted for years? it's not easy. you've been following a few leads. but we will not get out of this unless we take strict and demanding measures, unless we use all the necessary means, because these texts will not be implemented without financial and human resources, while adopting sanctions that are much more dissuasive than they are today in relation to illegal fishing, and this will not be very difficult, given the very low number of infringements and fines that have been taken in recent times. it will also be necessary to encourage and reward much more, to pay much more for behaviour, for smart, sustainable practices, and often fishermen, fisheries companies that are moving towards practices that are both extremely respectful of the rules and innovative in terms of sustainable fisheries management, may feel that they are not recognised, that they are not being rewarded enough. i also believe that, both in terms of the fight against illegal fishing and in relation to other subjects that have been discussed, such as discards or resource management, respect for quotas, we must also think about a policy that is much more rewarding for those who are moving forward and in the right direction, which i believe is not the case today. in conclusion, i think that this report gives us an opportunity to raise all these questions. of course, this discussion will not solve the problems. we shall continue to discuss this, i think, in the next report, but i believe that we need a high point of very general consultation, not this head-to-head between the representatives of the profession, the government and the commission, seen from the top down, but a very broad, very transversal, more horizontal than vertical consultation, which allows us to find the right solutions and here the european union, the european parliament, once again plays its full role and will assume all its responsibilities in the solutions to be found to respond to the crisis in the sector.
in writing. the european parliament deals a fresh blow to illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, a veritable international scourge. the measures adopted effectively complement the existing system. i am particularly concerned about the introduction by the port state of a system of control of vessels calling at the port, involving the issuing of a certificate attesting to the legality of the catch and the prohibition of accepting pirate vessels. i also welcome the ban on the import of fish from illegal fishing and the publication of a list of rogue vessels. the added value of these new european rules also derives from the development of a community alert system triggered in the event of suspected illegal fishing. the system of sanctions has also been strengthened, including a ban on illegal vessels from receiving public subsidies and an obligation to repay them, if any. above all, i have successfully fought for the european parliament to give special attention to the outermost regions in the fight against illegal fishing, because of the exceptional fragility of their ecosystems. it is a strong signal to the unscrupulous fleets that will make it possible to put a real brake on the unfair competition which is slowly suffocating our fishermen.
the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the customs union, which celebrates its 40th anniversary in 2008, was one of the first steps in the process of european integration. it has made it possible to abolish all customs duties between the member states and to adopt a common external tariff. it is one of the conditions necessary for the proper functioning of the internal market and the proper application of the union's trade agreements. within the customs union, the effectiveness of import and export rules and procedures is a major element of the economic performance of the european union and the social protection of its citizens. you have recently published, commissioner, the customs statistics for 2007, which show, i quote, new and alarming trends. counterfeiting, you said, continues to pose a dangerous threat to our health, our security and our economy. there are many concerns about consumer protection and my report makes proposals for compliance with european standards, particularly in the area of health and safety. another example: the issue of cigarette smuggling, which was raised in this parliament last september and on which i was rapporteur for my political group, has clearly highlighted the scale of the problem and revealed the weaknesses of our community transit system. that is why our committee on international trade has questioned the quality of our customs system and its ability to meet the challenges of globalisation of trade in a context where the citizens who are watching us expect the union to protect them. this is what the treaty of lisbon, which is currently being ratified by the member states, proposes, and article 1 (4) provides that the protection of its citizens will be one of the objectives of the union in its relations with the rest of the world. at international level, the main uncertainty is the outcome of the doha round negotiations, led by the world trade organisation, for which reaching an agreement seems a distant prospect. we all know that if the global multilateral trade negotiations fail, we will enter into bilateral competition governed, we are all aware of this, by the law of the strongest and we will need a strong and effective customs union. within the world customs organization itself, progress towards the efficiency and global harmonisation of customs procedures has been slowing down, following security concerns in the united states since the september 2001 attacks. however, on international trade, the report points out that overly strict import and export rules and procedures can constitute a non-tariff barrier that discourages trade. i would ask the commission to pay particular attention to small and mediumsized enterprises, which list excessively restrictive customs rules and procedures as one of the main obstacles to international trade. the customs system must be used to facilitate trade and the report proposes that this issue be the subject of a global agreement separate from the doha agenda. the report also examines the many issues relating to tariff classification, value and the preferential and non-preferential treatment of goods, with the aim of drawing the attention of the commission to the requests of the industrial sectors concerned. finally, i would like to emphasize that the persistence of a lack of harmonization seems to me to be one of the obvious causes of the weakening of the european customs system. i understand, commissioner, that the reform of the community customs code and its application is your priority, that it is a sufficiently complex task not to add institutional reform. however, i would like to open a line of thought by proposing that the possibility of creating an integrated coordination of national customs administrations be studied, with a view to moving towards a community administration in charge of the customs union. the logic of ever greater harmonisation of customs rules implies that the customs function will become de facto identical throughout the union. given the long delays involved in community developments, especially those affecting the prerogatives of the member states, i believe that the time has come to bring this question to the table, which is both symbolic, because it is the culmination of forty years of ever-increasing customs integration, and pragmatic, because it is raised with the aim of managing procedures more efficiently in a world that is becoming increasingly complex, fast-moving and not waiting for us.
madam president, commissioner, we are in the midst of a customs night, as we have mr markov's report on the gsp and jean-pierre audy's report on non-tariff barriers, that is to say, the rules of procedure for import and export, the so-called administrative protectionism, that is to say, the pharisaic customs barriers. in fact, if we talk a lot about tariff reductions from gatt to the wto, we also practice subtle protectionism, with quotas, with tariff peaks - europe has more than 110 tariff peaks; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. europe has more than 5 000 tariff lines. in agriculture alone, we have 2 726 tariff lines. japan, it's true, has 1,890 and the u.s. has 1,779. so what do you do with a commodity in terms of tariff lines? for example, the mummy that comes from egypt for an exhibition, where do we put it? we classified it as dried fish! so the audy report swept all these issues under the rug and saw very clearly that the united states had returned to mccarthyism of customs with the hunt for security or insecurity. so, the customs pacifism of john paul ii, with the famous homily of 1978 - "open the borders of the states, the economic systems, non avere paura, do not be afraid" - all this is over, we are afraid, hence the doha cycle which is not concluded ten years after its opening, while the uruguay round cycle had only required eight years, if i dare say so. what's the problem? the problem is that customs duties are 2,000 years old and they go back to rome, to the customs duties of rome, whereas we are in the 21st century. and in the 21st century, commissioner, we need to invent a new customs technology, and this new technology has been invented by scientists. these are deductible customs duties, customs duties that are modulable according to the differentials of production costs, that are refundable, that are tradable on a customs duty stock market, and that are modifiable to help developing countries. that is what you have to put on the wto negotiating table, commissioner, the new customs technology, to get out of the customs archaism.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as you know, the fishing industry is currently facing a serious crisis, not only because of the increase in the price of diesel, for which we must propose a durable, global outlook and not just temporary measures, but also because of the poor management of fisheries resources, the overcapacity of the european fishing fleets and the increasing arrival on the european market of products from illegal fishing. this highly lucrative illegal fishing accelerates the degradation of fisheries resources and marine ecosystems and destabilises the entire sector, which is subject to unfair competition. the european commission's proposal and this report are therefore an essential element in implementing sustainable, responsible fishing that enables european fishermen to make a living from their trade. the report was voted unanimously in the committee on economic and monetary affairs. we must send a strong signal to the council and to the member states most concerned that they must now assume their full responsibility and take the necessary, rapid and effective measures, and i am counting on your determination.

in writing. i voted in favour of the joint report by my finnish colleagues kyösti virrankoski and ville itälä on the third draft amending budget for 2008 of the european union. this mainly involves budgeting the revenue from the microsoft case (fine and bank interest totalling eur 849.200.000), savings from the lower than expected increase in civil servants' salaries and pensions in 2007, the strengthening of the veterinary emergency fund due to the bluetongue crisis (to eur 130 million in commitment appropriations and eur 63.950.000 in payment appropriations), the creation of the necessary budget structure for four joint technology initiatives: the innovative medicines initiative (imi), clean sky, artemis (embedded information systems) and eniac (european nanoelectronics research technology platform), for eur 257.5 million in commitment appropriations and eur 194.6 million in payment appropriations from the seventh framework programme; the eu solidarity fund has provided €98 million for forest fires in greece and floods in slovenia.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my finnish colleague kyösti virrankoski on the fourth draft amending budget for 2008 of the european union. in fact, the only thing that is at issue is the surplus for the 2007 financial year, namely eur 1 528 832 290, to be entered in the 2008 budget. for 2007, the difference between revenue realised (eur 117.4 billion) and expenditure realised (eur 112.9 billion) shows a surplus of eur 4.5 billion, of which payment appropriations carried over to 2008 must be deducted; the total amount of the loan was eur 3.1 billion. to this surplus of 1.4 billion, we must add the appropriations carried over from 2006 to 2007 which were cancelled by 0.2 billion and subtract the negative balance of monetary exchanges of 0.1 billion to have a surplus of 1.5 billion euros in 2007. this surplus is mainly due to under-spending of just under €1.6 billion. i regret that the allocation of this surplus, rather than being automatically returned to the member states, has not been the subject of political discussion to be allocated, for example, to the financing of investment such as the trans-european transport networks. i still remember the difficulties we had in finding some €3.5 billion to finance the excellent galileo project.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my french colleague marie-hélène aubert, which proposes to amend, following the consultation procedure, the proposal for a council regulation establishing a community system to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing. it is becoming urgent to tackle this issue as illegal fishing is a serious problem all over the world. i fully support this initiative, which, as the rapporteur has pointed out, was proposed by the european parliament in february 2007. i support the clarification that, except, of course, in cases of distress or force majeure, fishing vessels from third countries on the community iuu vessel list should be prohibited from accessing ports of the member states, from benefiting from port services and from carrying out landing, transhipment or processing operations on board in those ports. i am in favour of a catch certificate allowing traceability of the fisheries, provided that it is not too complex.
in writing. the fishermen of france, spain and italy are expressing their legitimate revolt, their right to live from their work, their indignation. the peasants, by the way, say no different. we have known for a year that the price of fuel is economically suffocating our fishermen. this shock is added to the bureaucratic strangulation of our fishermen by quotas, penalties, surveillance, inspections, which transform the freedom of the high seas into a liquid soviet union. in the face of the tragedy of a profession, what is being offered to these men, to these regions, to these villages, to these local economies? i didn't say anything. otherwise, it's a vague, temporary help, like palliative care. worse still, on the day when mediterranean fishermen are in brussels to protest for their right to live, we are discussing here further criminal sanctions against illegal fishing. even the path of vat and excise duty relief is denied to fishermen. the solution is a european fund to compensate fishermen for their debts, so that they do not have to bear the burden of the inequality of public charges caused by import policy and the domination of the distribution giants.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my portuguese colleague, mr duarte freitas, which proposes amendments, following the consultation procedure, to the proposal for a council regulation on the protection of vulnerable marine ecosystems of the high seas against the adverse effects of the use of bottom fishing gears. the draft regulation implements the 2006 united nations recommendations and is aimed at community vessels operating on the high seas in areas not regulated by a regional fisheries organisation, which therefore requires regulation by the flag state. between doing nothing and banning everything, i support the third way advocated by the european union, based on strict regulation of bottom fishing activities by defining the conservation and management measures adopted by the regional fisheries organisations (rfos) and also determining the discipline that flag states must impose on their vessels when they operate in high seas areas not regulated by a rfmo.
in writing. the european parliament has voted to introduce strict principles governing the activities of community vessels using bottom trawls on the high seas in areas not regulated by regional fisheries organisations. in line with the recommendations of the united nations general assembly, which has been at the forefront of this issue, the parliamentarians are putting an end to the legal vacuum that has made possible the irreversible destruction of our marine ecosystems. i am glad that the members of the european parliament have recognised the importance of deep-sea ecosystems as a major source of marine biodiversity, and that shifting fishing effort to these habitats could lead to the destruction of our heritage. the ecological awareness of the european parliamentarians is not intended to hinder the already difficult work of our fishermen, nor to increase bureaucratic pressure. from now on, fishing activities in these specific areas will be subject to a licence, subject to a prior assessment by the member state, ensuring that the fishing will not have any noticeable adverse effects. the precautionary principle is also applied here. the preservation of marine biodiversity will only be guaranteed if it is vertically integrated into other community policies, in particular the future maritime policy of the european union.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr audy's report calls for the harmonisation of import and export procedures to ensure the proper application of the european union's trade policy, and above all for consistent application at all eu entry points in order to make life easier for businesses. this might seem logical, since we have been in a customs union for over 40 years. but mr audy wants this harmonization of procedures to be complete and entrusted to a single european customs service. it is true that customs are responsible for checking the movement of goods and their compliance with standards (product safety, consumer protection, health, environment, etc.). they also have a fiscal function: the application of the appropriate customs duties, of course, but also that of vat, which remains, if you like, a national tax. finally, and perhaps above all, they contribute to security and are involved in the fight against all kinds of trafficking, the most important of which is drug trafficking, in close cooperation with the police. it is not surprising that the rapporteur favours the first function, in the name of the virtues of international trade, and underestimates the other two. that is why we are voting against this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my german colleague, reimer böge, which proposes to approve as is the commission's proposal to mobilise the european union solidarity fund to provide assistance to slovenia and greece, respectively, affected by floods and forest fires in 2007, for a total amount of approximately eur 98 million, which is to be the subject of an amending budget adopted in parallel. in order to avoid any delay in the provision of financial assistance in the event of disaster, i support the recommendation in the report to ask the commission to propose amending budgets with the sole purpose of mobilising this fund, the use of which must not exceed eur 1 billion annually under the current interinstitutional agreement.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my german colleague helmuth markov, which was voted unanimously in the committee on international trade and which proposes to amend, in accordance with the consultation procedure, the proposal for a council regulation applying a scheme of generalised tariff preferences for the period from 1 january 2009 to 31 december 2011 and amending various regulations. this proposal for a regulation follows the 2004 guidelines on the role of the gsp for the decade 2006 to 2015 which introduced several new objectives such as, for example, targeting preferences on countries that need them most, extending gsp coverage to products of interest to developing countries, increasing the transparency and stability of the graduation mechanism and introducing a new special incentive scheme to promote sustainable development and good governance. i fully support the report in that it calls for the european parliament to be more involved in this gsp policy which is important for the countries that need it and which costs us 3.5 billion in lost customs duties every year.

in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my distinguished polish colleague, mr jacek saryuz-wolski, on the common foreign and security policy (cfsp) and the european security and defence policy (esdp), which have helped to strengthen european identity and the role of the european union in the world. i share the view that the cfsp must gain more democratic legitimacy by allowing parliament to exercise real control over this policy, also speaking with one voice and demanding various priorities: the causes of the current insecurity in europe (terrorism, organised crime), energy security, the fight against climate change and sustainable development, improving stability in neighbouring regions, crisis management and conflict prevention/resolution, non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, migration management, the promotion of human rights and civil liberties worldwide. the first geographical priority must be stability in the western balkans and the strengthening of the dialogue with serbia and kosovo. i support the idea that the european parliament should make specific proposals for the financing and budgetary control of the future european external action service (eeas).
in writing. the two reports, one on common foreign policy and the other on security and defence policy, which are to be voted on today, have one thing in common: the dispossession of the member states of their foreign and defence policies to the benefit of officials in brussels. diplomacy will be in the hands of a high representative, a real foreign minister. and because it is common, defence will become unique, under the high patronage, this time, of the united states, via nato and the un, as clearly stated in the constitution bis of europe, the treaty of lisbon. our military resources are reduced to their simplest expression, since the bulk of the budgets are now spent by france and the united kingdom and are subject to the stability pact. the french and british permanent seats on the un security council will be combined into one, with a european plenipotentiary... in short, no member state will have the political and military means to ensure its independence and freedom on its own. but it is true that they have already largely abdicated them in favour of the eurocrats. we are resolutely opposed to this disastrous development.
in writing. i voted for the joint resolution tabled by five political groups on the union for the mediterranean. the mediterranean region and the middle east are of strategic importance to the union and a mediterranean policy based on solidarity, dialogue, cooperation and exchanges is necessary to address common challenges and achieve the objective of creating an area of peace, stability and shared prosperity. i welcome the initiative of the president of the french republic, nicolas sarkozy, to whom this union for the mediterranean is very dear, and i wish him every success at the inaugural summit scheduled for paris on 13 july. i support the political proposal to give this future union a parliamentary dimension by building on the euro-mediterranean parliamentary assembly. i welcome the examples of initiatives proposed such as the motorways of the sea, the interconnection of the arab maghreb motorway (ama), the decontamination of the mediterranean, civil protection and the mediterranean solar plan, the production of high-powered solar thermal electricity in the north african desert, the desalination of seawater to facilitate access to drinking water, etc.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the joint resolution on the 'barcelona process: union for the mediterranean'. this resolution rightly recalls the strategic interest of the mediterranean region and the middle east for the european union. our policy towards these countries must be based on the principles of solidarity, dialogue and cooperation. the barcelona process now needs to be relaunched to maximise its effectiveness. the commission's initiative is therefore a step in the right direction and has the merit of focusing on specific regional projects whose implementation will make it possible to respond effectively to the needs of the citizens of this region. the commission proposal also provides for the establishment of a co-chairmanship of the barcelona process, a joint standing committee and a secretariat, which will improve cooperation and dialogue between the various partners. it also recalled that the main objectives of this policy must remain the promotion of the rule of law, democracy, respect for rights and political pluralism.

in writing. in view of the difficulty of replacing the generations of european farmers, the european parliament wanted to consider ways of encouraging young farmers to set up their businesses, which should guide the cap's health check. as co-rapporteur of the pse group, i made the following proposals:- this is a priority to meet the food, energy, environmental and territorial challenges, - new farmers must benefit from support measures, especially those who do not inherit the holding and those who move to areas with permanent natural handicaps: higher set-up aid, reduced rates for agricultural loans and accompanying measures after set-up - these support measures must be mandatory under the 2nd pillar of the cap and the issue of access to land must be studied - living conditions in rural areas must be improved: equal access to public services, public services, social living spaces ... - we must develop vocational training (during access to employment and vocational training) and promote farmers' knowledge by respecting the standards of the european level and by promoting the quality of life of farmers.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report, which highlights the fundamental challenge for the european union of renewing generations of farmers. young farmers are best placed to meet the new agricultural challenges. with the experience of their elders, they have the dynamism and enthusiasm to make the necessary environmental, technological and economic changes that will enable european agriculture of tomorrow to maintain its central place in the world. the aim is to reconcile an ever-increasing level of agricultural production with a constant concern for the quality and safety of products, all in the context of a comprehensive approach to the conservation of natural resources and environments. but these requirements require ever greater financial and personal investment from young farmers. the acquisition by the latter of the appropriate material and intellectual tools must therefore, as this report calls for, be given increased support by the union, particularly in terms of access to technological innovations. the cap cannot afford to neglect those who will ensure the community's food sovereignty in a sustainable way that respects people and the environment.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as the rapporteur rightly points out, 'for a market to exist, there must be supply and demand'. this does not seem to be the case for a cross-border market in retail financial services. the report is based on the assumption that allowing supply will necessarily encourage demand. however much we may wish to have cheaper loans or more profitable investments, it is not tomorrow that an italian will go to a danish or cypriot bank to borrow money to buy his house or his car. and everyone can see why: problems of language, of correct apprehension of risks, uncertainties about the tax system, etc. the rapporteur is not mistaken when he talks about the importance of trust, proximity and personal relationships for consumers. this desire to create such a market artificially is hard to conceal one of the main aims of the manoeuvre: to force the states to harmonize tax and regulatory measures to deal with any eventuality or to impose a supranational legal order. with the added bonus of the adoption of the euro by the countries that have refused it, in order to be able to participate fully in this hypothetical market. we cannot ratify these proposals.

the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the report we are presenting today at second reading is the result of the work of a team which has been able to reach an agreement with the slovenian presidency and the european commission. it has been a real pleasure for me to work with my fellow rapporteurs from the political groups to find a compromise. it is a good thing to have competent and experienced colleagues who are listening and present at negotiating meetings. i would like to express my sincere thanks to you, ladies and gentlemen, and also to the secretariat of the committee on the environment, the advisers of the political groups and my assistant, sylvain maréchal. i am talking about teamwork because we have had excellent cooperation with the representatives of the slovenian presidency, who have taken parliament's recommendations into account, and with the representatives of the european commission, who have provided feedback to help us better understand this draft directive. i believe that everyone will be able to see the fruit of their collaboration in the compromise amendments which will be put to the vote tomorrow. so thank you all for making my work as rapporteur on this technical matter so much easier. i'm coming to the bottom. the water framework directive sets out a strategy to combat chemical pollution of water. the purpose of this proposal for a daughter directive is to ensure a high level of protection against the risks posed by certain substances in the aquatic environment by establishing environmental quality standards. let me highlight the main advances in this compromise text. we have included two major principles: the polluter pays principle and the principle of first fixing the source. the most significant elements are concrete elements. these transitional overrun areas - now known as mixing areas - are no longer a means of detecting a problem but a tool for highlighting it and it is therefore up to the member states to describe the corrective actions. the aim of the directive was to harmonise standards at community level. it was therefore obvious that the commission should draw up guidelines to help harmonize inventories, emissions and discharges and mixing areas. we got it. we have also succeeded in ensuring that the situation of bodies of water which cross borders between member states, but also from third countries, is better taken into account. as regards the additional substances, parliament wanted to add a substantial number of them. on the basis of a preliminary screening, the commission selected 13 substances considered to be of concern. the compromise clearly states that the commission will have 24 months to decide on the final classification and propose relevant limit values on the basis of scientific data. this is a significant progress, since these substances include pcbs, free cyanides, edta, dioxins and biphenols. on the sensitive issue of sediments and biota, in the absence of scientific consensus, the compromise states that member states will have to monitor these to provide an analysis of the long-term trend of substances accumulating there. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu, including the member states, and to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the member states. in view of these developments, i would ask you, ladies and gentlemen, to support this compromise package.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, thank you for your contribution to this debate. what are the aims of this directive? the aim, of course, is to improve the quality of surface water. we do not want to find lead, cadmium, nickel, mercury, solvents, these highly toxic and carcinogenic substances, including pcbs, in water. my colleague, mrs lienemann, was referring to a report from a fortnight ago which showed that pcbs were bio-accumulated in fish and that man then ate these fish. we cannot accept that any longer and i believe that the european citizens are perhaps also expecting europe to give this strong signal for the protection of our environment, for the protection of our health. i believe that it is by respecting this framework law on water, with its daughter directives, that we can also convey this message from europe. some colleagues have said that there may not have been enough substance, that parliament had moved backwards from the first reading. at first reading we had proposed a total of 33 + 28 substances, i.e. 61 substances analysed. the second reading gives us 33 + 13, or 46, but it must be remembered that these are dangerous substances of particular concern, which should no longer be present in river waters today. the other interest of this directive is that it makes it possible to check that european legislation is being properly respected - i am thinking of the application of the reach regulation, i am thinking of the ippc. we have an instrument here to verify that. commissioner, you have heard my colleagues, if the council and parliament approve this text, the ball is in your court. you have a lot of work to do, you have a lot of analysis to do, you have these inventories to list. have a good one! in any case, we will be there to follow up on this legislation.

on behalf of the pse group. mr president, we are discussing today one aspect of the establishment of a european immigration policy and we can already make a statement: we are building a europe that is closed in on itself, whereas, in order to try to combat illegal immigration, we should put in place tools that allow the legal arrival of migrants. my group does not accept the compromise that has been worked out between the presidency and the rapporteur, not because we are opposed to any european return policy, but because we think that the result is very inadequate in terms of the protection of fundamental rights. we have always said that we are in favour of a return directive because we have seen too much horror when we have visited the detention camps. but we do not want a directive at any cost. i have heard that this directive is a way of bringing people out of hiding. this is a serious error of assessment because this directive merely sets out rules on the organisation of returns and does not in any way allow for the granting of residence rights. the rapporteur considers this compromise to be balanced, since it confers a number of rights. however, the rights conferred by the text, such as access to education for minors or access to legal aid, are not really mandatory. the directive will not improve detention in the european union. for example, an increase in the length of detention to 18 months appears to be an improvement in nine out of 27 countries. however, three of the nine member states will not be affected - the united kingdom, ireland and denmark - as they are not party to the directive. there will be very little improvement in countries like malta, where the majority of people in detention are asylum seekers, who are excluded from the directive. in greece, the main persons detained are those who are intercepted while illegally crossing an external border. and those people are also excluded from the scope. the socialist group has therefore tabled a limited number of amendments to establish the human aspect of this text. this is the first co-decision of the european parliament in the field of combating illegal immigration and that is why we have a duty as members of parliament to defend clear legislation which is not subject to different interpretations by the member states or arbitration by the court of justice. and that is why i call on the european parliament to use all the legislative powers it has to enable legislation to be passed that improves the lot of those detained. it is our duty as parliamentarians! this does not exempt us from reflecting on a larger and more philosophical question: does the earth belong to all humans? is there really a share of these humans that should be assigned to residence in poverty? don't you think that's the real question?

in writing. it is shocking that a dangerous criminal can hide behind the lack of information on his criminal record in order to escape the rigors of justice or to carry out his crimes in other member states. the case of fourniret is a sad and painful example of this. in these circumstances, allowing the compilation of complete criminal records, containing convictions in different states and easily available, appears to be a welcome improvement. but this laudable initiative does not only target the pedophile monsters, the murderers, the robbers... it also targets, by the introduction of the simple words "defections following a criminal conviction", the international prosecution of crimes of opinion. and we know well, in this mad europe, open to all the winds of uncontrolled immigration, in perpetual remorse for what it was, what it is and what it could be, who is its target: the patriots attached to their identity, proud of their people, their nation and their history, and who dare to proclaim loud and clear their will to defend them. we shall therefore abstain because we fear that this text will allow, beyond the legitimate suppression of crimes, the extension to the whole union of the freedom-threatening laws which are so damaging to the democratic life of our countries.
in writing. according to oecd figures, we will produce 45% more waste by 2020 than in 1995. it is therefore urgent that the european union develops a new waste management strategy which allows each waste to be considered not only as a source of pollution to be reduced but also as a potential resource to be exploited. the compromise adopted in plenary today will focus on prevention and recycling with a target of stabilising the volume of waste produced by 2012 and recycling targets of 50% of household waste and 70% of construction and demolition waste by 2020 , impose separate collection by 2015 for at least paper, metal, plastic and glass, strengthen the regulation for hazardous waste by imposing separate collection and reliable traceability, separate collection of waste oils also to be provided, and differentiate incineration operations for the final disposal of waste from those that generate energy recovery. thus, under an energy efficiency formula, only the most energy efficient municipal solid waste incinerators will be classified as recovery facilities.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which sets environmental quality standards for priority substances and certain other pollutants, with the aim of ensuring a high level of protection of the aquatic environment. 33 pollutants (mainly pesticides and heavy metals) that can be found in rivers, lakes and coastal waters will be subject to environmental quality standards. these substances can threaten the survival of ecosystems but also - through the food chain - human health. the compromise that has just been voted will thus allow member states to 'make progress' towards meeting these standards by 2018. the decision to classify new substances as 'priority' or 'dangerous' should be taken by the commission as soon as possible. in the vicinity of sources of pollution, it will not be possible to meet environmental quality standards quickly. in these 'mixing zones' concentrations of pollutants could exceed the limits set. we must have the necessary guarantees that the member states use the best available techniques for water treatment when they determine 'mixing zones'.
in writing. in the light of the recent maritime disasters of the erika and the prestige, it is clear that the human factor is a very serious aspect of maritime safety. the proper training of the crews is therefore essential. i would like to raise two fundamental points in this connection. the first concerns the very logic of europe's wish: the refusal to promote in any way the employment of seamen from member states. on the contrary, far from being a community preference, the aim is, as in all economic and social fields, to encourage the recruitment of non-community seamen. this deliberately anti-national approach will only increase the current shortage of qualified seafarers in the union and the lack of interest in this difficult and dangerous profession. all this for the benefit of an under-skilled, cheap labour force from asian countries. secondly, it is a question of ensuring the highest possible guarantees as regards the quality of training, its control and the granting of licences. instead of mutual recognition of diplomas based on lower technical standards outside the community, let us preserve and restore the true value of our diplomas and save our jobs at sea in the name of maritime safety and the protection of our national jobs.

president of the commission. − madam president, the european council starting tomorrow has a heavy agenda covering many issues where citizens expect europe to act. (some members on the right, who were wearing green t-shirts, stood up to display banners and posters calling for respect for the ‘no’ vote in ireland. the president asked them to remove the banners and posters.) the issues are the surge in oil and food prices, climate change and energy security, migration and asylum to name but a few. but of course foremost in everybody’s mind will be the ‘no’ vote in ireland. this ‘no’ vote was a disappointment to all those in favour of a stronger, more efficient and accountable european union. the lisbon treaty remains essential to help us respond to the challenges that europe faces today; to have a more democratic union, increasing the powers of this parliament and recognising the role of national parliaments in european politics; to enhance europe’s capacity to act in areas like migration, energy, climate change, internal security; to increase europe’s coherence and effectiveness on the global stage. these challenges have not gone away. the truth is that the ‘no’ vote did not solve the problems which the treaty seeks to tackle. for the last six years we have spent a lot of energy on institutional issues. with so many key issues pressing for action today we cannot afford this energy to go to waste, and the world does not stop and wait for europe. as i said last week, the commission fully respects the outcome of the irish referendum. we must show the same respect for all national ratifications, (applause)whether they have chosen to take the route of referendum or of parliamentary ratification. there have been 19 democratic decisions in the process so far: 18 in favour of the lisbon treaty; one against. eight other member states still have to take position. the irish government has set out clearly its respect for the right of other countries to continue their ratification processes. this is, i believe, self-evident. all the countries in europe are equal; all the countries have the right to express their opinion. (applause)while it is clear that the lisbon treaty cannot enter into force before unanimity about its ratification, it is also clear that an irish vote decides on the irish position but cannot determine the position of other countries. i expect the member states that did not ratify the lisbon treaty to continue their own ratification processes. (applause) the european council gives us all an opportunity to listen very carefully to what prime minister cowen will say. then we must work very closely with the irish government to help solve this problem. let me be clear: ireland has a responsibility to contribute to finding a solution. when governments sign the treaty they assume a responsibility to have it ratified. but let me be equally clear: this is a time for us to be serious about solidarity. twenty-seven member states signed the treaty; we must make every effort to make sure that 27 member states find a way forward. member states are equal in their dignity and we should be clear about that. this will take time and effort for the irish, but also for all of us. i do not think that we can rush into a premature decision about the next step. we need to take the time to find a real consensus and see what is possible for ireland. but equally we should not take too long. i know that this parliament is keen to give voters clarity on the way forward by the time of the european elections. the european commission is ready to make its contribution – and i am sure this parliament is too – but there is no way around the fact that governments have a particular responsibility here: in signing the treaty, in making sure it is ratified, in promoting the european project in their national public opinions. and on this last point let me make a general comment that i think may be useful for the debate that is going on now. years of treating the european institutions as a convenient scapegoat leaves fertile ground for populist campaigns. (applause)as i have said several times before, you cannot bash brussels or strasbourg from monday to saturday and expect citizens to vote in favour of europe on sunday. progress in the past couple of years and it has been on the back of a determined effort to deliver policies in the interests of european citizens. at a time when rising food and oil prices are leading to great expectations for action, we cannot afford to abandon this path. that is why i very much welcome prime minister janez janša and the slovenian presidency’s decision to ring-fence the debate on lisbon to the dinner on thursday night and to devote the rest of the european council to furthering our policy agenda. today, everyone is feeling the pressure of price rises in food and fuel but for some there is an extra burden. for poorer households these costs are a bigger share of the household budget so the rises hit even harder. the same is true for some economic activities, with fuel so critical for some industries. in two communications on food and oil prices the commission has made a careful analysis of the causes of the price rises, of where the squeeze is most intense and of what we can and should do. the european union needs to show that it is bringing to bear the full range of measures available at european and national level. we need to take a dynamic and imaginative look at the tools at our disposal – to look at what will have a real impact in the short, medium and long term. let us remember previous oil shocks where europe failed to learn the long-term lessons. let in writing. i am pleased that mr weber's report on the return directive was adopted by a large majority. this vote is a clear demonstration that the european parliament has not succumbed to the demagogic and populist campaign against this draft directive, preferring the path of responsibility and pragmatism. the european parliament has shown its maturity and conscience by adopting a text which will undoubtedly raise the level of protection of the nationals concerned in the member states where it is at its lowest or even zero. this vote has the double merit of not calling into question existing national systems which already offer sufficient guarantees - this is the case, for example, of france - and of bringing the member states with the most restrictive and least protective systems down to a more humane level. this text, which does not concern asylum seekers, is only a starting point towards the framing and minimum harmonisation of immigration rules. it should not be seen in isolation but as part of the overall eu policy to promote the legal immigration we need.

in writing. the text adopted today is a complete reversal of the work done in the libé committee, which had made it possible to significantly improve the european commission's proposal. this so-called compromise does not bring any change that would raise the level of protection for these people in the states that practice the most unacceptable policies. firstly, because of its limited scope: asylum seekers and persons intercepted at borders are excluded, although they represent a significant proportion of illegal immigrants. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rights of the child are respected. the latter could thus be extended to 18 months, as against the six months proposed by the pse. i am ashamed that our assembly has overwhelmingly supported the possibility of imprisoning for so long people whose only crime is to have sought better living conditions in our territories and who are often in a very vulnerable state. i myself voted against this text in good conscience. if common minimum rules are necessary, they must be established in the context of a responsible and humane approach to illegal immigration and in no case at the expense of forgetting our own fundamental rights and values.
in writing. the highly publicized 'return' directive, proposed by the brussels commission and falsely and wrongly stigmatized by the left and the far left as a directive of shame and anti-human rights, has just been voted to their great dismay by the european parliament. however, this directive, which is supposed to organise the return of illegal immigrants, is not repressive in any way. it does not criminalise immigrants who have entered europe illegally. better still, it gives them the choice between legalization or voluntary return, all of which come with rights and guarantees linked to the indispensable human rights. what about the right of peoples to protect themselves and not be overwhelmed by a global immigration? i didn't say anything. the fortress europe so much maligned in all the media in france and elsewhere does not exist. it is a fantasy to better pass legislation that is favorable to immigration and immigrants under the guise of repression. this directive is not good. it's like powder in the eyes. it has the merit of being a first step towards a less immigration-friendly policy. it should not make us forget that others are in preparation, such as the one concerning the 'european blue card' guaranteeing legal immigration for work, and that these have the avowed purpose of encouraging ever more immigration into europe.
in writing. today, the european parliament adopted the draft 'return' directive by a majority. the draft directive, which aims to establish common minimum standards for the treatment of illegal immigrants, was originally intended to respond to the often dramatic situation in the some 224 detention camps scattered across europe. this is a sensible move, since in some countries there are no rules or limits on the detention of irregular migrants. the socialists had made substantial progress in the vote in committee on the introduction of essential human rights guarantees, which were absent from the original proposal. they have been eliminated by the council and the epp rapporteur, who prefer the repressive approach in the hope of discouraging people who are already desperate. the result is a directive which endorses the criminalisation of migrants, their cramming into appalling conditions for endless periods and the separation of minors from their families, while the so-called guarantees of legal aid or recourse will in fact be applied voluntarily by the member states. it is simply unacceptable, contrary to the values which europe is proud to embody, and that is why i have decided to vote against this text.
in writing. this third energy package dogmatically persists in the path of total separation between production activities and energy distribution networks. it aims to subject the entire energy sector to the sole laws of the market and competition between all. the same causes produce the same effects, and it will lead the union to a catastrophe of a magnitude greater than that experienced by california in the year 2000. this policy is bad for users, for employees in the sector, for smes/smis, for employment, for safety and for the environment. the market and the private sector are unable to meet the energy needs of the european people, the challenges of global warming and post-fossil energy. their objectives are to maximize shareholder returns, not to serve the public interest. we need a real energy europe, but it can only be built on the basis of cooperation. the energy sector must be driven by the coordinated public action of the member states and not by that of the financial markets. the union must act to ensure that energy is recognised as a global public good and not just another commodity.
in writing. i voted against this report which, as a common rule for the internal electricity market, proposes the dismantling of the legacy of the european incumbents. the separation of electricity generation and distribution activities will not, in my view, provide any additional guarantee in terms of efficiency, safety or accessibility of the network, especially in the current context of strong growth in overall electricity demand and high uncertainty about resources. the latter requires ever more structural investment to secure our supply and stimulate research and innovation, a prospect which seems largely incompatible with the logic of strong competition and short-term profitability which underlies the choice of full liberalisation of the sector. the third option, supported by the french socialists but unfortunately not adopted, appeared to be a much more reasonable solution since it would preserve the financial integrity of the major european energy groups while entrusting the organization of electricity distribution to independent regulators. i welcome, however, the progress made in this report in terms of consumer protection, and in particular the introduction of the principles of combating energy poverty and of transparency and accessibility of information for the end user.
in writing. clearly, the real objective of this third energy package is not security of supply, quality of service, affordability or the real choice of supplier by consumers, but the final dismantling of what remains of the old public monopolies in electricity. the commission and many members of parliament's insistence on imposing 'separation of assets', i.e. the forced surrender of ownership of their network to 'historic' operators such as edf, is unacceptable. the accusations against them - restricting access to the network for their competitors, deliberately limiting investment in infrastructure - are completely unproven. it is also not clear how entrusting the management of the network to a single operator other than the electricity supplier can guarantee the relevance and adequacy of investments, the non-abuse of a crucial position or the best congestion management. that is why, although we have always defended here the exclusive prerogatives of the states in the field of energy, a strategic area of too great importance to be left to the eurocrats, we will support as a lesser evil the solution of 'effective separation' proposed by france and germany, among others. and we will vote against texts whose philosophy we fundamentally disapprove of.
