the agenda calls for the debate on:- oral question to the council on the crisis in the fisheries sector due to the increase in the price of philippe morillon diesel fuel, on behalf of the committee on fisheries (o-0063/2008 b6-0162/2008), and - oral question to the commission on the crisis in the fisheries sector due to the increase in the price of philippe morillon diesel fuel, on behalf of the committee on fisheries (o-0064/2008 b6-0163/2008).
author. - madam president, i am giving commissioner borg time to settle in. this oral question was initiated at the unanimous request of the groups in the committee which i have the honour to chair, and i am glad that it comes after this very rich debate which dealt with general questions. my father was born, madam president, commissioner, president-in-office, more than a century ago in a village near saint-malo, which i knew in my youth as a place teeming with life, fuelled mainly by agriculture and fishing. today, the village is dying of cancer, caused by the proliferation of dead cells in the secondary residences and the gradual disappearance of all activities that allowed it to live except during the six weeks of summer. this is not an isolated phenomenon, it is a phenomenon found practically on the whole of the european coast, which has led commissioner borg, to whom i pay tribute, to propose the implementation of this integrated coastal management, which should allow a restoration, a preservation, a resurrection of life on all our european coasts. although this decision has led to the transformation of the directorate-general for fisheries into a directorate-general for 'mare', it does not mean that the european union is determined to see the resources that our fishermen must continue to derive from the exploitation of the oceans disappear. why does the european union only implement two common policies, the common agricultural policy and the common fisheries policy? the answer to this question is simple: to enable our continent to continue to obtain its food supply from the exploitation of both the land and the coast. so this is where the impact of the huge increase in oil prices has consequences that could be catastrophic, particularly, of course, in the fisheries sector. the profession, already severely affected by the shrinking resources, is now threatened with extinction and this explains, without excusing them, the violent manifestations of despair to which some of its representatives have succumbed and continue to do so here and there. that is why i am pleased, commissioner, that your executive committee has just proposed a number of measures to provide immediate relief for the industries most at risk, in particular by allowing member states to derogate exceptionally and temporarily from the rules imposed for the implementation of the european fisheries fund in accordance with the arrangements which will be discussed, mr president-in-office of the council, in luxembourg on 24 june at the next meeting of the agriculture and fisheries ministers. let us not lose sight of the need for the european union - and for the planet - to be able to continue to draw from the oceans the resources needed to provide food. there is no point in preserving the survival of fish if there are no more fishermen to go and get them. this is a fact which, in my view, justifies the detailed proposals which concern not only the short term but the medium and long term, on which we are working together, commissioner, in the committee on fisheries and which will be further developed by all my colleagues and by the draft resolution which will be put to the vote tomorrow.
for the greens/efa group mr president, commissioner, as you have said, this structural crisis is deep and lasting. it is therefore a question of finding sustainable solutions, not just for the fisheries sector, but for all the sectors concerned. it must also be said that this crisis is the result of years of blindness to the dependence of fisheries on oil - and cheap oil - and to the forward flight towards what has been called the arms race, with ships that are more and more powerful, that go further and further and can bring back more and more fish. these are the questions we must also deal with. the problem of expensive diesel is inseparable from all the other issues affecting the fisheries sector - fisheries resource management, price formation, world trade, the fight against illegal fishing - and it is difficult to deal with this issue in isolation from the rest. the subsidies and aid proposed by the commission, which i believe are in the right direction, are acceptable, especially for our fellow citizens, only if they are conditional on a fundamental reorientation of fisheries policies and practices. we regret that the compromise resolution does not make possible aid and subsidies conditional on this reorientation and on the need to put an end to fleet overcapacity and to move towards better management of fisheries resources and the protection of marine ecosystems. it is the very condition for the economic and social viability of fisheries undertakings. finally, we want the member states to take full responsibility and to stop making demagoguery by promising money they do not have, without offering sustainable prospects for fisheries.
mr president, from all the fishing ports in the union, two demands are strongly expressed: diesel at a unified price at union level of 40 cents a litre and concerted management of quotas. these just demands are vital for small-scale fishing and its jobs. the rising oil price and the preservation of fisheries resources are real problems. the free market has proved incapable of dealing with the consequences of the rise in oil prices. oil companies, eager to make profits, respond by speculating on the growing demand for oil from emerging countries, hoping to break the bank. by reducing taxes which are only increasing and by taxing the enormous profits of the oil companies, we can easily meet the demands of fishermen without paying out subsidies, which are particularly random. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fishermen are not treated as criminals by a commission which covers the real criminals of the sea, the flags of convenience and the industrial fishing trusts. no one is more committed to the preservation of fisheries resources than they are. the system must be completely reformed, with the commission working democratically with the fisheries professionals rather than imposing its dictatorship through the governance of its pseudo-experts.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, relations with russia, as mr wojciechowski, the previous speaker, said, are extremely delicate and ambiguous. i understand the attitude, particularly of our colleagues in central and eastern europe and the baltic states, who have suffered greatly from russian domination through soviet domination, through a ruthless system of oppression of the peoples which has now fortunately disappeared and regressed. i believe that we must take this opportunity to establish more friendly relations with the great russian people, who are unquestionably a european people and who are today somewhat of a sentinel, because russia is facing the same problems as we are. it is facing problems of birthlessness, and the vast space that siberia represents could be very attractive to the 1.5 billion chinese who consider that part of this territory has been taken from them. i think that the misunderstandings which may exist and which may persist with russia and which we hope will be resolved at the summit on 14 november are also partly our responsibility. we have joined the american political cart, we have reintegrated - i speak for france - into the north atlantic treaty organization, nato, which was a response to the warsaw pact. the fact that the warsaw pact has disappeared, i think, can also legitimately arouse russia's suspicion of us and i would like to see these misunderstandings resolved bilaterally.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i also welcome your presence here this evening. it is a kind of baptism of fire for you and i particularly appreciate, as a frenchman, that on monday evening and again tonight you spoke french with talent. it's a real pleasure. i should also like to thank mr liberadzki for the discussions he has had in the committee on transport and tourism on the proposal for a directive on the transport of dangerous goods. as i have just said, parliament already voted on this draft directive in september 2007 and i am pleased that an agreement has been reached with the council and the commission and i consider that the debate on this text tonight is, in a way, a mere formality. but i would like to take this opportunity, since we are in a sense among ourselves, to stress that this text represents in my view an important step towards better regulation of the conditions for the transport of dangerous goods within our borders and that the question of the transport of goods, and in particular dangerous goods, is an important problem for our citizens and in relation to sustainable development. the current volume of dangerous goods transported in the union is 10% of all transported goods, which is very high. that's 110 billion tons per kilometer per year, 58 percent of it by road, which is huge, 25 percent by rail and 17 percent by inland waterways. this directive, which aims to modernise existing provisions, also has the merit, perhaps more importantly in these difficult times, of merging four directives into one legislative act. this is an obvious step towards greater transparency and it is very important that all europeans can read our decisions. finally, i am also pleased that the shipyard sector has been integrated into the directive. the transport by water must be given more consideration, since it is an environmentally friendly mode of transport and can also be one of the answers to our constant desire to rebalance transport modes in europe. here too, this merger into a single legislative act will make the rules applicable more readable and more transparent in the current context in which we want greater intermodality in transport. i welcome this progress, particularly for those involved in the transport sector, at a time when the work of europe is not always sufficiently explained and when, unfortunately, it is sometimes misunderstood by our fellow citizens.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to thank our rapporteur for the discussions he has had for more than two years in the committee on transport and tourism in preparing this text to improve safety on europe's main roads. this is a major and almost constant concern of our parliament, which is often called upon to give its opinion on all these technical problems of vehicle safety standards, and once again, finally tonight, we can emphasize that this is a very concrete answer for our fellow europeans. these safety problems concern them and can speak to them in their daily lives and, indeed, if this legislative proposal aims to reduce the risk of accidents and to reduce the number of deaths and injuries by ensuring integrated safety in all phases of planning, design and operation of road infrastructure on the transeuropean transport network, then it must be considered with interest. i will support this initiative because, without imposing too strict procedures which would not take account of the economic and structural reality of each member state, this proposal for a directive provides clarity by organising a procedure for the assessment of any new construction, an audit procedure to allow the evolution of existing equipment, but also a risk management procedure to provide specific responses to targeted risks. i am not as optimistic as commissioner tajani, but i hope that the european commission's estimates of the effects of these measures will be in line with reality. if it is estimated that the introduction of these measures will reduce the number of injuries and deaths in the union by almost 7 000, i think that is a very good thing.
on behalf of the pse group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking the rapporteur, mr aylward, for his excellent work in listening to the sheep and goat sector and the professionals and for the very comprehensive report he has put before us. the sheep and goat sector has been badly affected over the last ten years by successive crises, notably related to animal diseases, but mainly because of the decoupling of aid, which causes a very significant decrease in sheep herds due to the abandonment of farmers' activities. this sector is facing real difficulties and requires special attention from us, because it produces high-quality meat or milk and is also a tool for maintenance and land use planning, in particular to reduce the risk of fire or natural disasters. i support the proposals of our rapporteur and the committee on agriculture and rural development on measures to support production and promote products. it seems to me important, in view of the fact that imports from outside the community already account for almost a quarter of european production, to develop a european logo in addition to the indications of local and national origin. i also believe that electronic identification of the herd will only be possible on the date decided by the european institutions if the european union has previously mobilised the necessary funds, because the profession, in view of the great difficulties it is currently facing, will not be able to do so. the setting up of a monitoring team seems to me very timely, unlike my predecessor, but i believe it should include representatives of the professional organisations in order to take account as closely as possible of developments on the ground. finally, i would remind you that action is urgently needed, and that action must be taken as early as next year if we are to save this sector, because i fear that the use of article 69 - now article 68 - in the context of the health check, for sectors in crisis, will be too late.
mr president, commissioner, we are dealing with a serious subject, the slow disappearance of european sheep and shepherds. the world has one billion sheep, europe has only 97 million, which is less than 10%, and it's worse for sheep, we have only 67 million. it is true that britain can be deluded with 15 million heads, spain with 16 million, or president parish's ireland, self-sufficient at 333%. but france, for example, has seen its herd increase from almost 13 million 25 years ago to 8 million today, and to 5 million in 2015 alone. in france, one out of every two pieces of lamb we eat comes from abroad. worse, it's the nursing sheep that are disappearing. the causes are well known: the explosion in food costs, the decline in consumption, the difficult pastoral life, catarrhal fever, the fall in prices, the decoupling, but first and foremost, the duty-free importation of sheep from new zealand. 227 000 tonnes of sheep arrive from new zealand every year, twice the french production. it's not the wolves that eat the sheep, it's the new zealand sheep that eat the european sheep. a century and a half ago, new zealand had a million sheep. today, it has 40 million. in the same period, france's population has fallen from 30 million to 8 million. so what do you do? we need a major european sheep plan, a will with a premium of 15 euros per suckling ewe, an oat premium of 125% of the bovine premium, credits for the modernisation of buildings, local slaughterhouses, a european livestock risk insurance fund, an assistance plan and, why not, erasmus grants for young shepherds who could go to spain, italy, to learn their trade. i thank you, mr president. sheep is civilization!
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first of all like to congratulate our colleague, mrs zita gurmai, on the successful completion of this report on the 'smart vehicle' initiative. in the concept of the development of society, we know that mobility brings wealth, growth and, consequently, a capacity to assume the solidarity of territories and people. sustainable development requires combining the different modes of transport to achieve better fluidity in our cities and countryside. far from being built around the car as in the past, the motor vehicle remains an essential vehicle for the intelligent and sustainable mobility we wish for. this is achieved through the concept of intelligent and sustainable vehicles, based on a triptych: a safer vehicle, a cleaner vehicle, a smarter vehicle. beyond this declaration of principle, europe must accompany this action in practice by means of directives and policies which, in the long run, will integrate all electronic systems, whether nomadic or not, allowing process control and vehicle controls in compliance with greater safety, greater cleanliness in terms of reducing co2 and particulate emissions. in this spirit, commissioner, we must encourage car manufacturers to think about integrating all these electronic devices into the design of new vehicles, not only for greater efficiency and driving comfort, but also, by this volume, to reduce costs, manufacture and installation. if we want to be part of sustainable mobility, we must also widen the scope of these policies. the research and innovation axes must make it possible to incorporate this research in order to eventually create the intelligent road, enhancing safety, managing energy expenditure, using dialogue between vehicles, and making traffic more fluid. the european union wishes to promote the knowledge society and knowledge and sustainable development. these initiatives must be fully integrated into this framework. i would like to conclude by reiterating the urgent need for real ambition, setting ambitious targets and creating the conditions for growth and progress in europe. in line with the report by our colleague, mr gurmai, the european parliament is convinced that the commission, mr commissioner, will meet these expectations and requirements by setting a new frontier for the european intelligent vehicle and finally providing the financial means for this ambition.
in writing. i welcome the commission's initiative to finally produce a document on enhancing the coherence, effectiveness and visibility of the eu's response to natural and man-made disasters. i regret, however, that this is still not a genuine, concrete proposal that could boost europe's civil protection capabilities, including prevention and rapid reaction, in the event of major crises occurring inside or outside the union. i thank the members of the european parliament for their support for my amendment to exploit 'the combined expertise in the geographical location of the outermost regions (ors) and the overseas countries and territories (octs) '. these overseas communities have made europe present off the coast of africa (canary islands, madeira), in the indian ocean (reunion), close to the american continent (guyana, guadeloupe, martinique, azores) and in the octs of the pacific (french polynesia, new caledonia). europe's overseas territories are poised to become focal points for the pre-positioning of essential products and logistics. the project would facilitate the deployment of european human and material resources in the event of emergency intervention outside the union.
in writing. the dramatic increase in the price of diesel fuel, 300% since 2003, is having a major impact on the fisheries sector. the continuing worsening of the crisis has put many fisheries undertakings in a very fragile financial situation. the fisheries sector is a particularly important pillar of the economic and social development of the outermost regions. in addition, the increase in fuel prices is all the more marked because of their remote geographical location. this is unacceptable. it is the duty of the european union to find a compromise. the european parliament has just sent a strong signal to fishermen. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. these proposals will be discussed by the council of european fisheries ministers on 23 and 24 june. the european union has no choice but to restore confidence with the fishing fleet, thus closing the abysmal gap that has recently been revealed.
the agenda calls for the debate on six motions for resolutions on burma.
member of the commission. − mr president, mrs ferrero-waldner is unfortunately not here today, so i shall – on her behalf – share with you a few remarks about the situation in burma/myanmar. the european parliament’s motion for a resolution focuses on the political situation and in particular on the continued detention of political prisoners. before commenting on this issue, i would like to inform you about the commission’s activities in response to the cyclone which devastated the delta of the ayeryawaddy river six weeks ago. the commission’s response to the cyclone was quick and substantial: we have approved eur 17 million in humanitarian aid, including eur 5 million in food aid. we have also activated the civil protection mechanism – the cooperation with the eu member states having joined the mechanism has worked very well. we cover water purification, boat transport, primary health care and other issues of importance in the post-disaster context. the humanitarian emergency is not over. so far, approximately half of the survivors reached, that is, one million, are still in desperate need. accessing the disaster-hit areas and distribution of aid is not without difficulties. this has as much to do with the size of the disaster as with the bureaucracy. our field workers in myanmar report gradually better cooperation from authorities. our own humanitarian activities continue with reasonable efficiency. we recognise that the international ngos are in a more difficult situation, as regards access to the stricken areas. in the mean time, the asean countries have taken the lead in coordinating external assistance. they are a member of the so-called ‘tripartite mechanism’, which comprises the asean countries, the government of burma/myanmar, and the united nations. the government has issued new ‘guidelines’ for external aid. we have no evidence yet whether they are being used to narrow the space for aid delivery. for us, the cyclone and its terrible consequences are a purely humanitarian issue. we defend the concept of ‘needs-based’ humanitarian relief. on the political situation in burma/myanmar, the government seems committed to proceed with its so-called ‘road map to democracy’. we read this road map as a tightly controlled, slow transition towards a civilian government where the military still plays a dominant role. the government seems committed to deliver, at its own pace and without regard to views and comments from outside. realistically, there is hardly an alternative. national reconciliation would require an inclusive dialogue. such dialogue cannot take place with political stakeholders in jail or under house arrest. this is why we continue to push for the release of all political prisoners. my colleague, mrs ferrero-waldner, has said publicly that the government has missed a chance to send a signal of reconciliation at a moment of national distress when the government again extended the house arrest of aung san suu kyi. the people of burma/myanmar would deserve a system of government which focuses on economic and social development, and on the participation of the electorate in the political process. for europe, expressing our indignation and isolating the country is clearly not an adequate response. the people of burma/myanmar shall not pay the price of a political stalemate. they deserve better. in conclusion, i wish to highlight our commitment to follow closely the situation in burma/myanmar. this includes continuing to push for a release of all political prisoners, and for an inclusive dialogue, including legal political parties and ethnic groups. we continue a balanced approach. we are not up to confrontation for the sake of confrontation. our ultimate goal remains to help a peaceful transition to a legitimate, civilian government. this is why we are fully supportive of the good offices of the un secretary general and his special advisor for myanmar. the interest of the burmese people is best served with a balanced policy, including substantial assistance. the commission has carefully chosen the areas of assistance to help the most vulnerable class of society. we have already significantly increased funding and hope that – in a coordinated effort with other donors – the overall funding level could reach the equivalent of what is spent per capita in comparable countries, like laos and cambodia. the people of myanmar deserve a better future.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place at the end of the debate.
the agenda calls for the debate on six motions for resolutions on somalia.
member of the commission. − mr president, unfortunately my colleague louis michel is not here today, so on his behalf i wish to share with you some remarks about this issue in somalia. firstly, i would like to share your concern about the continuing conflict and political instability in somalia. somalia remains a context where fundamental rights and respect for basic human dignity continue to be shunned by armed entities perpetrating systematic and widespread attacks against civilians. seventeen years of statelessness have seen loss of civilian life, mass displacements and destruction of physical infrastructures. one third of the population, corresponding to 2.6 million people, depends on humanitarian aid today. the european union, together with other key international actors, is committed to helping at this critical juncture. at the political level, the eu will continue to provide its full support to the un special representative of the secretary general in his efforts to coordinate the action of the international community and to facilitate inter-somali political dialogue. we are now examining – together with other donors – the appropriate ways and means to better assist somalis to effectively implement the djibouti agreement reached on 9 june. this agreement offers fresh hope for long-term peace and stability to the people of somalia. at humanitarian level, the eu is mainly focusing on supporting basic sectors such as health, nutrition, food assistance, shelter and non-food relief items, water and sanitation, as part of a range of activities particularly targeting central and southern areas of the country that have been badly affected by civilian strife and extreme natural hazards. in 2007 our humanitarian aid department managed to provide eur 18 million in humanitarian assistance. in response to the worsening humanitarian situation and to the increase in food prices, the level of assistance should reach a total of eur 27 million for this year. at the development level, the eu is already the main aid donor for somalia, providing medium- to long-term support for establishing a peaceful and self-sustainable society. the eu country strategy for somalia allocates more than eur 212 million for the period 2008-2013, under the 10th european development fund. one third of this programme will be spent on education, which is relevant to respect for human rights. the critical goal is to encourage reconciliation, democracy and the development of governance structures at all levels. however, without peace and security it is not possible to engage effectively in longer-term development. priority is therefore given to promoting a peaceful and secure environment in which human rights are respected and democratic processes and institutions can develop. commissioner michel met with the somali president, just a few days ago, on the margin of the igad summit in addis ababa. on that occasion, president yusuf made a strong appeal for international assistance to support a better, secure environment for people living in somalia. we gave a commitment to provide strong support for the somali government to this end. the european commission is already financing the training of somali police forces through the un, and funds are also being contributed to the costs of the amisom operation. ultimately the political process of reconciliation and stabilisation will also depend on the engagement and support of key regional players, namely ethiopia and eritrea, which have used the somali theatre for a ‘proxy war’. in this respect the withdrawal of ethiopian troops from somalia is a key element for any political breakthrough. commissioner michel, who met prime minister meles of ethiopia and president isaias of eritrea last weekend, urged them to support the djibouti process, which, although far from being perfect, offered a real if not the only opportunity to bring together the different somali actors. despite the difficult circumstances, the commission will continue its programme of aid to somalia, which has been designed with member states, in order to alleviate the suffering of the somali population and to establish the ground for a peaceful society. some questions were raised about piracy and i would add that, although it is not competent for the deployment of naval forces as foreseen by unsc resolution 1816, the commission has set up, together with the council, a working group composed of the relevant directorates-general – namely the energy and transport dg, the maritime affairs and fisheries dg, the development dg and europeaid – to study the best way to implement the un resolution.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place at the end of the debate.
the agenda calls for the debate on six motions for resolutions on iran.
member of the commission. − mr president, my colleague benita ferrero-waldner is unfortunately not here today, so on her behalf i thank you for the opportunity to address the issue of juvenile executions in iran. the commission shares your deep concern about this harrowing question. while, as you know, the commission lacks a representation in tehran, it follows the human rights situation very closely and acts in close concertation with the eu member states’ embassies represented there. it is important to note that the european parliament, the council of the european union and the commission have taken a coherent and consistent line. the seriousness of our concerns has been clearly stated through the three statements published by the eu presidency over the past two weeks: on 4 and 10 june, over the cases of mr fadaei, mr shojaee and mr jazee, all facing imminent executions for crimes committed when they were minors; and on 13 june, on the execution of mohammad hassanzadeh. the commission fully supports the principle and the content of these statements: there can be no justification for the use of the death penalty by the iranian authorities in the case of juvenile offenders. this explicitly runs counter to the legally binding provisions of international law, which iran has ratified, notably the international covenant on civil and political rights and the convention on the rights of the child. the fact that we have had to issue so many statements at such a rapid pace obviously reflects the growing number of executions in iran, including of minors. the moratorium decreed by iran’s chief judiciary, ayatollah shahroudi, on youth executions is blatantly violated by his own judges. but, unfortunately, the tone and the frequency of our statements on iran also reflect the fact that our dialogue and démarches on human rights in general and on the issue of juvenile executions in particular have not been effective. the iranian authorities increasingly turn a deaf ear to our calls for compliance with international human rights law and we have therefore no choice but to resort to the so-called ‘megaphone diplomacy’ via public statements that tehran claims to abhor and reject. iran must face up to its own responsibilities. for its part, following the execution of mr hassanzadeh, the commission has explicitly told the iranian authorities that such an act could only cast a shadow over’s iran’s international reputation and our relationship. without a concrete improvement of the human rights situation, our common objective of developing substantively the relationship between the european union and the islamic republic of iran is hindered. i trust that the european parliament and all eu partners will agree to this line and act accordingly. therefore, i solemnly reiterate our call to the authorities of the islamic republic of iran to abide by the international conventions to which it is party and spare the life of all minors still on death row.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place at the end of the debate.

internally and externally. we have many challenges to face, and the financial perspective is very limited. i therefore particularly welcome the courageous and political work of our rapporteur, jutta haug. it has succeeded in anticipating the steps of the budgetary procedure so that we can make clear the direction of our institution. this new procedure provides greater clarity for the citizen and therefore democracy. the priorities of the parliamentary committees and political groups were thus understood and discussed. unfortunately, i must once again deplore the council's lack of ambition and the systematic nature of its cuts in the commission's gnp. we find that his ambition is to save money on administrative expenses. it is not a question of identifying a political priority, but of making technical savings which sometimes double the margin in certain headings, as göran färm said about heading 1a. i also cannot explain the linear cuts in payments: minus one billion euros compared to the gnp. as regards heading 2, the statement is clear. in 2008, we left an unused margin of over 3 billion euros. for the 2009 budget, the commission proposes a margin of more than 2 billion, and the council says better by increasing this margin to 2.4 billion. however, there is a need for rural development, energy, immigration, global warming and international solidarity. at a time when the for the greens/efa group madam president, our colleague, mr jutta, is right to alert the commission to the possible improvements in his proposal when he talks about transparency of administrative expenditure, particularly for the agencies, better financial programming or better evaluation of human resources. i will focus on a paragraph in the haug report which points to the lack of correlation between the needs to combat climate change and the budget of the european union. our budget is roughly 1% of the continental gdp, which is paltry compared to the 20% of gdp that the united states commits at the federal level. the commission tells us that it takes 10% of this small percentage for climate change, i.e. 0.1% of gdp. the united nations framework convention on climate change, the stern report, the undp, the world bank, all tell us that to really counteract these effects, we would need to mobilize between 0.6 and 1.6% of gdp. the stern report even talks about 2% of gdp. the commission is therefore between 500 and 2 000% below what all these international reports tell us. another interesting figure is that to help developing countries, the un convention on climate change - mr president, on the gas market i would stress two points. the first concerns longterm contracts. this type of contract is an important tool for consumers, whether private or industrial. it allows a long-term view of the market and thus ensures a more stable and efficient functioning of the market. the second concerns the security of the networks and, above all, the security of gas supplies. even more than electricity, gas transmission networks are of strategic interest. the question of ownership is essential in the context of the european model, which is characterised by a high degree of dependence on producing countries outside the european union. for these reasons, i support the amendment in favour of a third way, which guarantees non-discriminatory access to the networks. my group has also taken the initiative, as it did for the electricity market, of creating a single european transmission system operator, which would safeguard our strategic interests. i would like to reassure my dear colleague, claude turmes. the aim of this gas market directive is not to protect national incumbents but to give them the opportunity to be major european energy champions.
mr president, we are faced with two radically opposite approaches to gas, as to energy in general. the liberal approach of treating gas and its supply as one commodity and one service among others, which leads to unbridled competition and the absurd dismantling of integrated utilities. prices are rising, services are deteriorating, and marketing and advertising costs are skyrocketing at the expense of research and development and security. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the fact that the community is not able to meet the demands of the world market. this approach is the basis for the reports submitted to us. another approach is to treat energy and gas and their supply as a public service due to all on the basis of equality and territorial equalization. it would lead to a genuine energy europe based on cooperation and the common interest. it would be built around a european energy agency which would coordinate and pool all the research efforts of the member states and guarantee equal access to energy for all citizens. it would be based on a grouping of economic interests including european energy companies, both public and private. this eig would lead to large industrial projects throughout the union in a cooperative framework and would make it possible to pool resources.

author. - madam president, madam president-in-office of the council, mr vice-president of the commission, thank you for giving us the opportunity to have this debate with the two institutions of reference. i hope, mr verheugen, that you can report to commissioner charlie mccreevy on the nature of our debate. we have had sovereign wealth funds active in europe for a long time, starting with the norwegian fund, and yet, until now, none of the actions of this fund have caused us any problems. two new developments have changed the game. firstly, the creation of large reserves by both the oil monarchies and the countries which have managed to create trade surpluses that feed these sovereign funds. the second event that has changed the balance of the debate is, of course, the subprime crisis, which has highlighted the strategic role that these sovereign funds can play. yesterday, when these funds intervened to invest here and there, particularly in the united states, their strategic nature was called into question. today, when we look at the role of sovereign wealth funds in providing cash and equity to investment banks, we see that they have become rather investors of last resort. in these circumstances, a certain emotion prevails, and that is why we wanted to ask this question. that is also probably why, unlike the commissioner responsible for the internal market, the president of the commission himself considered it useful and necessary on 27 february to put on the table a document which forms the basis of our discussion today. we are facing the risk of seeing a strategy put in place in each of the member states which, in the end, would not lead to facing the following reality: sovereign wealth funds have now acquired responsibility, an active share in the capital market, and this new situation, in a way, obliges them and obliges us in the dialogue we wish to have with the managing bodies of these funds. so, in the end, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, we would like to raise five questions today. firstly, we feel that the response so far from the commission's point of view has been to say: 'well, let each member state implement its own strategy, both in terms of transparency and governance requirements for these funds and at community level we will simply check whether these requirements defined in the framework of each member state are not contrary to the rules of the treaty and the rules of the internal market'. we do not think that is the appropriate strategy. it seems to us that in a case like this we should be much more proactive and coordinate at community level, both to avoid unfair competition between member states, because we see that there is a kind of 'chestnut race' where each member state wants to be the first to benefit most from the safe long-term investment capacity of these sovereign funds and at the same time define and work together on strategic or sensitive areas which should be preserved. the second question is the problem of recording these funds. can we imagine, at community level, prospects for registering these funds, just as we are thinking about them for the rating agencies? the third question concerns the interpretation of article 58, which allows restrictions on the free movement of capital where public policy so requires. is there, from the point of view of the council and the commission today, one interpretation which should prevail in this area? we'd like to meet her. fourthly, is this not a debate which is, in any case, of an international nature? and our concern is that, from the point of view of the european union, we would be better equipped, better equipped to tackle the international dimension of this debate if we had, in a certain way, defined the position of our base camp, that of the european union, and not that of this or that member state which has rushed into this race for the attractiveness of its financial centre. the last question is the question of the exchange rate. what about a situation where the oil monarchies are now investing in euro assets, money that has been accumulated through oil sales in dollars and that in writing. i have today supported the corbett report on the amendment of article 29 of the european parliament's regulation on the formation of political groups, namely the need to represent at least a quarter of the member states (instead of the current one-fifth) and to bring together at least 25 members (instead of 20), for several reasons. firstly, because i consider that this is a necessary reform to enable our institution to function better and to put an end to the fragmentation it is suffering from, with rules that have remained unchanged despite successive enlargements and the increased size of our assembly since 2004. the solution proposed by my socialist colleague, which ultimately led to a compromise with the majority of the political groups, seems to me very reasonable compared with what is happening at national level within the european union. moreover, given the human and financial resources made available to the political groups by the institution, a clear representativeness seems to me to be sufficient to justify this change as well. finally, it is a question of promoting a certain degree of coherence between the political forces at european level. our democracy can only emerge stronger.
in writing. this report does not accuse us of betrayal. from paragraph 1 it sets out its aim: the creation of a single european order. the report, which is a real pamphlet in favour of community law, calls for greater involvement and responsibility of national courts in the implementation of community law. it is therefore suggested that community legislation and related case law be incorporated as quickly as possible into national codes. the merger of the national and community legal systems is thus being pursued without at any time raising the question of the excess of community standards, their confusing wording, their frequent lack of coherence. the fact that we are moving towards simplification and codification of community legislation is certainly a good thing. the same applies to the adoption of regulations guaranteeing legal certainty; i am thinking in particular of those relating to the harmonization of the management of conflicts of laws. however, the case law of the court of justice often proves dangerous for the respect of national rights which are forced to accept its principles and dogmas, even if they are contrary to the best-established legal traditions of the member states.
in writing. so, are sovereign wealth funds, these state-owned funds that are investing all over the world, are they a good thing or a bad thing? that is a good thing, if that resolution is to be believed. but it is true that a europe which is economically broken by its own economic and monetary policies cannot afford to ignore the trillions of euros of potential investment that they represent. it is true that for the time being sovereign wealth funds do not disrupt financial markets (they have even come to the rescue of the us banking system) and are rather oriented towards long-term investments. but that can change. everyone knows how opaque most of these funds are about the amount of their resources, the distribution of their assets, their management structures, their investment strategies which range from ethical investment to the search for high returns, positions of control and perhaps tomorrow the capacity to cause harm. the countries holding these funds are far from all friends of europe. one of them has already raised the threat of "financial nuclear weapons". however, we abstain on this text instead of voting against it because, although it supports the free movement of capital at world level, it cautiously calls for some monitoring and protection against these funds.

in writing. on the basis of the report by my british colleague sarah ludford, i voted for the legislative resolution amending, at first reading by codecision, the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the common consular instructions to career diplomatic and consular posts in connection with the introduction of biometric identification elements and provisions on the organisation of the reception and processing of visa applications. this proposal aims to create the legal basis for member states to collect the mandatory biometric identification elements face photograph and 10 flat fingerprints of visa applicants and to establish a legal framework for the organisation of member states' consulates for the purpose of implementing the visa information system (vis) with the development of common visa application processing centres to avoid all member states equipping each of their consulates with the necessary equipment for the collection of biometric identification elements. i support the main amendments, in particular those on the representation of one member state by another, the safeguards for service providers in the event of outsourcing and information campaigns.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution of 10 july 2008 on the proposal for a council regulation establishing a temporary specific action to encourage the restructuring of the european union's fishing fleets affected by the economic crisis. one of the main challenges facing the european union's fishing industry remains, in many fisheries, the structural imbalance between fleet capacity and available resources. the overcapacity of the european union fleet was estimated some years ago at about 40%. this overcapacity, combined with the erosion of the resource by decades of overexploitation, has the effect that the sector is unable to withstand external economic pressures such as the sharp rise in fuel prices. i regret that no community instrument is envisaged to annualise the rise in oil prices in order to give the internal market time to be able to influence the rise in its cost prices. i welcome the action of the french minister for agriculture and fisheries, mr michel barnier, who has spared no effort to achieve such a result as to obtain immediate support measures.
in writing. i voted against the european parliament resolution calling on italy to stop the ethnic census of roma because it seems premature and i regret that parliament did not vote on the motion for a postponement in september 2008 that my political group, the epp-de, proposed. let me be clear: i am naturally in favour of a ban on the collection of fingerprints from the roma population, including minors, and on the use of fingerprints collected, because this would clearly constitute an act of direct discrimination on grounds of race and ethnic origin, prohibited by article 14 of the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms, and would also constitute an act of discrimination. nevertheless, i was convinced by the arguments of my friend jacques barrot, vice-president of the european commission, because he made it clear that the commission was following the situation closely and transparently to ensure that community law was being applied. i have been conscious of the fact that we should wait for the proven and contradictory responses of the italian state before taking political initiatives such as the resolution adopted which may be misinterpreted by the european citizens.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this joint resolution on the situation in china. it is important to keep up the pressure on china before the olympics are held in less than a month. we cannot turn a blind eye to the serious human rights deficiencies that persist, in contradiction to the commitments made by china itself. it is the responsibility of the european parliament to recall these public promises. it was important to mention minority rights, the rule of law and the still frequent use of the death penalty. finally, i regret that some of the more severe amendments against china were not adopted; i am thinking in particular of the demands for the release of dissidents and human rights defenders such as hu jia and his wife zeng jinyan, the mention of the situation in tibet which is far from being normalized, and the disproportionate sentences handed down without transparency against protesters in connection with the protests this spring.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i take from mr brok's report on enlargement that any new accession can only be a success if, i quote, 'there is clear and long-term support from the population'. this phrase seems hypocritical, just a few days after the eurocracy's contemptuous reaction to the irish's clear "no" to the lisbon treaty, which is itself only a repetition of the french and dutch "no's" of 2005. or after the replacement in the french constitution of the mandatory referendum on eu membership by a pseudo-referendum on "popular initiative" which in fact depends on the goodwill of the assembly and the senate. but it is true that mr brok, knowing that the vast majority of europeans are against turkey's membership, does not even envisage consulting the people by referendum. it is only the good old propaganda that is used to win support for public opinion, which is considered ignorant or even primitive. if mr brok and his european or national peers fear - or despise - the people so much, they should at least have the decency not to stand for their votes. democracy in europe would certainly be strengthened.
in writing. like all the peoples of the world, zimbabweans want peace, democracy, prosperity. with robert mugabe, they have none of that. he was once the liberator of his country, now he's the executioner. today, this parliament is sending a clear message: it does not want mugabe and his regime anymore. because the people of zimbabwe have decided so. the eu must weigh in with all its might to support a zimbabwean and african way out of the crisis. the priority is to end the violence. only a dialogue open to all components of zimbabwean society will allow the establishment of a transitional regime with a clear mandate for the organisation of free, transparent and internationally monitored elections. but robert mugabe will only come to the negotiating table if he is forced and coerced. that is why we must strengthen the arsenal of targeted sanctions against the regime. finally, we must prepare today for the reconstruction of zimbabwe of tomorrow: i welcome the commission's proposal to release eur 250 million as a matter of urgency, as soon as zimbabwe is given legitimate and credible power.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my excellent german colleague karl von wogau on space and security. the time has come to have a common approach to defending european interests in space. it is becoming increasingly clear that we need space assets so that the eu's political and diplomatic activities can be based on independent, reliable and comprehensive information to support its conflict prevention policies, its crisis management operations and global security (in particular the monitoring of the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their means of transport), the verification of compliance with international treaties, the monitoring of transnational smuggling of small arms and light weapons, the protection of sensitive eu infrastructure and borders, and civil protection in the event of crises and natural disasters. gallileo is, in this respect, an important building block for the eu's space role. this approach must go hand in hand with a defence europe and support for a european defence industry, particularly in the space sector.

president of the commission. - mr president of the european parliament, mr president of the european council, ladies and gentlemen, dear friends, i am pleased to be joining you in the european parliament to present the french presidency of the council of the union for six months. i believe that this will be a presidency full of dynamism and determination and rich in concrete results, which we will all be working towards. the return of france to europe, which you have called for, mr president, is undoubtedly very good news for us all. the french presidency raises many expectations in europe, among the citizens and certainly among the european parliament, which is here. as i said at our meeting in paris on 1 july, the commission will stand by your presidency to give it its full support and ensure the success of the european union during this six-month period. because there are challenges! globalisation is here and international competition is increasingly fierce. new global challenges, such as the scarcity of fossil fuels and climate change, require urgent and joint solutions. all these factors place europe in the need to reform its economies to increase its competitiveness, to modernise its social models and to invest in education, research and innovation. europe has many assets to succeed, including its position as the world's leading trading power. but it needs to have the courage to adapt; if we want to protect it, we have to adapt. that's the problem. europe is going through a difficult period, there is no need to deny it: the irish 'no' and the world economic situation, the soaring prices of oil and raw materials, the sharp rise in food prices, the inflationary surge, which is the first enemy of purchasing power. inflation is the first enemy of social justice because when there is very high inflation, those who suffer first are those who have low wages or live only on their pensions. all these factors are casting a shadow over our economies at the moment and are placing policy makers, both at european and national level, before difficult choices. we must face these realities and deal with them realistically and with determination. we have just returned from the g8 summit in japan and my observation is clear: the influence of the european union, but also the expectations and respect it arouses in the world, contrast very sharply with the feeling of pessimism which is very often expressed within the union. i can tell you today that the european union is perceived more than ever outside europe as a positive and decisive actor. an actor who has great influence on the world stage. let us take two concrete issues that were at the heart of the g8 debates: climate change and development issues, two issues in which europe has taken the lead on a global level. the united states has now joined the fight against climate change by very broadly agreeing with our positions. last year, at heiligendamm, i remember very well that we had a lot of trouble - president sarkozy was already there - to convince the americans and the russians to accept the principle of a mandatory target for 2050. and there it is! it is done, and it was made possible by our european leadership role; i am proud of that as president of a european institution. this is a success which we owe, once again, to european unity. the second example is development, and more specifically the soaring food prices which are jeopardising the achievement of all the millennium development goals (mdgs). we have also been able to play a catalytic role in this area, thanks to the conclusions of the european council last month which, i quote, welcomed 'the commission's willingness to put forward a proposal to establish a new fund for agricultural support in developing countries'. the european commission will adopt this proposal next week. i am counting on the full support of both arms of the budgetary authority so that europe can quickly provide the aid it needs to farmers, especially farmers in africa, in close cooperation with the relevant multilateral organizations. this support is essential to ensure the 'green revolution' that africa needs for its stability and prosperity, which, as we all know, is also in europe's direct interest. as the european council has asked, our proposal will be within the limits of the present financial perspective. the logic of our approach is to attribute the savings which the rise in international prices enables europe to make in its internal policy of agricultural support to those who are now suffering most from this increase. there are situations of tragedy in the world that are extremely urgent. if you had heard directly what i heard from the president of the world bank, if you had heard from the mouths of some of the leaders of these african countries and other countries who were also represented in the enlarged meetings, the drama, the hunger that now constitutes a real threat to so many citizens of our world, you would understand how necessary and indispensable the help of europe is. (applause) i would like to thank that is why i believe that here again we can set a good example of solidarity between european and african farmers, a good illustration of how the cap and development policy can and must go hand in hand, because as president sarkozy has just said, we have food security problems in the world and we must face them in solidarity, not in isolation, but in solidarity. so there are concerns, it is true, but it is also true that, more than ever, the european union is indispensable to address them. instead of indulging in what i often call 'crisophilia' - there is even talk of an industry of europe's decline - let us therefore value the concrete and positive action of the european union! this is the best way of resolving the institutional issues raised by ireland's non-ratification of the treaty of lisbon. we must work on this because the lisbon treaty will enable us to work more efficiently and more democratically, but we must not use this as an excuse for not responding immediately to the needs of our citizens. the citizens of europe look to us for answers. the best way to respond to them is to speak the language of truth and to show political courage. two qualities that the french presidency does not lack! in a europe that is being tested, we must make europe by proof. we need to focus on policies that bring europe closer to citizens and make a positive difference to their daily lives. more than ever, our course remains the europe of results. i'm still confident about myself. the priorities of your presidency will enable europe to meet the major challenges it faces today, while preparing for the challenges of tomorrow. i welcome the priority given by the french presidency to the establishment of an integrated energy policy and the fight against climate change. as you said, mr president, this is the top priority of your presidency, and we know your determination to conclude this strategic agreement by the end of the year, which would put the union in a good position to enter the copenhagen negotiations in a year's time. the commission will give its full support to our efforts to reach an ambitious and balanced agreement with the european parliament and the member states. i have made it a priority for my institution, and i would like to thank president sarkozy again for his unwavering support of the european commission's climate/energy package. we must also move towards a controlled immigration policy in europe. first of all, we must deal with the immigration that an ageing europe needs in certain key economic sectors, and that must be accompanied by decent integration conditions so that we can be proud in our humanist europe of the integration we offer to those who honestly want to work here. the adoption of the 'blue card' under the french presidency would be a very important step in this direction. but we also need to tackle illegal immigration and the exploitation that often follows, including by putting forward the proposal to penalize employers of illegal workers. this is where the main effort should be made. we must not threaten the poor workers who want to work with dignity in europe, but we must punish those who want to exploit the underground. their practice is not worthy of our europe. so let's be clear, there is no contradiction. we must look at this question of immigration in a very realistic way. i am firmly convinced, ladies and gentlemen, that our failure to deal with this matter in a serious and responsible manner is one of the greatest threats to europe. it is not a policy of absolute permissiveness that will enable us to solve the problem. it would be the best pretext for extremist forces, for xenophobic forces. we must be firm, absolutely firm against illegal immigration, and at the same time be generous and show solidarity in integrating migrant communities who also want to contribute to the development and growth of our europe. i think we need to be clear about this; we must be firm against crime, but always with respect for human rights, which are the very hallmark of our european civilization and our project of european construction. of course, these are sensitive subjects, which are easily subject to controversy and misunderstanding. the commission has therefore proposed a balanced basis and has set out ten main principles for moving forward together. i am pleased with the positive response to this integrated approach by the french presidency and the ministers of justice and the ministers of the interior at their informal meeting in cannes this week. i would like to say to you, ladies and gentlemen, that in a europe, in the schengen area, where freedom of movement is a reality, it is absurd, i repeat, it is absurd to continue with 27 different immigration policies; we need a european immigration policy. another project for the future is our social agenda. there can be no dynamic and competitive economic model without a real approach to social investment to prevent the risks of poverty, exclusion and marginalisation. france has made the new social agenda presented by the european commission a few days ago one of its priorities. i'm glad you did. to prepare europeans for the future, we must provide them with opportunities, access to quality services, education, health care and always solidarity. no one in europe should be left on the sidelines. europe is a project of openness and solidarity. ladies and gentlemen, many other projects will be opened during the semester, i cannot mention them all, but if i may briefly highlight two, i would like to pay tribute to those of european defence and the union for the mediterranean, which will be launched on sunday in paris. i see two opportunities for europe to assert its role in the world. here too, it is up to us to turn that will into concrete action. i wish the french presidency of the council every success and assure you of the commission's full support throughout this exciting six months ahead. the first duty of political leaders is to face the challenges as they arise and to redouble their determination to meet them successfully. we can do a lot if we move forward together. i would like to welcome the efforts made over the last few months by the french authorities, at the highest level, to work closely with the european institutions. the institutions, the presidency, the member states: we must work hand in hand. this is the key to the common success we owe to the citizens of europe and i would like to i am glad to see the chairman of the committee on constitutional affairs here, because we have a delicate problem to deal with. my dear jo, if you'll just go back to your seat. i will explain the problem we have, colleagues. rule 149 of our rules of procedure says that we can check whether a quorum has been reached. you know that parliament is still in session to deliberate on its agenda and to adopt the minutes. so, there is no quorum required. on the other hand, rule 149 (3) of our rules of procedure provides that, at the prior request of at least 40 members, it may be checked whether or not a quorum has been reached. i have received a written request from 40 members to check whether or not the quorum is reached. so, obviously... mr. posselt, please, let me explain the facts. obviously, i can see that there is a prior request, clearly stated. the problem is that afterwards our rules are much more vague. it is never stated that the forty must be present in the chamber to make this request for verification of the quorum, but it is not ruled out either. so i have a margin of appreciation. in previous cases - we have checked - the president of the sitting has always considered that the forty must be present in the chamber to give any substance to rule 149 (4), which provides that when the quorum is counted, the forty must be counted. that implies that all 40 must be in the room. but i have a margin of appreciation. and there is the wording of the request: it concerns the vote on emergencies, but all emergencies, not one of the emergencies, all emergencies. if we ever consider the request for a quorum to be admissible and the quorum is not met, all the emergencies will fall, and you know that we cannot postpone them. so we will not vote on kashmir, or on the death penalty, or on bangladesh. if we do not vote, we shall not adjourn to the next part-session. parliament will not be voting on these matters which are said to be urgent. before giving my opinion, i would therefore like to hear, in particular, the opinion of the chairman of the committee on constitutional affairs. mr leinen, do you think i should consider that all 40 petitioners must be present in the chamber as is suggested by rule 149 (4) or can i consider that a simple prior written request is sufficient as is suggested by rule 149 (3)? i'm listening to you very carefully.
mr president, you asked our colleague jo leinen first to try to give you our feeling. as my colleague has said before, it is true that the manoeuvre seems a little delaying, that is to say that 40 colleagues who, for reasons of their own, were unable to attend this sitting are trying by means of measures and procedures to avoid having an emergency debate here this afternoon. i think, however, that perhaps we should look beyond the scrupulous application of the rules and look at the spirit of the regulation. the spirit of the rules is to ensure that the people who put in the request for a quorum are at least present to see for themselves that there is no quorum. otherwise, i think the request is either a political maneuver or a tactic, but it is a delay. i would not like to see us, by strictly applying the law, regularly having all the important emergency debates on thursday afternoons, which, if they were to be 'avoided', would not enhance the value of parliamentary work.

member of the commission. − mr president, the european union is firmly opposed to the use of the death penalty and actively works towards the abolition of capital punishment worldwide. in countries that maintain the death penalty, the eu aims at the progressive restriction of its scope, as well as at the establishment of a moratorium so as to eliminate the death penalty completely. the guidelines to eu policy towards third countries on the death penalty, adopted in 1998 and revised in 2008, set out the framework for eu action. they include declarations or demarches in international fora and towards third countries, including the united states of america. as regards the usa, the eu is deeply concerned about the resumption of executions since the lifting of the de facto moratorium on the death penalty in may. we have repeatedly urged the us government to reintroduce a moratorium on the death penalty at federal level and we hope that the united states will consider abolishing the death penalty by law in the foreseeable future. we take note of parliament’s motion for a resolution regarding the individual case of mr troy davis. we have intelligence from our washington delegation that the governor of georgia has not yet signed the execution order and that he is apparently in no hurry to do so. the commission, along with eu member states and the presidency, will of course follow this case very closely.

on behalf of the pse group. mr president, the dublin system should indeed make it possible to determine the member state responsible for an asylum application, but this system is profoundly unfair. asylum seekers may thus sometimes be returned to a member state which is known to reject their asylum application when the member state in which they are present would have granted them refugee status. that's the first injustice. the system also poses a problem of solidarity between member states. the member states on the external borders of europe bear a greater burden, as is well known. on our return from malta we had asked for the very principle of the dublin system to be called into question. we believe that the member state responsible for processing an asylum application should not necessarily be the first country of access. there must be solidarity between the processing of applications. we have seen serious shortcomings, particularly in the protection of unaccompanied minors. we have found that the member states do not make sufficient use of the instruments which enable minors to be reunited with their family members in another member state. we also want minors to be able to join, for example, uncles and aunts in another member state, rather than being left to their own devices. so we need to broaden the concept of family. finally, we deplore the almost systematic use by some member states of the detention of persons awaiting dublin transfer. it should be remembered that these people are seeking international protection and that their application has not yet been thoroughly examined. and the evaluation of the dublin ii regulation must therefore enable us to correct the serious shortcomings we have observed during our visits to the detention camps. we visited many of the camps and returned, i must say, quite disgusted with some of the visits. i would remind you that the purpose of the dublin regulation is to determine the member state responsible for the application for asylum. the regulation must allow access to the asylum system and must ensure that a member state carries out a thorough examination of any asylum application. the european union must member of the commission. - ladies and gentlemen, i think that the depth and passion of the debate have clearly shown that social europe is on the move again. the debate has covered a number of detailed issues and i do not think it is necessary to respond to them in detail, because there will be an opportunity in the next negotiations to deepen the argumentation, to find the appropriate balance. but let me respond to some things in a more general way. firstly, this agenda, because of its breadth, considers the social agenda and social policy as an expression of a comprehensive policy approach and as the result of an integrated approach in a number of policies. it is a certain notion of the mainstream, that is, not a social policy confined somewhere on the periphery, with a number of undoubtedly interesting and technical aspects, but still in a way marginalized. this agenda has placed social policy at the heart of european policy. of course, the question arose whether this agenda, which i think should be rejected in all seriousness, does not have some simple technical instrumental political interest. it doesn't, because the approach to it was formulated many years ago. it is also in a number of european commission documents which have been discussed by parliament. so it's not related to any major event, like the irish referendum. among other things, this agenda also shows that the commission is determined and has proposed the agenda as a procedure that seeks to use all the instruments available to the european commission and at european level, legislation, the open method of coordination and all other methods. it therefore contains not only legislative proposals but also, of course, draft communications and other documents. i would like to stress that this agenda is specific within the possibilities that are within the european commission's control. the individual proposals will undoubtedly be debated in parliament, and will certainly be amended on many occasions, but they are nevertheless concrete proposals that can be discussed. the debate also raised the argument, albeit partial, and i think it is necessary to respond to it, that the proposals which are aimed at the health sector are a kind of back door to the bolkenstein directive on health care. it's not like that. these proposals are not designed to provide free services but to facilitate access to healthcare for europeans. there are undoubtedly many very delicate aspects to these proposals and it is clear that they will be seriously and deeply discussed, but nevertheless their basic trend and result will be to improve health care for european citizens. the other idea that i would like to stress very much is the idea of fighting poverty. the fight against poverty is clearly formulated and the debate raised a very clear question: 'by what methods?' the agenda does not assume that there is a single effective method to combat poverty, but it intends to attack poverty from a number of aspects. trying to reduce early school leaving is a fight against poverty. the effort to open up the space for lifelong learning is a fight against poverty. the clearly formulated intention that equity and social efficiency should be at the forefront of pension systems is also a fight against poverty. the issue of discrimination and anti-discrimination directives are also an issue of fighting poverty, because opening up access to people who are disabled, preventing discrimination against people who have aged in service, etc. are simultaneously fighting poverty. the question of equal opportunities for men and women was also open. i would point out that other directives cover equal opportunities for men and women and, in this respect, it was not necessarily necessary to include explicitly equality between men and women in the proposed directive. there was also a debate on the ilo conventions. i want to make it clear that this agenda clearly demonstrates the strong commitment of the commission and europe to the concept of decent work at global level. as well as a directive to implement the social partners' agreement in the maritime field, it is a clear approach to how europe views the various ilo conventions. in all the documents, european states are called upon to ratify as quickly as possible the overall package of documents they represent. ladies and gentlemen, the debate has been deep and at times hard. i think this is a debate that is on par with the importance of european social policy.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place at the next partsession, somewhere in europe. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.

in writing. i voted, on the basis of the report by my distinguished british colleague neil parish, for the legislative resolution approving, as it stands, in accordance with the consultation procedure, the proposal for a council regulation amending the council regulation of june 2007 on organic production and labelling of organic products. normally, the council regulation of 28 june 2007 on organic production and labelling of organic products was to be applied compulsorily as from 1 january 2009. the purpose of this proposal is to postpone the mandatory use of the eu logo pending the creation of a new logo to help avoid confusion in the minds of consumers following a rapid change of eu logos and to avoid an additional financial burden for operators who are required to change their packaging and printing within a very short time. the proposal is therefore to defer the mandatory use of the eu logo until 30 june 2010.
in writing. the european parliament has just delivered its opinion in accordance with the agreement on fisheries in the southern indian ocean, signed by the european community in 2006. the community had fishing interests in the area and, as a result of the presence of réunion, was obliged to cooperate with the other parties involved in the management and conservation of the resources of this area under the united nations convention on the law of the sea. this new regional fisheries organisation establishes a specific institutional framework, the centrepiece of which is the standing scientific committee. the main task of the centre is to provide a scientific assessment of fisheries resources and the impact of fishing on the marine environment, taking into account the environmental characteristics of the area. the agreement also encourages cooperation in the field of scientific research. on the basis of these scientific recommendations, the parties will be fully able to develop conservation and management measures that are best suited to address the challenges facing the area. this agreement is a real step forward in the promotion of fisheries resources and sustainable development.
