mr president, for several weeks now the world has been going through a serious financial crisis. it has often been explained as having its origins in the vagaries of unfettered capitalism, the pursuit of profit without any basis in reality and the lack of regulation of our financial system. and of course, the analysis is correct! but less attention has been paid to the whirlwind into which our currency would have been plunged had it not been for the economic and monetary policy of the european union. the euro has proved to be much more resilient than the mark, the franc or the lire. it is also clear that the decisions taken eight days ago by the eurogroup, on the initiative of the president-in-office of the council of the european union, have had an immediate effect on the financial markets. of course, measures will have to be taken to prevent a future financial crisis. but if they are to be effective, they must be taken at european level. this crisis shows us that the european union is strong when it speaks with one voice. it shows us, if need be, that the institutional improvements provided for by the lisbon treaty are more necessary than ever. so what we need is more and better europe.
mr president, i wanted to respond to the comments made by mr corbett and others about our return to strasbourg and the cost of doing so. it is true that europe is not just a matter of reason. even though it tries to be rational, it also works from symbols. it is not a unitary state and we do not operate with a single capital within which all our institutions are located. some of them are here in strasbourg, the central bank is in frankfurt, i believe the medicines agency is in britain. all of this comes at a cost. but we also know the cost of the absence of europe, and we have paid a lot for it in our history. so, two hundred million euros - if it is one of the elements that allows institutions to function well and, for example, europe to better understand the dysfunctions of financial markets and, perhaps, tomorrow, to save rescue plans for financial institutions of more than one trillion euros - i believe that this is a price worth paying for a well-functioning democracy.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i hope that the presidency of the council will join us, it is now more than six years since the adoption of the directive on temporary agency work was postponed, not because parliament, which took a decision on the commission proposal as soon as it was before it in 2002, was concerned, but precisely because of the blockage of certain member states in the council. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this field, and i am sure that the commission will be able to take them up in the near future. temporary agency work accounts for more than three million employees in the union. they are employed by some 20 000 companies, representing a turnover of 75 billion euros. this is obviously a sector which is very sensitive to changes in growth and temporary workers are now the first to be affected by the economic downturn and the rise in unemployment, but like other forms of precarious and atypical work, it has been increasing structurally in recent years and this development is estimated at almost 60% over the past five years. this trend is continuing particularly strongly in the new member states. temporary work affects a very large number of sectors, which vary from one member state to another: industry in some countries, services in others, construction, agriculture, transport in others. the proportion also varies greatly from one country to another. it can be as high as 5% of all workers in countries such as the united kingdom. the duration of the missions also varies. in some countries it is short, such as missions of about ten days in france, less than a week in spain, or about 20 days in finland. but in other countries, such as ireland, belgium and the netherlands, it can be several months, or even a year or more in austria. we know that temporary workers are more exposed to physical risks, to the intensity of work, to accidents at work. their training is often less important. the stress of precarious employment is also very much present. however, the legislation and the types of legal framework governing their situation vary widely in the member states. so that temporary workers are, for example, only really protected by equal treatment, especially in terms of pay, in ten of the twenty-seven countries of the european union. their access to training, social protection, maternity leave - all these subjects are variable and are not guaranteed in the same way in all the member states. this is why the european commission, at the request of the social partners and with the support of the european parliament, has wanted legislation to ensure equal treatment. after a first draft was presented to us, the european parliament, in november 2002, on the basis of the report by my colleague, ieke van den burg, who is still present in this house and whom i would like to congratulate, strengthened this draft legislation by allowing, in particular, equal treatment to be ensured from the first day, particularly in terms of pay. when adopting its common position last june, the council finally agreed with the european parliament's position. it considered that equal treatment from day one should be the general rule and that any derogation from this principle should be agreed by the social partners through collective bargaining or agreements with the social partners at national level. the european parliament's amendments concerning the definition of the essential conditions of work and employment, including the inclusion of remuneration in article 3, were also adopted in the common position. finally, the council's common position retained the amendments relating to access to employment, collective facilities, vocational training and the right to representation for temporary workers under the same conditions as for permanent workers in the user undertaking. a debate was held in the committee on employment and social affairs on parliament's initial proposal to amend the commission's proposal to add elements on health, safety and hygiene at work, which were not accepted by the council. but these guarantees exist under another directive, the council directive of 25 june 1991, which complements the measures to promote the improvement of safety and health at work of workers in fixed-term or temporary employment relationships. as you know, ladies and gentlemen - i shall conclude this first speech on this point - the european trade union confederation, on the one hand, and the trade organizations representing temporary agency workers, on the other, want us to adopt this legislation. adopting this legislation today means ensuring that the european parliament's positions at first reading now become law, that this protective framework for temporary workers can be transposed within the next three years and that the pandora's box of uncertain negotiation within the council is not reopened. that is why the committee on employment and social affairs decided on 7 october to recommend adoption of the common position without amendments in order to protect this sector of work, which is the most precarious in europe.
the european parliament has a duty to protect the environment. madam president, mr minister, mr commissioner, first of all, we have here the conclusion of extremely constructive work between the european institutions on the one hand, the member states but also between the political groups and the social partners. the text we have reached is based on consensus with the social partners. this proposal for a directive now defines a general framework for temporary workers in the 27 member states and is an extremely important step forward, based on the principle of non-discrimination between permanent and temporary workers. we have put in it a desire for transparency - transparency on the conditions of workers - but also a desire for trust between workers and employers. the security of workers and the flexibility that companies need are extremely important, which is why today the european people's party, which has relied on these principles of equal treatment, access to vocational training and the arrangements for representing temporary workers under collective agreements, has also wanted to advance this work in consensus. europe today protects these workers. this framework directive for the protection of temporary agency workers sets out new working conditions. we are convinced that we will move forward together on the social europe. that is why we will of course vote for this directive without any amendments as proposed today.
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i should first like to thank my colleagues for their speeches and the shadow rapporteurs, the coordinators, all those who have taken part in this debate, for their support for your rapporteur and, in so doing, for the completion of this procedure. it is true that the report was reduced to a statement of reasons and a single request: "let us approve!" the next adoption of this directive, i hope in two days' time, is a victory for the european parliament and a victory for the social partners. and i would like to take this opportunity to reply to my colleagues in the gue who tabled some amendments, the value of which i can understand in substance, but i would nevertheless like to stress the fact that the european trade union confederation again addressed the chairman of the political groups a few days ago to say that the adoption of this directive, without amendment, would be a strong signal that social progress at european union level is necessary and possible and that social europe is still alive. as the temporary work sector, like other types of atypical employment contracts, developed, a legal framework was needed. and that's the decision we make. europe is a space of law. it must be so in the area of civil rights, it must be so in economic and social matters. we have affirmed, through other directives, the protections and rights enjoyed by all workers. as the number of temporary workers increases, we must ensure that they enjoy the same rights and that the use of temporary work is not used in an abusive way to circumvent the rights of the workers concerned or of other workers who would then be subject to a kind of pressure and social dumping. we also want to show, by adopting this directive, that social europe can move forward, that it can have a concrete content, contrary to what has sometimes been heard in the commission - not from commissioner vladimir špidla, but from other members of the college. in social matters too, we can legislate, we can collegiate, and show the members of the council who have blocked the adoption of this legislation for too long, as well as other legislation, that they should not be frightened by the advances of social europe and that showing that europe is defending citizens and workers may also help to reconcile citizens with the institutions of the union and respond to the anxieties and concerns that have been expressed in ireland, the netherlands and my country, france. more progress on the social directive, i believe, will also contribute to more progress on political europe and to citizens' support for the progress of political europe.
on behalf of the pse group. mr president, we are debating two joint issues today: the eu-australia agreement on the transfer of passenger data - pnr - and the establishment of a european pnr. the agreement with australia seems to us to be much more acceptable than other agreements with other third countries. it is therefore particularly positive that data are made anonymous and that the transfer and subsequent use of data is limited. we are also particularly pleased that the australian authorities have confirmed the unnecessary collection of sensitive data such as food preferences. however, we remain concerned because the purpose for which the data can be used is poorly defined. the data retention period and the number of data required also appear to us to be excessive. finally, i think it is essential to define more clearly the data protection which will benefit european citizens. we also call on the council and the member states to strengthen democratic control by involving the european parliament before the agreements are finalised. the issues raised by the agreement with australia reflect the problems of setting up a european pnr. we cannot simply respond to requests from third countries. the european union must lead by example in safeguarding its tradition of privacy protection. we refuse to simply copy the pnr agreement with the united states at the level of the union. there is a need for an open debate on whether the use of pnr data is actually useful and, if so, under what conditions.
the rapporteur. - mr president, we are debating this evening the erasmus mundus programme 2009-2013, on which we have finally reached agreement with the council. the programme will therefore be able to enter into force in january 2009 and will thus benefit students from the beginning of the academic year in september. i would like to thank all my colleagues for their opinions in the committees on employment, women, budget, development and foreign affairs, and also my colleagues on the committee on culture and education. i want to thank the european commission, of course. i would also like to thank the president of the erasmus mundus association and the executive agencies who have been able to provide us with their expertise and, above all, their experience. five years after the adoption of erasmus mundus, almost to the day, i am pleased to present this second generation programme, which continues to promote excellence in european higher education by enabling the most talented students from third countries and europe to follow high-level joint programmes at at least three universities and benefit from a high-quality welcome and substantial scholarships. the results of the previous programme speak for themselves: between 2004 and 2008, 103 master's degrees were selected and awarded, more than 6 000 students received an erasmus mundus grant, more than 1 000 teachers from third countries visited our european universities, and more than 400 higher education institutions from europe and third countries were involved. this new programme comprises three actions. the first opens up the programme to doctoral students and will allow european students to also receive grants, albeit at a lower level. the second concerns exclusively partnerships with higher education institutions in third countries, and the third is devoted to the information policy to be pursued on the international scene. the budget is €950 million. by comparison, the first programme had a budget of only eur 230 million. the improvements made by parliament to this programme have been very important and i should like to quote them to you as a tribute. first improvement: the criteria for selecting students now remain academic excellence, even in the context of partnerships. secondly, the criteria of geographical distribution will be respected in order to achieve the most balanced representation possible. thirdly, the principles of gender equality and non-discrimination will be respected. fourthly, administrative obstacles and procedures, particularly those relating to visas, will have to be removed. member states will have to take the necessary measures to facilitate the issuing of visas to third-country students who are moving between several member states. we are very keen on this, even though it has been a little difficult in our negotiations with the council to achieve it. secondly, the teaching of foreign languages in the host universities will be encouraged. the doctorates will involve institutions from at least three different european countries. this will allow a wide variety of research topics, theses, and much more varied mobility opportunities. the scholarships will be more tailored and will take into account the amounts of the enrolment fees as well as the amount of the estimated expenditure for the student's studies. the registration fee was worked out in close cooperation with the danish permanent representation and an expert from the danish ministry of education, which enabled us to find a compromise satisfactory to all. public-private partnerships with universities will be encouraged, with particular attention to the issue of brain drain. under action 2 the funds will be allocated and used in accordance with the objectives of the development instruments and external relations. the information available at universities will be clearer. finally, the evaluation report which will be drawn up in two years' time will be more detailed and will be broken down by action and geographical area. i would like to thank the rapporteur for his excellent report, which has been very helpful in this respect. i therefore hope that parliament will adopt it in order to meet the expectations of many students, academics and researchers in europe and the world.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, let me tell you how much i enjoyed applying the principles of governance myself in the preparation of this report with the various stakeholders. this method of working, moreover, has proved to be very useful in the preparation of this report, since it has enabled me to take account of almost all the proposals of my colleagues, and this resulted in a unanimous vote in the committee on regional development on 9 september. but this consensus would be nothing if it were not embodied in a text that is as concrete and coherent as i shall show you in a moment. i would therefore like to express my sincere thanks to all my colleagues who have contributed to this report, and in particular to the fictitious rapporteurs who would have liked to be here tonight to show their commitment. i would like to thank the commission, mr commissioner, and thank you for passing them on to them, because this cooperation has been both constructive and pleasant. i would also like to thank the european economic and social committee and its rapporteur, mr van iersel, the committee of the regions, mr kisyov, and the many bodies which took part. so governance, partnership, what is it all about? well, we must have an own-initiative report on this question of governance and partnership, since we talk about governance and partnership every day. you can look in the newspapers, you can look in the reports, you can always find these words! in fact, commissioner, there is a time for words and a time for deeds! there is a time to set goals and there is a time to give oneself the means to achieve them. the need for improved governance has been repeatedly stressed for several years now. we write it in our regulations, we talk about it in our speeches and nothing much progress. what is really happening when we see that the integrated approach is included in the many reports of the commission and parliament? are our european policies on transport, the environment and regional development really taking each other into account? where's the whole-of-the-whole approach we call vows? each has its budget, each its minister, each its commissioner, each its calendar. and we can see, even if only in the case of the structural funds, the application on the ground and separately between the erdf, the esf and other eafrd. as commissioner, you and your colleagues know that we are all committed to achieving the lisbon objectives. but if you continue to do this, to be so compartmentalized on the ground, do you think that's possible? do you think that an organization as powerful as this, as determined as this, can succeed by allowing this "every man for himself" to be juxtaposed on the ground? today, the time has come to bring our skills together, to bring our budgets and our timetables together between the various private and public actors concerned with the same subject in the same territory. to achieve this, my report proposes 37 concrete actions, but i will not list them, only three key points. the first key point is to give the various actors, private, public, individuals, organisations, the means to implement this governance. the first point, as i pointed out to your colleague, mrs danuta hübner, is the creation of a practical guide to governance. it is no longer an abstract message, it must be a practical guide. secondly, the training of elected officials under an erasmus scheme. our local and regional elected representatives must be the real locomotives of this new governance of the territories. secondly, our european and national institutions must set an example. that is why i am asking in my report for an annual meeting of the ministers responsible for cohesion policy in the council. and then you, commissioner, as you know, there are differences between commissioners, between dgs... there is a need for more effective inter-service work. the committee of the regions has anticipated my request, since it already replied to our proposals two weeks ago. thirdly, we must of course have binding arrangements, commissioner. i have little time to develop them further, but i want you to know that we now expect the commission to spearhead this revolution in current practices. we must do what we say! i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this.
madam president, i would first like to congratulate our colleague, mr andersson, on his work. but what exactly does the european union want? a single market in which there is unbridled competition and which would crush all collective rights, or a single regulated market which would enable citizens to work in a decent way throughout the whole of europe? the messages from the european court of justice, often from the commission, sometimes from the president of the council, are neither clear nor always consistent. a company is only worth and survives by the contract it makes. deregulation, "every man for himself" leads to even more deregulation and the final explosion of the system. that is not what we want. a very good internal market! but a market as a means of improving the living and working conditions of our fellow citizens. the lisbon treaty sets out a number of principles, including the right to negotiate collective agreements. let us ensure that this principle is respected by the european union and all the member states.
president of the council. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is an honour for me to come before the european parliament once again to report on the work of the council presidency at such an important time for europe. if you will allow me, i will try to speak very freely, as is proper in this chamber, which is the heart of the democratic europe we want. what have we been trying to build? firstly, the presidency wanted the european institutions to be united in all the crises we have had to deal with. i wanted the european parliament to be involved in every moment of the great events we have experienced. and i want to thank the chairmen of your political groups, of all tendencies, who have played the game of dialogue and unity with the council presidency. i also wanted to work hand in hand with the commission, and particularly with its president, mr president of the european parliament, because whatever the differences or the divergences between all those who sit here, everyone knows that the division between the institutions of europe is a weakening of europe, and that the duty of those who assume responsibilities is to work hand in hand. europe will move forward if the european parliament, the commission and the council find a way of consensus on the major issues to make europe's voice heard. (applause) i would like to thank we wanted this europe to be united - which was not easy - to have independent thought, because the world needs the thought of europe, and to be a europe of will! if europe has something to say, let it not just say it, let it do it! first we had the war, with the completely disproportionate reaction of the russians in the georgian conflict. words have meaning. i use the word "disproportionate" because it was disproportionate to intervene as the russians did in georgia. (applause) but i use the word "reaction", because if this reaction was disproportionate, then there was a completely inappropriate action before. europe must be just and not hesitate to go beyond ideological schemes to bring a message of peace. on august 8, the crisis began. on august 12th, bernard kouchner and i were in moscow to obtain the ceasefire. i'm not saying it was perfect, i'm just saying that in four days, europe got a ceasefire. and in early september, europe got the commitment to withdraw to the lines that existed before the crisis of 8 august. in two months, europe had ended a war and had withdrawn its occupying forces! there were several theories. some said - and they had good reason to say - that dialogue was useless, and that the answer to military aggression must be military. this is crazy! europe has seen the fall of the berlin wall and the end of the cold war. europe must not be complicit in a new cold war simply because of a lack of restraint! but the important thing is that they start. i should also like to say that president medvedev has fulfilled the commitments he made to the presidency of the commission and the presidency of the european council when we visited moscow at the beginning of september. europe has made peace. europe has obtained the withdrawal of an occupying army and europe has wanted international talks. it seems to me that europe has not played such a role in a conflict of this nature for a long time! i see, of course, all the ambiguities, all the shortcomings, all the compromises that had to be made, but in my conscience i feel that we have achieved the maximum of what was possible and above all, mr president of the european parliament, that if europe had not made the voice of dialogue and the voice of reason heard, who would have made it heard? and when we left, with bernard kouchner, on 12 august for moscow and tbilisi, all the media in the world knew it well, the russians were forty kilometres from tbilisi and the objective was to overthrow the regime of mr saakashvili! that was the reality! we have come very close to disaster, but thanks to europe, a determined europe, this disaster has not happened, although, mr president pöttering, of course, the road to easing tensions in this part of the world will be long. secondly, the crisis. the financial crisis, systemic, incredible, implausible, which began let's say things as they are on september 15, not august 7, 2007. on august 7, 2007, a serious crisis began, a worrying one, but i dare say, a normal one. on august 15, 2008, we entered another crisis, because what happened on august 15, 2008? it's the lehman brothers collapse. and the world, in shock, learns on august 15, 2008, that a bank may fail! it is not our place, and it is not my place, to pass judgment on what the u.s. government has done or has not done. i simply say, and i assert, that on september 15, 2008, the serious crisis became a systemic crisis with the collapse of the american financial system, then the european financial system, then little by little other stock exchanges and financial systems. at that time, what did we try to do? there was the paulson i plan, which didn't work. it's not criticism just saying it, it's describing a reality. and at that time, with the president of the commission, we tried to build a common european response, first in the euro area. mr president, you have spoken about this, whether we are for or against, the fact remains that in the zone we have the same bank, the same currency, and therefore the same duty of unity! it was not easy to reach a common position. we have first proposed a meeting of the four european countries which are members of the g8. it is not an insult to anyone to say that the influence of the united kingdom, for example, on the world financial system is greater than that of any other country in the group of 27. and i thought that if we could, by some extraordinary fact, bring together english, german, italian and french, it would not be against other europeans, but for the service of other europeans. of course, there were different analyses - and who could blame us? - because in the first days of the crisis, it was not immediately clear what the right response was to a crisis unprecedented in economic history, at least in the 20th century. i thought that after all, after bringing the four together, we should bring together the eurogroup countries plus slovakia, which will join us. and that extra week allowed us to come up with, together, the solution that was to allow the banks to do their job again: lend. but we were in a solution where the banks stopped lending to each other, they had no money to lend and the whole system was collapsing. the nationalized banks in the united kingdom, the bankrupt banks in belgium, the collapse of the icelandic system - out of europe but so close to europe - the very bad news in switzerland and, little by little, the contagion: germany, france, all swept away! and we have managed, in the eurogroup, to agree on a gigantic plan 1.8 trillion euros to enable our financial institutions to do their job and to reassure european savers and entrepreneurs. then we went to the european council, which adopted the same strategy, and from that point on we were able to calm the markets in europe. the paulson ii plan arrived as a pleasant surprise and everyone could see that the paulson ii plan was very much inspired by the european plan. there is no glory to be gained from this, but simply to think: the crisis is global, the answer can only be global. the clock in the united states and the clock in europe must be the same. but all this is crisis management, mr president, nothing but crisis management. it's not over, and if we hadn't, what would have happened? but the real answers are yet to come. how could this have happened? how can we prevent this from happening again? and does europe have any ideas to defend, any policy to propose? and it was in this context that, on behalf of europe, at the united nations general assembly at the beginning of september, i proposed that an international summit be held to create the basis for a new bretton woods, in reference to what had happened in the aftermath of the second world war to bring about a new global financial system. this idea is progressing. what should be europe's objective in this summit? europe must carry the idea of a refoundation of world capitalism. what happened was a betrayal of the values of capitalism, not a challenge to the market economy. no rules, the reward of speculators at the expense of entrepreneurs! we must bring the idea of a new regulation. europe must and will put forward its ideas. firstly, no bank, mr president, which works with state money, can work with tax havens. (applause) mr president, no financial institution should be able to operate without being subject to financial regulation. i would like to see traders calculating and organizing their remuneration system in such a way as not to encourage the kind of reckless risk-taking we have seen. that our banks' accounting rules do not accuse the gravity of the crisis but, on the contrary, allow us to accompany it. that the monetary system be redesigned between fixed exchange rates and no exchange rates between currencies. we've tried everything in the world. can we, the rest of the world, continue to bear the deficits of the first world power without having a say? the answer is clearly no. (applause) i would like to thank it is not necessary to point out who is to blame, we simply need to find ways and means to prevent this from happening again. and then there are many other things to say, but i would like above all for europe to look at global governance in the 21st century. no wonder it doesn't work. we are in the 21st century and we have the institutions of the 20th century. the president of the united states and europe have therefore proposed several summits, starting in mid-november, which will focus on a new regulation, a new global governance. i hope that europe can debate this. i shall have the opportunity to propose to my partners, the heads of state and government, a meeting to prepare for these summits. the question of the re-foundation of our capitalism and our international system is a matter of common concern to the european parliament, which must debate it and put forward its ideas. but europe must speak with one voice if it is to have a chance of being heard. who will be attending the summit? there are many schools. i think the simplest thing is the g8, which is indisputable - with the russians, of course - to which we should add the g5, which is also indisputable and which will allow china and india, in particular, to be involved in this essential debate, and this will be the whole purpose of the visit we are making, with president barroso, to china, to convince the asian powers to participate in this refoundation. mr president, there has been a third subject during this presidency, which is extremely difficult: the future of the energy-climate package. i am well aware that your assembly and some of your groups are divided on what to do next. i would like to express my conviction and the policy i intend to propose. the ambitious energy-climate package is based on the belief that the world is headed for catastrophe if it continues to produce under the same conditions. that's the analysis! (applause) i would like to thank i don't see any argument that the world is better off, environmentally, because of the financial crisis. when we decided to embark on the energy-climate package, we did so with a sense of responsibility towards our children and the future of the planet. it is a structural policy, it is a historical policy, and it would be dramatic to abandon this policy on the pretext that the financial crisis has occurred. (applause) that would be dramatic and that would be irresponsible. why irresponsible? it would be irresponsible because it would send the signal that europe is not determined to make the efforts it has promised to make in this area and if europe does not make these efforts, our chances of convincing the rest of the world that the balances of the planet must be preserved are nil. so it is not simply europe's resignation for itself, it is the resignation of the whole world to the environmental appointment. because if europe is not an example, it will not be heard, respected and listened to. and if europe does not do this job, no one will do it for it! then we've missed our appointment with history. (applause) what does that mean, not being on a date? i think that means two things: firstly, we must look again at the objectives of the 'three times twenty'; the second is that we have to go back to the calendar, which is the end of the year. but i have no intention - and i have no power or will - to question the co-decision in any way. and besides, must you have bad thoughts for lending me this thought! and so we have a few weeks to convince a number of our partners, whose concerns i understand. because you don't create the conditions for compromise without trying to understand what the person who disagrees with you is saying! there are some economies that are 95 percent coal-based. we cannot ask them to do things that would bring them to their knees, when the difficulties are already immense. we must therefore find ways and means of being flexible, respecting the two red lines i proposed to the council: respect for the objectives and respect for the timetable. i shall have the opportunity, mr president, to explain this more fully in other places, perhaps, but i do not want to abuse your patience. i would like to say that this is what we have been wanting to do, and i hope that everyone will follow. a word on the fourth subject, the immigration pact, to say that i believe it is a good example of european democracy, that despite the differences at the outset, everyone was able to agree on a chosen immigration policy, in consultation with the countries of emigration, so that we draw the consequences of schengen which concern three quarters of the european countries. and if we have abolished visas between us, it is still reasonable that the countries which do not need visas to move from one to the other should have the same body of thought for a european immigration policy. two more points and i'll be done. the first is that the financial crisis has brought us an economic crisis. this economic crisis, it's here! there's no point in predicting it, since we're living it. i personally, as someone who is well aware of the disagreements between certain countries, cannot imagine being told that the financial crisis required a united european response and that the economic crisis did not require a united european response! a word about what "united" means. "one" doesn't mean the same answer! we have proposed a toolbox, a roadmap, harmonization, coordination for the financial crisis. well, i think that economic policy will need the same. this does not mean that we will all do the same, but it does mean that we have an obligation to talk about it, to inform each other and, on certain subjects, to agree. there are several leads. let me just say one thing: scholarships are at an all-time low. i would not like european citizens to wake up in a few months' time to find that european companies are owned by non-european capital, which has bought them at the lowest price on the stock exchange, at a low price, and which then owns them. european citizens would then ask: "what have you done?" i would ask each of us to consider the possibility of setting up sovereign wealth funds in each of our countries, and perhaps these national sovereign wealth funds could coordinate themselves from time to time to provide an industrial response to the crisis! i should add that i have been watching with great interest the american plan for the automobile industry: twenty-five billion dollars of interest rates at unbeatable prices to save the three american car manufacturers from bankruptcy. i would like to take a moment to reflect on this in europe. we are asking our manufacturers - and we are right - to build clean cars now, to completely change their production apparatus. as a result, thanks to the environmental bonus, 50% of the cars sold in my country are now clean cars! can the european car industry be left in a situation of serious distortion of competition with its american competitors without the question of european sectoral policies to defend european industry being raised? this does not mean that the single market should be called into question! this does not mean that the principle of competition should be called into question! this does not mean that the principle of state aid should be called into question! this means that europe must provide a united and not naive response to competition from the other major regions of the world. our duty is to ensure that europe can continue to build airplanes, ships, trains and cars because europe needs a strong industry. well, that's the policy the presidency will fight over! the last point is the institutions. i don't know if it's an "ah" of relief because i'm finishing my speech, or if it's because the other subjects were less important... the institutions are not the only european subject and it was a great mistake to devote too much attention exclusively to this issue! but institutions are a subject. i am convinced that the crisis calls for reform of the european institutions. the crisis presupposes that europe can respond as strongly and as quickly as any other global entity, such as the united states, has been able to respond to the financial crisis. i am one of those who think it would be a very serious mistake not to reform our institutions. it's very serious. and particularly because, to follow complicated issues like georgia and russia, the financial crisis, the economic crisis, it doesn't seem very reasonable to have a rotating presidency every six months. whatever we voted in the last elections, let me say that, frankly, if we love europe and if we want europe to speak with one voice, it does not seem reasonable to me to consider that every six months the presidency of the council must change. and so we will have to build a road map with president barroso for december to see how we can respond to the irish question. and i intend, before i leave the presidency of the council, to propose this road map and to indicate, by consensus, the ways and means of getting out of it. i would also like to say one last thing: the euro zone cannot continue without a clearly identified economic government. we can't go on like this! i want to pay tribute to the ecb's action. i mean my conviction that the ecb must be independent. but for the ecb's action to be fully effective, it must be able to discuss with an economic government. that was the spirit of the treaty! the spirit of the treaty is dialogue, democracy and mutual independence. and in my mind, moreover, the real economic government of the eurogroup is a eurogroup that meets at the level of heads of state and government! and how surprised i was when i asked for this meeting to be held for the first time since the euro was introduced! finally, frankly, we have a currency, we have a central bank, we have a single monetary policy and we have no economic government worthy of the name! the effort, commissioner almunia, to elect a chairman of the finance ministers - i was involved in the decision, i was myself finance minister at the time - is a salutary effort. and i want to pay tribute to the work of jean-claude juncker and to yours. but i want to say one thing: when the crisis takes on the proportions we know, the meeting of finance ministers alone does not measure up to the gravity of the crisis. and when it was necessary to mobilize the funds we have mobilized, it was not the money-changers who had to be mobilized, but the heads of state and government who alone had the democratic legitimacy to take on such heavy decisions. ladies and gentlemen, there is so much more to say! i would simply like to say in conclusion that the world needs a europe that speaks with a loud voice. it is on your shoulders, it is on the commission's shoulders, it is on the council's shoulders. and i would like to tell you all how useful it was for the presidency to feel, beyond the differences, the solidarity of a european parliament which had analysed from the beginning the seriousness of the crisis and which was ready - and i thank you for that - to overlook our differences of sensibility in order to create the conditions for the unity of europe. i wanted to tell you because i feel it very deeply. in writing. i voted in favour of the legislative resolution approving the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on insurance against civil liability in respect of the use of motor vehicles and on the enforcement of the obligation to insure against such liability, on the basis of the report by my british colleague diana wallis. this proposal is part of the consolidation of community law, which i think is improperly called codification. this is commendable, but i regret that, in view of the evolution and complexity of the texts, the commission did not revise its position of 1 april 1987 to instruct its departments to codify all legislative acts at the latest after their tenth amendment, while stressing that this was a minimum rule and that, in the interests of clarity and the proper understanding of community legislation, the departments should endeavour to codify the texts for which they are responsible at even shorter intervals. in this particular case, we are codifying various directives dating from 1972, 1983, 1990, 2000, 2005 and texts amending them. i believe that the policy of consolidating community law should be a priority for the european commission.

in writing. mr beaupuy's report is very informative. it talks about the governance of structural policy and shows that, far beyond a rebalancing of the levels of development of all the regions of the european union, the real aim of regional policy led by brussels is to change in depth the territorial organisation of the member states and thus their administrative and political structures. actually, that's not really a surprise. everything is being done in this europe to bypass or destroy the nation-states: from above, by entrusting its powers to the european superstate; from below, by promoting, against the traditions of certain states, against the natural or identity borders of the provinces, and with billions of euros, the "region" as a privileged level of infra-national organization or the constitution of infra-national transfrontier spaces. the 'integrated approach' of european legislation, which the rapporteur welcomes and which involves taking this dimension into account in all european policies with a territorial, economic and social impact, is contributing to this development. beyond the electoral manipulations, this is certainly the framework in which mr sarkozy's administrative reform project should be analysed.
in writing. the commission has just published its 24th annual report on its monitoring of the application of community law by the member states. the question that arises is whether there are any differences or improvements compared to the previous one. apparently not. the bad pupils of europe would therefore be the states as always! what is the rapporteur's solution? more and more firmness towards the states, more referral to the court of justice if necessary and more firmness in the implementation of the judgments given by the court of justice. in short: more powers of coercion and repression for the european institutions over the member states. the community legal order, which the treaties have already established as a higher standard than national rights, is now becoming more and more oppressive and destructive of the rights of the states. we are resolutely hostile, because the encroachment on national rights and the legal specificities of each one will inevitably lead to the encroachment of the states themselves on a europeanist and federalist whole.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on a strategy for the future implementation of the institutional aspects of the regulatory agencies, on the basis of the own-initiative report of my excellent colleague and friend, the former greek minister georgios papastamkos. it is regrettable that the efforts of parliament and the commission to establish a legally binding framework for european regulatory agencies have not produced any significant results. i share the view of the vast majority of my colleagues who deplore the lack of a general strategy for the creation of eu agencies and it is becoming urgent and necessary for the council and the commission to work together with parliament to establish a clear, common and coherent framework for the future role of agencies in european governance with the need for parliamentary control over the constitution and functioning of regulatory agencies.
in writing. the european union has 29 agencies, which are truly micro-institutions, costing over €1 billion and whose usefulness is questionable. the rapporteur is therefore right to call for more transparency and accountability in the management of these multiple agencies, for real political control over their activities, for an evaluation of existing agencies, for a moratorium on the creation of new ones, and for a cost-benefit analysis before any decision is taken. but the real problem is the very existence of these agencies, additional layers of european bureaucracy, some of which have regulatory powers, others executive functions that interfere with, if not complicate, the work of national administrations. the real problem is their proliferation, their dispersion across europe, their seats being distributed as so many patronising gifts. the real problem is that 40% of them are based on article 308 of the treaty, the famous article which allows for the extension of the powers of brussels when they are not expressly provided for in the texts. because this report solves nothing, we cannot approve it. but because it is, nevertheless, an attempt to put some order into this mess, we cannot reject it. that's why we're not going to vote.

in writing. i voted in favour of the legislative resolution amending the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on genetically modified micro-organisms (recast) on the basis of the report by my hungarian colleague jozsef szajer. i regret that, in view of the evolution and complexity of the texts, the commission did not revise its position of 1 april 1987 to instruct its departments to proceed with the codification of legislative acts at the latest after their tenth amendment, while stressing that this was a minimum rule and that the departments should endeavour to codify the texts for which they are responsible at even shorter intervals. in this particular case, we are revising the 1990 directive and the texts which amended it four times in 1994, 1998, 2001 and 2003. initially intended to be codified, directive 90/219/eec was finally recast to introduce the necessary amendments to adapt it to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny introduced in 2006. i believe that the policy of consolidating community law should be a priority for the european commission and the current situation is not normal, particularly with regard to the member states and the citizens.
in writing. i voted the legislative resolution approving, subject to amendments, the proposal for a council regulation amending the 2003 regulation as regards jurisdiction and establishing rules on the law applicable in matrimonial matters, on the basis of the report by my german colleague evelyne gebhardt. the increase in the mobility of citizens within the european union, which has led to an increase in the number of 'international' couples, i.e. couples in which the spouses are of different nationalities or reside in different member states or in a member state of which at least one of the spouses is not a national, and the high divorce rate in the european union, have made it necessary to legislate on the applicable law and on matrimonial jurisdiction, which affect an increasing number of citizens every year. it must be constantly recalled that the treaties provide for the progressive establishment of a common area of freedom, security and justice and for measures to 'promote the compatibility of the rules applicable in the member states in matters of conflict of laws and jurisdiction'.
in writing. the new legislation proposed concerns divorces for 'international couples', i.e. those whose spouses have different nationalities or reside in different states. the aim is to lay down the rules on the competent court and the applicable law in order to overcome the legal uncertainty in this area. the law applicable is currently determined by national conflict-of-law rules, which vary widely between member states and are complex. most member states determine the applicable law on the basis of attachment or residence criteria (lex loci). other states systematically apply their national law (lex fori), which can of course lead to the application of a law with which the spouses have only tenuous ties and to a result which does not comply with the requirement of legal certainty. the new regulation proposes harmonization of these conflict-of-laws rules. we are in favour of this because it should make this tragedy more predictable, and above all because it is in the interests of the safety of children who are too often victims of the disunity of their parents.

i'm the reporter. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to warmly congratulate the council, the commission and my colleagues, the fictitious rapporteurs, on their cooperation on this dossier of amendments to marketing authorizations for medicinal products. medicinal products, regardless of the procedure used for their marketing authorization, must be able to be subject to the same evaluation, approval and administrative treatment criteria in the event of modification. these changes, known as variations, concern, for example, manufacturing methods, the introduction of a new therapeutic indication, updating of the information sheets, or administrative changes. such variations must be reported to the competent authorities by the marketing authorization holders of a medicinal product. but the current management of variation is proving increasingly ineffective. it is no longer satisfactory, either for the authorities or for the pharmaceutical industry as a whole. there's too much red tape, at the expense of patients, who have delayed access to better medicines. the pharmaceutical industry devotes an increasingly important part of its regulatory work to managing these variations. for example, for a medium-sized company producing generic medicines with more than 400 products on its list, the total number of variations submitted is more than 4 000 per year. for a large company, this number can be as high as 19 000. amendments to purely national marketing authorisations follow specific provisions for each member state which differ from european regulatory requirements. since 80% of all medicines, both human and veterinary, are authorised through the national procedure, this review has a considerable impact on the pharmaceutical market in the european union. the same amendment concerning products authorised by national procedure in different member states is therefore treated differently as regards the dossier to be submitted and the evaluation procedure. this situation therefore has negative repercussions, i.e. it imposes an additional and unjustified administrative burden on the competent authorities and pharmaceutical companies, a difficulty in forecasting the implementation of the amendments, significant differences in the time-frame for the introduction of the amendments at the level of the summary of product characteristics and the package leaflet, for healthcare professionals and for patients, and thus has an impact on the overall functioning of the internal market for pharmaceutical products. finally, it is unfavourable to patients, since the introduction of certain modifications to improve the efficacy of a medicinal product may be delayed or, worse, not be introduced at all. the main purpose of my report is therefore to simplify and harmonize the rules on these variations in the marketing authorizations for medicinal products. with this directive, the situation will be simpler, clearer and more flexible for all actors. the rules on variations will be the same everywhere, regardless of the type of authorization, whether it is a national authorization, mutual recognition, or centralised recognition of the medicinal product. the simplification of these variations will result in their being subject to the same criteria for authorization, administrative management and monitoring of the changes introduced. it does not matter which legal procedure these drugs have been authorised by. i have also proposed a further improvement to the system where a change affects more than one marketing authorization. in such a case, it shall be possible to submit a single application covering all such mmfs. i know, mr president, that the commissioner is going to speak to us about the counterfeiting of medicines. we are very much looking forward to his statement because it is important that this package, which includes the counterfeiting of medicines, can be offered to us. we've been waiting for this for a long time. counterfeiting is a crime, and it's a public health issue. it is important that the commissioner can tell us where he stands because we are looking forward to this text and, in any case, we give it our full support.

in writing. the report by mr andresson seeks to draw lessons from the scandalous judgments of the luxembourg court of justice, notably in the laval and viking cases. these judgments give priority to the free provision of services and the freedom of establishment of undertakings over the defence of the interests and rights of national workers against social dumping. they unacceptably subordinate the exercise of social rights to a 'principle of proportionality' which goes far beyond the legitimate restrictions (e.g. public order and health) recognised in national law and ilo conventions. they are a disguised re-establishment of the bolkenstein directive in its first version, the one where the law of the country of origin (social law, labour law, wage law, etc.) applied to the worker going to work in another member state, irrespective of the legislation or collective agreements in force in the latter. this version has been rejected by the european legislator and it is unacceptable that judges can pretend to be the authors of the law under the guise of interpreting it. even if he is sometimes well-meaning, mr andersson is too attached to the ultra-liberal principles which have led to this situation for his report to win the vote. that's why we're not going to vote.

madam president, from lenin's soviet russia to kim il-sung's north korea, today, mao's china, mengistu's ethiopia, pol pot's cambodia - and this list is, alas, not exhaustive - it can be said that hunger is the very essence of communism. however, the famine that killed nearly 10 million ukrainians in 1932 and 1933 was not just the result of the economic and social absurdity of communism, nor of its hatred of the peasantry. but it was planned by the soviet authorities, who on the one hand requisitioned all the peasants' food stocks, including seeds, and on the other hand used the police to prevent, by all means, the mass departures of ukrainians who were trying to escape death. this is what is happening in north korea today. article 6 of the statute of the international criminal court defines genocide as the intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnic, racial or religious group as such and also, i quote, "the intentional subjection of the group to conditions which are to result in its physical destruction, in whole or in part". the extermination by famine - the holodomor - decided by the soviet communists in 1932 fits this definition, and mr markov is not pleased about it. on november 28, 2006, the ukrainian parliament officially declared the holodomor genocide. it is regrettable that the united nations, because of the russian veto and the cowardice of the french and british governments, refused to give it this status. it does not, moreover, call into question the honour of the russian people, who were also victims of communism, but it denounces the horror of this totalitarianism, which killed 200 million people in the world, and which we are denouncing today, it must be said, very belatedly.
madam president, we talking about this man-made famine now, 75 years after the events, because, if we do not talk about itnow,then it could become like the dark midnight of justice. it is still two hours to midnight now, but we are building the future. we cannot build that future on wobbly foundations. it has to be built on a solid foundation, and a solid foundation means the truth. the future cannot be built on lies, which would be like building it on sand. it does not really matter how many people died in the ukraine. what matters is that the victims of that man-made famine–the ukrainian populace –feel that justice is being done, because we have to restore people’s faith in justice. otherwise we cannot build a just society and they cannot believe in a future. all victims’ cries have to be heard, regardless of whether they are the victims of nazism, apartheid, slavery or communism. this house stands for the fundamental values of humanity. we cannot send out an ambiguous message. that is why we have to be truly unbiased, however painful that might be politically for us. otherwise we are not defending human dignity. it is very alarming that, in russia today, history is being rewritten, so how can we build a common future? it is a fitting time for us to discuss ukraine now, because at this very moment, in 2008, ukraine needs help. it needs hope for a better future, which means accession to the eu one day.

in writing. having a european budget of around €130 billion for 27 countries, the equivalent of spain's budget alone, is, in normal times, already a curiosity. but now, in a europe where there is a shortage of high-speed trains from finland to spain or from france to poland, as well as of equipment and staff for the universities, research centres and retirement homes of a continent overwhelmed by the tsunami of old age, the global crisis of interbank liquidity, the property shock in several economies and the decline in the confidence of entrepreneurs and workers are demanding a budgetary effort without any measure with the usual european budget. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. this is a continental loan, equivalent to the €1.7 trillion raised for the banking sector.

in writing. our assembly finally recognises the horror of the extermination by famine, the holodomor, in ukraine, caused by the soviet regime. it is regrettable, however, that it has not, like the ukrainian parliament, given the qualification of genocide to this mass crime. the famine that killed millions of ukrainians in 1932 and 1933 was not only the result of the economic and social absurdity of communism but was the result of a plan of extermination that met the definition of genocide, that is, "the intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnic, racial or religious group as such", and also "the intentional subjecting of the group to conditions that would result in its total or partial physical destruction". at a time when in france in particular a certain extreme left communist group is receiving support from the media, the recognition of such a genocide would be a reminder of the horror of marxism-leninism, which has been responsible for the death of 200 million people since the bolshevik revolution of 1917 and which today still oppresses more than one and a half billion people in cuba, north korea, vietnam and especially in china, where the most savage capitalism marries very well with communist totalitarianism.

member of the commission. − mr president, the commission is following the situation in venezuela with great interest. the country is in the process of preparing for the regional and local elections which will take place on 23 november. it is worth noting that in the last few years several democratic electoral processes have taken place in venezuela. some of them have been monitored by european observation missions which concluded that, in general, they complied with international standards and national legislation. others have not, as was the case with the last referendum, since we were not invited. the commission is aware of the concerns expressed by some of you and also many sectors of venezuelan society about the constitutionality of the ‘disqualifications’. these are believed by some to be intended to obstruct the full participation of the opposition in the november elections. the commission has taken note of the explanation provided on several occasions by the venezuelan authorities, in relation to the constitutionality of these ‘administrative sanctions’ imposed by the state controller on a number of civil servants. we stress the importance of guaranteeing the rights of all citizens who want to participate in the elections, in accordance with the constitution and the rule of law. we hope that the upcoming elections will strengthen democracy in venezuela and that the results will reflect the views of the whole of venezuelan society. we encourage all actors to engage in the electoral process in a spirit of tolerance, civic-mindedness and respect for pluralism of opinions. the commission is also aware of the expulsion of the representatives of human rights watchfrom venezuela. we have heard the voices which have condemned this decision as a measure which adversely affects the right to freedom of expression and an act demonstrating an intolerant attitude towards criticism. in this context, we stress the importance that the eu attaches to freedom of expression and opinion. freedom of expression is one of the fundamental human rights, and constitutes the cornerstone of democracy and the rule of law. i wish to assure parliament that the commission will continue to follow closely the developments in venezuela. the commission’s commitments to supporting development of democracy and the promotion of human rights will continue to be reflected in our cooperation policies and relations with venezuela.

member of the commission.− mr president, the commissionshares the concerns about the degraded situation in the eastern democratic republic of congo, which is causing further stress to an already seriously affected population. it is also particularly worried about the widespread human rights violations in the region, including violence against women and the continuous mobilisation of child soldiers in the conflict. the commission restates its conviction that the current crisis involving kinshasa and the congolese rebel groups has no military solution. hence, we encourage all parties to this conflict to rapidly resume dialogue and promote courageous political compromises, taking into consideration the commitments agreed upon in january2008, the so-called actes d’engagement de goma. in this context, it is extremely important to restore acceptable confidence levels amongst all congolese stakeholders directly involved. as a preliminary step, all parties without exception should abide without delay by an effective ceasefire with a view to implementing the military disengagement plan provided by the united nations. in addition, it must be borne in mind that the underlying root causes of the conflict also include the dramatic problems posed by foreign armed groups in democratic republic of congoterritory, in particular the rwandan fdlr, an issue where most of the drc commitments taken in the nairobi communiqué have still to be put into action. given the multiple challenges which still lie ahead in the democratic republic of congo, the commission strongly advocates that the un’s peacekeeping mission mandate should be renewed and, where possible, strengthened in order to ensure effective protection for the population and support to the congolese army in tackling the foreign armed groups. in addition to the relentless efforts of the eu facilitation team, it is important to ensure the broader participation of african diplomacy (including the african union) in the resolution of the eastern drc conflicts, especially in areas where a sustainable solution would be greatly facilitated by close cooperation between neighbouring countries, in particular the democratic republic of congo and rwanda. as regards our support to the population in conflict-affected areas, the commission will continue to provide support via both our humanitarian and development cooperation. more specifically, regarding health services (an issue raised by all the resolutions), it is important to stress that the commission has been active since 1994 in the health sector in the democratic republic of congo, which is today one of the focal sectors of our cooperation. in addition to humanitarian aid, we are currently providing strategic and financial support to the congolese authorities to improve the quality of medical services and the qualifications of medical staff.

member of the commission. − mr president, i would like to start by reminding you that the commission’s response to the cyclone last may was quick and substantial. we provided humanitarian and food aid in writing. on 13 october 1981, in the french national assembly, andré laignel, a socialist mp, gave his famous reply to the opposition mps, arguing against the constitutionality of the nationalisations desired by the government: "your debate switches from legal to political. it's [your] right. but in this case you are legally wrong, since you are politically in the minority". the european parliament has clearly adopted this phrase when it comes to eliminating all those who dare to disturb it with their political views which are not considered sufficiently federalist or europeanist to its liking. my colleague, frank vanhecke, is the subject of a real witch hunt in this european parliament, from which he was legitimately elected. this institution has been misled and disgraced by accepting the unacceptable: the lynching of one of its members in defiance of all legal principles and legal protections relating to parliamentary immunities currently in force.
in writing. like many texts in this assembly, ms iotova's report is an example of a seemingly good idea with a misleading title. a superficial reading might suggest that this is about protecting consumers by informing them of their rights and educating them about financial services, in short, making them responsible and informed interlocutors of their bank. in reality, it is a question of making them from an early age (from primary school, it seems) perfect little customers of a financial system eager for their savings but stingy with its loans, of accepting as normal any financial product that pseudo-initiates call complex and which, for the most part, are simply aberrant, of doing their accounts wisely and preparing their retirement (with banks!) even if they also contribute to compulsory public systems ... at a time when the world financial system has just shown its perversity, when banks are reluctant to grant loans to companies and individuals despite the hundreds of billions of public aid released, when workers and smes are paying the price of a financial madness that is still current and when the "big" of the planet pretend to commit reforms to make the system last longer, the least we can say is that this report does not convince us.
in writing. the 'overall positive' assessment of the 10 years of economic and monetary union by the rapporteurs does not seem to be entirely objective, to say the least. unsurprisingly, the few problems identified are analysed as being the fault of the states and a lack of european integration. the truth is that the introduction of the euro has mechanically led to the explosion of prices of everyday consumer goods and the decline in the purchasing power of workers. the truth is that the stability pact is a fiscal and social malthusianism. the truth is that the absence of an exchange rate policy and the overvaluation of the euro have undermined the international competitiveness of the euro area. the truth is that a single monetary policy, a single policy interest rate for 11 or 15 economies of very different structures and levels of development are necessarily unsuitable for the needs of each of these economies as well as for the needs of the whole. the euro has failed to bring the prosperity promised to its members, most of whom are now in recession. because the euro, in its design and functioning, is not an economic tool. it is above all a powerful political tool for destroying the independence of nations.

madam president, mr president-in-office of the council, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, as has been said many times, the automobile industry directly or indirectly represents 12 million jobs in the european union. this is 10% of european gdp. the automobile industry is therefore facing a serious crisis: the european market is down by 15%. the commission has also proposed that the rate of inflation be reduced to 17% to 20% in the last quarters of 2008. manufacturers' profits are down. in this context, the lack of liquidity becomes the main risk for this industry. as a result, manufacturers are reducing production and trying to reduce structural costs. employment is the first victim of the crisis. as you said, mr president, in the face of this crisis, the response must be coordinated between europe and the member states, particularly those directly concerned. the proposed eib financial support is necessary. i naturally agree with your proposals. the first is to support investment, particularly in the design and manufacture of clean vehicles and the development of hybrid and electric vehicles. the aim is also to support the market by providing financial incentives for the renewal of the park. as the commissioner said, old cars are responsible for a large part of the pollution generated by cars. but we also need a stable, ambitious but realistic regulatory framework. the objectives on co2 emissions must be maintained, and the industry has devoted and is devoting considerable resources to them, but realism must lead to a moderation of the penalties for failure to meet the objectives. excessive penalties would kill the general contractors. the automobile industry is one of the most environmentally sensitive industries. finally, in the present circumstances, it would be detrimental to manufacturers if the protection of exterior body parts were to be undermined.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am particularly pleased that our legislative debate today is devoted to legal immigration, allowing us to participate in a debate which is not clear choice: to promote a common immigration policy that encourages legal, economic immigration, managed effectively according to the needs of national markets. so we are debating two major pieces of legislation today, pragmatic pieces of legislation, which are supposed to meet clearly defined labour needs in our member states. by adopting these two texts simultaneously, the european parliament is immigration. we have nothing to be ashamed of in our choices in this area and we have nothing to learn from the leaders of third countries who are unable to pursue appropriate policies to prevent their populations from risking their lives to find better conditions in europe. to focus on the single procedure directive for which i am the rapporteur, firstly, the proposal introduces a one-stop-shop system for third country nationals who wish to reside in a member state in order to work there. it provides for a single application procedure which is simpler, shorter and faster for administration and employers to check the validity of the titles. secondly, the proposal for a directive will ensure equal treatment for all third country nationals in a number of areas. the recognition of the fundamental social and economic rights of immigrants legally present in the territories of the european union and of newcomers will contribute to the improvement of their integration and thus to a better social cohesion. equal treatment concerns working conditions, health, safety at the workplace, education, vocational training, recognition of qualifications, social security, including health care, export of pensions, access to goods and services and tax benefits. realistic restrictions are indeed envisaged, but we will ensure that they are not wider than what is provided for in the 'blue card'. the interests of immigrants must be taken into account and their rights must be protected. the figures show that the unemployment rate of immigrants is higher than that of eu citizens, that they often have precarious jobs and that the language of the host country remains a major barrier. the two texts proposed by the commission, for whose good sense i am
