in writing. on the basis of my distinguished colleague and friend, the german ingeborg grassle, i voted for the legislative resolution approving, subject to amendments, the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1073/1999 concerning investigations by the european anti-fraud office (olaf). i support improving the protection of the rights of persons under investigation by olaf and strengthening cooperation with member states. it became essential to establish public governance of olaf's anti-fraud investigation activities and the need for independent control of the procedures and duration of investigations, while ensuring the protection of the confidentiality of investigations. inge grassle has done a great deal of work with this report, and we should thank her for it.
in writing. mrs stauner, the rapporteur, makes a lucid analysis of the challenges that the ageing of our populations and the decline of our working populations pose to our social protection systems, to which she seems committed. that's a good first point for her. a second good point is the timid question it raises about the real effectiveness of the usual panacea, namely the mass settlement of immigrant workers who are expected to pay for pensions and health care for the elderly in europe. it is also characterized by a stunning cynicism and selfishness, and is championed by people who often claim to have a monopoly on love and tolerance. finally, a final point for his critical analysis of the trend towards privatisation of health systems and the purely financial approach to reforms of national social security systems. but the report misses the point: since the demographic decline of our continent is at the root of these problems, it is this that must be remedied. the member states can no longer afford to have an ambitious family and maternity policy, which is no doubt a guarantee of the balance of their social security, but above all of their dynamism, their prosperity and, quite simply, their survival.
in writing. the stauner report, although it refers to the lisbon strategy, a blatantly europeanist failure, deserves support because it calls into question the credo of immigration as a remedy against the future worsening of europe's demographic, economic and social deficits. whether chosen or not, immigration distorts the identity and culture of the peoples of europe, it aggravates communitarianism and the resulting tensions, as is the case in all multiethnic and multicultural societies in the world. it is a neo-slavery for the sole benefit of the globalist predators who see in this cheap labour the means to put pressure on wages in a context of already very high unemployment. it will allow the plundering of the elites of third countries, making their situation even worse. it is a strategic decoy, since the behaviour of immigrants will inevitably end up being modelled on that of europeans, i am thinking in particular of the unfortunate tendency to have fewer children in a society, it is true, which is confused in every respect. in addition to support for families and european births, the new europe of nations needs a policy of national and community preference, a policy of national and community protection.
in writing. i voted for the klamt report on the creation of a european blue card because it offers us, for the first time, the opportunity at european level to move from a culture of 'no', that of fortress europe, to a culture of 'yes', that of an open europe, in order to develop a positive management of migration flows and to recognise a number of rights for workers. it is important that this process be continued rapidly by adopting further measures in favour of other categories of foreign workers. i'll be careful. we could have gone further, of course, and would have preferred a horizontal directive rather than a sectoral directive, but there are some achievements, including the principle of equal pay for equal work, the rejection of brain drain, particularly in key sectors such as health and education, and the doubling of the period of residence permitted for the purpose of seeking a new job after the end of an employment contract. the aim of this text is therefore to promote legal immigration channels and certainly not a selected form of immigration, which i am opposed to.
in writing. the european blue card, supposedly reserved for highly skilled workers, offering its beneficiaries freedom of movement and establishment in all the member states of the european union, will be a new vacuum pump for immigration that will be no more controlled at the union level than it is today in many countries at the national level. it will encourage permanent settlement immigration by providing an instantaneous right to family reunification without any real time limit. it is the bureaucratic organization of the new modern slavery, which now chooses its victims on the basis of their qualifications, not on the basis of their muscles or their teeth. it will deprive developing countries of the brains they so badly need, worsening their economic situation and ensuring the endless pursuit of ever-increasing illegal immigration. it introduces a totally aberrant and arbitrary minimum wage threshold, which takes no account of reality, the sectors or the trades concerned. the twofold consequence is foreseeable: the lowering of the wages of the most highly qualified europeans, who will be even more tempted than today to emigrate outside europe; the exploitation of immigrants, with no guarantee for them to obtain wages really commensurate with their qualifications.
in writing. the speeches by mr jean-pierre jouyet, president of the council, and mr jacques barrot, vice-president of the commission, during the debate on the european blue card and the single permit combining residence and work authorization were very demonstrative. petit florilège: 'these texts show the true scope of the pact on immigration and asylum, which the french presidency has made possible, and they prove that this pact is indeed balanced and that it also shows the willingness of europeans to open up to these migratory flows which can be particularly useful and prove very positive for the future of our european society' (sic jacques barrot). "the possibility of returning to one's country of origin for two years without losing longterm resident status is essential" (sic jacques barrot). "these two texts are a beginning and not an end, and they do leave room for circular migration" (sic jean-pierre jouyet). "these two texts demonstrate that the union is genuinely committed to promoting legal migration" (sic pierre jouyet). there can now be no doubt that our leaders and our french representatives to the european institutions are the proponents of a massive extra-european immigration of people leading to policies of national disintegration. we will vote against it.
in writing. mrs klamt's report on the conditions for entry and residence in the european union of third-country nationals for the purpose of highly skilled employment starts from a simple observation in order to reach incorrect conclusions. it is true that skilled immigrants from outside the community prefer to emigrate to the united states or canada rather than to europe. to try to reverse the trend and bring them into our house is a worrying masochism and loss of lucidity. can we not train engineers, computer scientists, doctors to bring them from the third world? is it humanly acceptable to loot the brains of countries which absolutely need such qualified personnel to develop? do you think that by encouraging the kind of immigration that mr sarkozy wants, we will stop legal immigration and especially illegal immigration? the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the answer to these questions is to point out the danger of such a europe committing, in this case, a real crime against humanity against the third world. we cannot therefore vote for such a report.
in writing. the 'european blue card', a veritable sesame meant to create additional extra-european skilled immigration, will be an economic, social and human catastrophe for the peoples and nations of europe already suffering from uncontrollable illegal immigration and exponentially growing legal immigration to avoid the inevitable social dumping which would result from the arrival of engineers or other specialists with degrees from other continents, the planned wage must be at least 1.7 times the minimum wage of the host country: the french worker will appreciate... the immigrant worker can also bring his family with him under an accelerated procedure, thus promoting family reunification, which is already important and dangerous. in addition, the immigrant will be able to accumulate his periods of presence in the european territory in order to obtain long-term resident status. the circle is complete: the conditions for mass settlement and naturalisation in the member states are met! the scandal is also that this will exacerbate the "brain drain" of third countries, especially africa, by capturing their elites. a further impoverishment of these countries is guaranteed. once again, the people of europe will not be consulted on this globalist and immigration policy of brussels. more than ever, our fight must be for the sovereignty of nations and the right of peoples to remain themselves.
in writing. on the basis of the report by my friend, mr patrick gaubert, i voted for a legislative resolution approving, subject to amendments, the proposal for a council directive establishing a single application procedure for the issue of a single permit for third-country nationals to reside and work in the territory of a member state and establishing a common set of rights for third-country workers legally resident in a member state. i would like to commend patrick gaubert for his important work on this sensitive subject, which is aimed at making efforts to develop a comprehensive european immigration policy. it made sense to work on the common basis of rights to be granted to all third-country workers who are already legally resident in a member state, as well as on a procedural aspect, namely the issuing of a single permit following a single application procedure.
in writing. the european parliament has just adopted by a very large majority two reports on the admission of migrant workers to european countries, demonstrating europe's real capacity to put in place concrete instruments for the concerted management of economic migration flows. the adoption of my report on the single procedure for the granting of residence and work permits formally contradicts the unfounded accusations of a number of african and latin american heads of state of a closed-in 'fortress europe'. " the european parliament has voted in favour of the commission's proposal to establish a european agency for fundamental rights. these decisions will help to improve their integration, migrant workers are not a threat to our labour markets. the blue card report will make it easier for graduates and highly skilled migrants to enter the labour markets of the eu countries, thanks to more attractive reception conditions. europe is demonstrating that it is capable of a dignified, firm and open immigration policy.
in writing. mr gaubert wants to 'bring a message of europe's openness to legal immigration', by granting legal immigrants all kinds of rights, by restricting the possibility for member states to limit the full equality of treatment between european nationals and immigrants from member states, in short, by organising a european positive discrimination obligation. mr gaubert should rest assured that it is well known in all the countries of emigration that europe is a real sieve. each year hundreds of thousands of legal and illegal immigrants enter the country, attracted not by the prospect of work (in france only 7% of legal immigrants enter for this purpose), but by the prospect of benefiting from the ever-increasing number of social benefits and other rights offered to them and sometimes even reserved for them. and this without any demands being made on them in return, or even a minimum knowledge of the language of the host country, if you listen to mr gaubert. at a time when our countries are entering recession, when our economic and social models are being undermined by globalisation, when the number of unemployed and working poor in europe is exploding, it is urgent to call instead for the application of the principle of national and community preference in all areas.
in writing. i am deeply sorry that the excellent motion for a resolution on the future of european space policy, which has just been voted, makes no reference to the kourou space centre. yet, guyana is inevitably central to europe's space history. it's so obvious to everyone, that we don't even think to note that all the ariane rockets are assembled there and all of them have been launched since that launch. i thank the french presidency, represented by mr jean-pierre jouyet, who had the presence of mind to mention this during our debate yesterday. in my view, the european space strategy must absolutely include a genuine reflection on the future developments of the 'spaceport of europe', both in terms of infrastructure and manpower and research projects. kourou is the showcase of europe's space. guyana, the union's outermost region, deserves to be commended for its past and future contribution to this strategic policy. i would have liked to see our parliament pay tribute to the guiana space centre and express explicitly the pride it inspires in all europeans. in a few decades, the kourou has become a major component of our european identity.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, on behalf of the commission and commissioner michel, i wish to share some remarks about this issue of human rights in somalia. firstly, i would like to share the concern about the continuing conflict and political instability in somalia. somalia remains a context where fundamental rights and respect for basic human dignity continue to be shunned by armed entities perpetrating systematic and widespread attacks against civilians. in the last few months, an escalating wave of attacks on humanitarian workers, peace activists and human rights defenders has been sweeping southern and central somalia. at least 40 somali human rights defenders and humanitarian workers were killed between january and september 2008 alone. as a result of these attacks, a number of humanitarian organisations have been forced to withdraw staff from mogadishu; humanitarian access received further blows; and human rights and humanitarian conditions further deteriorated. the commission, together with the member states and other international actors, is committed to helping at this critical juncture. the eu supports the efforts of the office of the high commissioner for human rights, including the independent expert on human rights in somalia, shamsul bari, to come to the creation of a mechanism to investigate systematic human rights abuses by all parties. at the development level, the eu is strongly involved in supporting human rights organisations, mainly in training and funding for identification, documentation, monitoring of human rights abuses, and advocacy. in particular, the commission is increasingly involving civil society in any programme of reconstruction and national reconciliation, including exchange programmes for civil society with other regional organisations, paralegal training, public awareness campaigns, and women’s groups’ work on enhancing their political representation and participation in reconciliation processes. moreover, the eu supports programmes focusing on law enforcement and reinforcing the judiciary. meanwhile, we need to work to improve security and to make the somali reconciliation process move forward. a climate of insecurity will only serve to worsen the human rights situation and encourage violations of international humanitarian law. any lasting peace in somalia must be based on accountability and justice for the human rights violations committed by all sides throughout the somali conflict.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place at the end of the debate. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, since its independence, nigeria has enjoyed only three periods of civilian rule and has endured 29 years of military rule. nine years ago, nigeria took a step towards democracy and came back to civilian rule, even though all elections since then have been widely criticised for irregularities, fraud and violence. the april 2007 elections could have set a good example for other countries, but the opportunity was missed and the new government took up office amidst doubts of legitimacy. it is in this context, and bearing in mind the importance of a stable nigeria for africa, that a suitable strategy has to be found to engage the government there in a constructive dialogue over human rights. the commission fully shares the concerns expressed by honourable members on the issue of the death penalty, and agrees with the need, pending complete abolition of the death penalty, to declare an immediate moratorium on all executions. at the same time, it should be acknowledged that the situation of human rights in nigeria has generally improved since the return to civilian rule. indeed, some steps have been taken to launch a debate in the country over the usefulness of the death penalty as a deterrent to heinous crimes. several prisoners on death row have been pardoned this year and nigeria has committed itself to an intensified high level political dialogue with the eu which covers, inter alia, human rights issues. the commission has contributed significantly to starting this process, which could lead to a global eu political strategy vis-à-vis nigeria, and which has already led to an important ministerial troika and to a comprehensive joint communiqué. in the context of this dialogue, it will be possible to discuss constructively human rights issues, and to undertake a range of cooperation activities in crucial sectors such as peace and security, and governance and human rights. examples of cooperation initiatives under consideration include: support for improving the investigative capacity of the nigerian police; access to justice and support for prison reform; support for anticorruption efforts; support for the democratic process; and support for federal institutions dealing with human trafficking, illicit drugs, human rights and counterfeited medicines. to be effective, these actions will have to be made known to civil society and ordinary citizens. the commission will develop a strategy, based on a combination of support for local mass media and cultural initiatives, to support sensitive cooperation initiatives and to disseminate to the public educational messages concerning respect for human rights and basic freedoms, the basic values of democracy, good governance, care for the environment and so forth.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place at the end of the debate. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.

member of the commission. − mr president, madam member, ladies and gentlemen, the first european roma summit, held in brussels on 16 september, was of fundamental importance for the partnership between all the key players in this field. more than 500 senior representatives from the eu institutions, member states and civil society attended, and it reflected our renewed commitment to step up efforts to tackle social exclusion of roma. he made it clear that the overall objective must be the full participation of roma in the economic, social and cultural life of europe and equal opportunities for everyone in the eu, including roma. civil society must be fully involved in this partnership. this means that roma must be involved in the design, implementation and monitoring of policies that affect them. the commission therefore welcomes the contributions of civil society to the roma summit, such as the statement of the eu roma policy coalition. this year, an unprecedented step forward in the area of roma inclusion was achieved through joint efforts by the eu and member states and cooperation based on mutual trust and goodwill. the commission's main conclusions from the summit were: a commitment to promote the individual rights of roma men, women and children; recognition that promoting roma inclusion is a shared responsibility of the eu and the member states in their respective fields of competence; recognition of the eu's role in supporting member states in implementing their policies through coordination and financial support from the structural funds; consensus that culturally sensitive approaches targeting roma should be promoted, but that they should not exclude other similarly disadvantaged members of society and should seek to mainstream roma in educational, employment and social terms. the commission also made clear at the summit that it would take all necessary steps within its remit to improve the situation of roma and ensure that they could fully enjoy the fundamental rights guaranteed by the charter. in the event of a breach of community law, including fundamental rights, the commission will not hesitate to intervene. following the summit conclusions, president barroso and i proposed the creation of a platform for roma inclusion. this would provide a framework for, for example, high-level bilateral meetings, so that financial instruments supporting cohesion and rural development policies can be better targeted at roma inclusion. in addition, the platform could be a concrete fulfilment of the commission's commitment to make community instruments and policies more effective and to report on the results achieved. following the conclusions of the june european council, member states should now assess the results achieved so far and intensify their efforts to achieve full roma inclusion. the commission will of course support the member states. in addition, the commission looks forward to the general affairs council meeting on 8 december, where draft conclusions on roma inclusion will be discussed.

in writing. on the basis of the report by my distinguished spanish colleague josé manuel garcia-margallo y marfil, i voted in favour of the proposal for a council directive amending the 2006 proposal on the common system of value added tax to combat tax evasion in intra-community transactions. at present, the system for the exchange of information on intra-community supplies of goods established under the transitional vat arrangements adopted on the occasion of the transition to the internal market is no longer sufficient to deal effectively with tax evasion linked to intra-community transactions. it should be noted that the measure is part of a package of measures, some of which are explicitly aimed at increasing legal certainty for companies and reducing their administrative burdens, as well as significantly improving the exchange of information and cooperation between tax administrations. i supported the amendments that two years after the directive enters into force the commission should draw up a report assessing the effects of the directive, particularly on the administrative costs of the new obligations for the taxable persons concerned and on the degree of effectiveness of these obligations in the fight against tax fraud.
in writing. we voted against the two reports by mr garcía-margallo y marfil on the 'fight against tax fraud in intra-community transactions', that is to say, in plain english, vat fraud in trade between member states. of course we condemn this fraud and support intergovernmental cooperation between the national services concerned. but the rapporteur's proposal goes much further, with the creation of a single 'european tax base' available to national administrations to gather information on those who have been involved in fraud in one way or another and to prohibit them from setting up or running a business anywhere in europe. in what name? is it a judicial, administrative or arbitrary decision? what's the level of the shot? on the basis of what powers - defined or not in this case - by the treaties? the supremacy of the european level, the self-assignment of quasi-criminal powers, the oversized executive role of the european commission, the increase in the bureaucratic burden on companies at a time when we are talking about a 'small business act' in the european style ...: all this does not suit us.
in writing. on the basis of the report by my distinguished spanish colleague josé manuel garcia-margallo y marfil, i voted in favour of the proposal for a council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1798/2003 with a view to combating tax fraud in connection with intra-community transactions. the commission will have to centrise information on the actions taken by member states to combat fraud, disclose those which have produced the best results and propose the measures it deems most appropriate to remedy fraudulent behaviour. the commission will develop a set of indicators to distinguish the areas where the risk of tax evasion is highest. national tax administrations must be inspired by the need to tackle fraud and help honest taxpayers to meet their obligations. on the basis of the data collected for the evaluation of the functioning of the regulation, the commission will have to establish a set of indicators to determine the extent to which each member state will cooperate with the commission and with the other member states, providing them with the available information and the necessary assistance to remedy fraud. the member states and the commission will have to periodically assess the application of the regulation.
in writing. having voted on the joint resolution tabled by four political groups, including the epp-de, on measures to improve the environment for small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in the small business act (sba) for europe, i would like to commend the immense work done by my french colleague nicole fontaine and the french presidency with minister christine lagarde. it is becoming urgent that member states confirm their intention to formally endorse the sba at the brussels european council in december 2008 in order to ensure its necessary visibility while making its provisions legally binding, in order to allow for a real positive effect on the sme environment. smes are at the heart of a very important part of the economic fabric and have an undeniable social vocation to be human-sized enterprises. but they are fragile and deserve special attention. in the interests of the european union's wealth-producing system, it is imperative that smes be supported.
in writing. we voted in favour of the resolution on improving the environment for smes under the small business act. because we are aware, and we have been saying this for years, of the crucial economic role of smes, the main creators of wealth and jobs. the problem is that all of this is still in the virtual realm today. it is the same institution, the commission, which calls on the states to 'think of small businesses first', but which multiplies the cumbersome and incomprehensible legislation and the administrative and regulatory constraints. it is the commission which, despite its duty, fails to carry out the impact studies which must accompany its legislative proposals. it is the commission which has put in place the policy of access to public contracts which leads to the systematic ousting of local smes in favour of large european companies, in the name of sacrosanct competition. it was the commission, obsessed with tax harmonization, which imposed the present constraints on vat rates. yes, it is time to finally give priority to all these small businesses, their managers and employees, and to think about this first and foremost in european regulations.
in writing. i voted in favour of the joint resolution tabled by six political groups on the eu code of conduct on arms exports. i agree with the principles of preventing irresponsible arms exports by strict application of the code criteria to both businesses and national armed forces, and of preventing illegal arms trafficking by inviting those member states which have not yet done so to transpose the 2003 eu common position on arms control into their national legislation. we must encourage investigations into violations of arms embargoes and improve the quality of the data provided by member states in the annual report on the code of conduct. that said, let us not be naive and in the complex and dangerous world in which we live, these issues are sensitive and that is why i have stood up to oppose the oral amendment by my colleague mr pflüger which, in my view, links too quickly the code of conduct with the implementation of the future directive on intra-community exports of defence equipment and the control of arms exports.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my belgian colleague bart staes on the european court of auditors' special report no 8/2007 on administrative cooperation in the field of value added tax (vat). while the court's special report is to be welcomed, its conclusions are worrying in many respects, particularly in the light of the findings that regulation (ec) no 1798/2003 on administrative cooperation in the field of vat is not an effective instrument for administrative cooperation given that several member states impede its implementation and that the commission's role is limited but it is imperative that the commission initiates infringement proceedings against the member state which delays the transmission of information. the commission's proposals for amending the vat directive and the regulation on administrative cooperation on vat are a good thing. i support the creation of a task force composed of the relevant commission services, the dg taxation and customs union and the european anti-fraud office (olaf).

in writing. for more than three years now, the working time directive has been the subject of a tug of war between the council and the european parliament. the agreement reached by the 27 eu labour ministers provides for a maximum working week of 48 hours, but with the possibility of derogating in certain cases for up to 65 hours per week. such a solution is unacceptable and as a socialist i have to make the concerns of millions of workers known and to fight so that this maximum of 48 hours is not subject to any exceptions, but also so that guard hours are taken into account in the calculation of these hours. i shall therefore vote in favour of the cercas report, hoping that if there is conciliation we will reach a text which achieves a real balance between the protection of workers and the optimisation of work organisation. we european socialists will in any case continue to defend the workers, because europe needs more than ever a social model that meets the needs of the most vulnerable citizens, and in particular those who are most affected by the consequences of the economic and financial crisis.

in writing. in coastal regions, particularly in the outermost regions, tourism, often the main economic activity, can have negative effects due to seasonality and lack of skills, low integration between the coast and the interior, low economic diversification and the impoverishment of natural and cultural heritage. solutions exist, in the form of the following actions. combating seasonality by offering alternative forms of tourism (business, cultural, medical, sporting, rural) while protecting coastal heritage. to seek an integrated approach between coastal tourism and the community's cohesion, maritime, fisheries, environmental, transport and energy policies, in order to create synergies and reinforce the coherence of projects. improve the quality of infrastructure by facilitating accessibility outside the peak season, while combating the effects of climate change by developing sustainable local public transport. to improve the quality of service by improving vocational training and to promote a tourist offer that responds to market developments in order to distinguish itself from the competition. promote new tourist destinations, including the outermost regions, and make coastal tourism the main focus of the european maritime day (20 may) or the 'european destinations of excellence' project.
in writing. whether traditional or new, media play an important role in our daily lives. in view of this, european citizens should be able to understand, analyse and evaluate the flood of information and images they receive so that they can make the best use of them. these skills are all the more necessary now that the use of the internet has become widespread and the consumer is no longer a mere spectator but is increasingly becoming an actor in this process. the report before us, which i personally support, is part of this context. it reflects the political will to act to safeguard the rights and freedoms of everyone in the digital environment. including all citizens, especially the youngest, this report advocates the establishment of a high level of media literacy. it aims at training adapted to each type of media, while reaffirming the right of access to information and communication technologies for all. it promotes quality training that emphasises a responsible attitude and respect for intellectual property rights. furthermore, as it contributes to the achievement of the lisbon objectives, media education is an indispensable asset for the development of an active and conscious citizenship.
in writing. the europeists see the use of labour and settlement immigration as the miracle solution to the problems of labour shortages and the low birth rates in all member states. this madness is an admission of impotence. the present europe offers nothing to meet the challenges it faces. the new europe must instead promote an economic and social policy of protection and national and community preferences, a family and natalist policy, a foreign policy of development aid to third countries in order to enable these countries, which are the source of massive emigration, to fix their populations by significantly improving their living standards. the european training foundation is an agency of the european union whose purpose is to contribute to the development of education and training systems in the union's partner countries. this would be highly commendable if it did not actually consist in preparing these non-european countries for their access to the european labour market. we do not want any more immigration from third countries, or even from non-european candidate countries such as turkey, an asian and muslim country which we refuse to accept into the european union.

in writing. we have had the opportunity to say here on several occasions that the simple objective of reducing the european union's dependence on imports of gas or hydrocarbons could in itself justify the promotion of renewable energies. the compromise presented today, which is part of the 'energy-climate package', is like all compromises: neither totally bad nor totally satisfactory. it is not entirely satisfactory, in particular, for biofuels, second generation or not: insufficient guarantees as regards competition with food production, vague as regards possible changes in the use of land, silence on the actual carbon balance of these energy sources... it is not entirely convincing on the "guarantee of origin" supposed to identify green electricity, especially when we know the reality of what the electricity supply is, the dubious advertising on the subject and the significant additional cost to consumers. finally, it is not at all satisfactory in terms of the social consequences: we would like to be sure, as with the whole of this legislative package adopted at the beginning of a global crisis which promises to be deep and long, that if the economic situation so requires, the interests of the citizens and workers of europe will take precedence over all other considerations.
in writing. the european union's only firm commitment is to reduce its emissions by 20% by 2020 compared to 1990. this is a drop of about 12% compared to today. taking into account that two thirds of this reduction can be achieved through carbon offsetting mechanisms - i.e. the purchase of carbon credits on the international market - the eu has committed to achieving only a 4% reduction on its territory. this is not enough to move international negotiations forward. another lack of compromise is the lack of a firm commitment to support developing countries in their efforts to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions. the eu has made a purely voluntary commitment to use half of the revenues from the auctioning of polluting rights for climate. a decline in income due to the many exemptions granted to industrialists. the compromise states that part of this money could go to developing countries for european countries that wish to do so. this is a voluntary commitment only. a very weak commitment to an issue that is crucial in international negotiations.

in writing. the energy and climate package we are voting on today is meant to be symbolic of an energy, economic and technological transition. and it is: the various measures proposed will profoundly change the energy mix of the member states, lead to a common or even a single energy policy, entail enormous financial costs, weigh on the competitiveness of our industries and thus on employment in europe, increase energy prices for individuals and businesses, have a significant impact on national budgets... it is true that many derogations have been provided for to avoid relocations. but this is not enough: in the current context of a widespread crisis which looks likely to be long-lasting, a general safeguard clause is needed to ensure that the interests of the european economy and workers will at least provisionally take precedence over environmental objectives as a matter of necessity. it is also necessary to provide for a general re-examination of the process if the forthcoming international negotiations fail, and in particular if the united states and the major emerging countries do not commit themselves in the same proportions. because then, the economic suicide of europe, which emits only 15% of the world's "artificial" greenhouse gases, would be useless.
in writing. i voted in favour of the four directives in the energy-climate package because it was important that the eu adopted these texts before 2009 and the international negotiations. deferring would have delayed the passage of the act, accumulated delays without guaranteeing a better text. it is a yes :- because the 3x20 targets (20% ghg reduction, 20% reduction in energy consumed, 20% renewable energy) and the transition to a 30% ghg reduction in the event of a more ambitious international agreement are confirmed; - critical because the texts proposed by the council are lagging behind the commission's proposals and risk not reaching the announced targets - staggered over time, large number of derogations, possibility of financing gas reductions outside the eu, which delays the necessary decarbonisation of our industries, economies and development modes;- vigilance because if the targets are not met along the way, the ep will have to impose new policies;- first step. i always thought that the ets would not transform our industry, our activities to reduce their ecological footprints. it is necessary to provide for substantial research and innovation funding, customs standards and tariffs to combat environmental dumping, and industrial policies and european funds to accompany the changes.
in writing. the common position on working time put to the vote by the council was a real setback for workers' rights and a real danger for our european social model. the socialist rapporteur, alejandro cercas, who i voted for, has succeeded in bringing down this conservative and reactionary view of the world of work, worthy of the 19th century, with a large majority. with the socialists as a whole, i have supported a series of amendments which guarantee essential advances for workers' rights. we have thus obtained the repeal of the so-called opt-out clause, which allowed freedom from the limitation of working time to impose up to 65 hours of work per week. similarly, because guard time cannot be considered as a time of rest, we have allowed it to be counted as working time. we have also obtained guarantees of compensatory rest and reconciliation between family and working life. this great victory of the european socialists, supported by the trade unions, is a victory for all europeans. the europe that protects is the europe that embraces major social advances such as those of today.
in writing. the european parliament's vote today is of paramount importance. the maximum working time in europe will remain at 48 hours, which will allow countries with more favourable conditions for employees to keep it at that level (such as france, which is at 35 hours). the council wanted to raise this limit to 65 hours. the left and workers' forces such as the etuc can take pride in this victory. doctors and medical students should not be forgotten because this victory is also theirs. the medical staff's duty time will be included in working time. the vote by a large majority will allow the 27 meps to make their position clear to the 27 ministers in the conciliation committee.
in writing. in the current context of crisis and social insecurity for workers, the council is today putting to the vote in parliament a common position which represents a real danger to the foundations of the european social model by weakening working time standards. the introduction of a waiver clause for the 48-hour week and the non-inclusion of guard time in working time risk creating a two-tiered social europe, between workers who will be able to benefit from social protection in their member states and others who will not be able to refuse to have their social rights reduced. contrary to the speech of the commission and some of the council of the european union states presenting the free choice of opt-out as a step forward, i have chosen to support the amendments of the rapporteur cercas, which are the expression of parliament's position at first reading in 2004. the latter require the repeal of the opt-out clause 36 months after the entry into force of the directive, the calculation of childcare time as working time (recognised by the ecj) and guarantees for compensatory rest and reconciliation between family and professional life.
in writing. i supported the position of the rapporteur, mr cercas, because the organisation of working time is an essential issue for the daily lives of european citizens. the massive demonstration by european trade unions yesterday in strasbourg showed their commitment to better protection for workers. several elements of this report have caught my attention and should be defended, such as the end of the derogation from the 48-hour working week currently in force in the european union. like other european socialists, i am convinced that reconciling work and family life is very important for the development of citizens. the cercas report, with its social advances, is a step in the right direction by removing the overly liberal measures applied in some member states, which would like to see them extended to the whole of the european union.
in writing. the commission's proposal for a directive is perhaps typical of what brussels europe calls flexibility and adaptability and dares to call social: opt-out (i.e. the possibility of going beyond the norms) for states or individuals, a limit of 78 hours worked per week, exclusion of guard duty from the calculation of hours worked, calculation of time by contract and not by person... in short, everything to allow the exploitation of people in a context of crisis, unemployment rising again, impoverishment of employees. that is why we voted for the amendments of the committee on social affairs and also for some of those of our political opponents, because they seemed to us to be in the right direction, that is to say, in the direction of the workers. two further remarks, however: - the rapporteur seems to be much more motivated by the image parliament would give to the citizens if it did not adopt its report six months before the elections, than by the well-being of the citizens themselves; - vigilance must remain: there is no majority in the council to abolish the opt-out and the report adopted today, which is already a compromise, may not be the last on the subject.
in writing. the european commission's draft working time directive, which was repeatedly criticised and then rejected in 2005, was clearly an ultra-liberal and globalist tool whose ins and outs formed an antisocial panoply that could lead to deviations. in particular, the "opt-out" principle allows the maximum weekly working time of 48 hours to be overridden. the employee could be called upon to work up to 78 hours per week. the report by mr cercas seems to have sought to reach an acceptable compromise. as amended, it is intended primarily as a political message to european workers and trade unions. on the other hand, there is no mention of the difficulties encountered by other professions when working time is too short, as with the 35 hours. especially in the health professions: hospitals, emergency rooms... the question of the regulation of working time, of the freedom to work more or less, requires an answer that goes beyond neo-marxist or ultra-liberal ideology to a more pragmatic and realistic approach. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council on the basis of a proposal from the commission.
in writing. i voted for all the amendments proposed by my socialist colleague cercas to defend the social acquis in europe, in particular the following three issues which i consider to be fundamental. the limitation of the working week to 48 hours is an imperative which we have defended to the letter, since the member states cannot impose on their workers working conditions which do not respect fundamental social rights. maintaining duty time as working time: this concerned the safety and health of healthcare workers, but also of firefighters, other sectors subject to duty time and all european citizens. promoting work-life balance: last but not least, this enables our citizens to achieve the balance necessary for their well-being. i have committed myself with my socialist colleagues to defending the social rights of my fellow citizens: this is a resounding victory for the european socialists against the proposals of the european council which they consider intolerable. as my colleague mr cercas has said, we are giving him a chance to correct a wrong decision.
in writing. the global crisis is undermining the fundamental rights of workers and the demand for a social europe is therefore growing among our fellow europeans. however, european governments continue to ignore this reality. i therefore welcome the adoption today of the directive on working time, which can provide a response to these social distortions. this is a strong message from the european parliament to the council. governments must now assume their responsibilities and meet the expectations of our citizens. the text provides, among other things, for the establishment of a working week which may in no case exceed 48 hours throughout the european union. the aim is to set a maximum for the whole of europe, and this will not affect the states which have more favourable provisions. other measures include the consideration of on-call time, including the period of inactivity, as working time. finally, we can also welcome the removal of the opt-out clause.
in writing. amendments nos 23 and 24 to the cercas report on sunday work were declared inadmissible on the grounds of respect for the principle of subsidiarity: this is an excellent decision which i fully support. it seemed to me inappropriate for the european union to legislate on sundays and impose a uniform solution on its member states, when negotiation on a case-by-case basis allows voluntary and acceptable solutions to be found. i think that it is essential to set a framework for the possibilities of working on sundays, but i think that this must be done at the level of the member states, taking into account the specific social characteristics and the nature of the activities. it seems to me that it is equally essential to take account of the local economic context, for tourist areas, mountain or thermal areas, where activity is essentially seasonal: the opening of shops on certain sundays of the year makes perfect sense here. this approach based on free choice is the one adopted by the french government and will make it possible to find fair and balanced solutions on a case-by-case basis. in reaffirming the application of the principle of subsidiarity, the european parliament decided not to impede those policies which take account of these different economic and social contexts.
in writing. the ayala sender report is a new instrument for the prosecution of motorists: cross-border prosecution of serious offences (but strangely not of driving under the influence of drugs!), imposition on the national authorities by brussels of the number and place of the annual checks to be carried out, harmonisation of sanctions, random means of appeal, information and access to these means of appeal not being guaranteed in the language of the person prosecuted, possibilities for extending the scope of the directive to other offences (maybe overtaking of drivers?)... despite the claims, you're not interested in saving lives, you're interested in getting the fines back into the state coffers. if your concern was really safety, and not purely financial, it seems to me that the facts to be relied upon should be about foreign drivers responsible for fatal accidents, and not just about the offences they commit, the number of which is increasing mechanically by the multiplication of automatic radar. there is not even a study of the effects of the equivalent bilateral agreements which have existed, sometimes for several years, such as between france and germany or france and luxembourg.
in writing. the taxation, penalisation and systematic flogging of motorists seems to be without limit. we know, in fact, that it is not a question of punishing those who do wrong but those who do wrong. the sad and unfortunate requirement of "quotas" and "numbers" to be met by the police forces only aggravates an often excessive police repression. in addition, while there are many differences between the member states in the conditions for withdrawing a driving licence, and while the scale of offences and fines in the field of road safety varies from one country to another, europe wants to establish an electronic system for the exchange of information between the member states on offences committed on their territory, in order to penalize motorists even more. while it is good to see a reduction in the number of road accidents, it is important to ensure that these new legislative measures are not accompanied by infringements of freedoms, illegalities, irregularities or inequalities.

the european parliament has a duty to protect the environment. mr president, mr vice-president of the commission, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, of course our group will vote for the report proposed by mrs van den burg, and i congratulate her on her work, which we know is always very good. i would like to draw attention to the fact that small and mediumsized enterprises are not necessarily in favour of the abolition of accounting requirements. in this connection, we receive many e-mails saying: "be careful, simplification is useful, but it must not have a boomerang effect". let me explain. accounting must be simplified, and that is the sense of the resolution which says that the commission must propose to us, as soon as possible, and in particular before the end of 2009, an accounting framework adapted to small and mediumsized enterprises. but that doesn't mean total immunity. why would you do that? firstly, accounting gives the head of a company the opportunity, at least once a year, to take stock of the situation of his company. accounting is also a very useful element in inter-company credit. it's also what banks ask for when they give out loans. there are the tax obligations. so let's not fool small business owners by telling them that we're going to save them a lot of money, a lot of time if they don't have to keep accounts anymore. we're going to disasters. what is needed is an accounting framework that is suitable for small businesses and that frees them from excessive or unnecessary obligations. but i think the greatest simplification, commissioner, would be to apply once and for all the rule that information is requested once in each member state and that companies are not periodically asked to make the same slips, the same printed forms, to give the administrations information they already have. this is how we can help businessmen, by ensuring that they have accounting rules which are adapted to their situation and free them from totally unnecessary administrative work.

in writing. in the community budget for 2009, we socialists proposed and got a preparatory action to develop social tourism in europe. the project responds to the fact that many citizens are excluded from travel for economic reasons and that it is necessary to correct this inequality by guaranteeing access to holidays for all. but it also has a usefulness in terms of spatial planning and local development. by combining social diversity and local development and by facilitating access to audiences for whom tourism is difficult, social tourism enhances the profitability of the tourism sector. it thus enables the development of off-season tourism, particularly in regions where the sector is highly seasonal, and encourages the creation of more permanent jobs in this economic sector. social and associative tourism illustrates that there is indeed an intermediate sector between the leisure market and the insolvent economy and that economic relevance is not incompatible with accessibility to the greatest number. through exchanges between european citizens, it also contributes to the strengthening of european citizenship. this is the importance of this sector, both in terms of economic impact and in terms of citizen resources.
in writing. the problem, according to the rapporteur, does not seem to be so much the removal of legal or administrative obstacles to the professional mobility of european workers within the european union as the fact that this mobility is not general and above all compulsory. we are being invited to a great population meltdown, accelerating the disappearance of the nations of europe. the idea is wage competition, social dumping and harmonization of wages through the bottom. the creation of a european social security card with very vague outlines is designed to jeopardize and dismantle national social protection systems. ask those french workers who were offered, a few years ago, to save their jobs on the condition that they decide to give up everything to go to work in romania for a few hundred euros a month what they think of your mobility! attempting to solve the tax problems or the acquisition of social rights of frontier workers, or those whose careers have been in several member states, is indeed a matter for the european union. but not at the cost of social uncertainty.
in writing. i found the compromise on the thyssen report too lax in terms of safety rules or the presence of chemicals in toys. in addition, the amendment calling for the conformity of toys to be checked by independent bodies has not been passed, whereas it seems obvious that the safety of children is being put before the interests of a few large industrial groups. i have always advocated stricter controls on products in general, and a fortiori on products for children. the disappointing final content of this text - far removed from our initial ambitions, even if it does make some progress - has therefore led me to abstain in the vote.
in writing. the frontex agency, which is responsible for the common management of the external borders of the european union, and in particular the fight against illegal immigration, owes its existence solely to the dismantling of internal border controls and the will of europe in brussels and the governments of the member states to pursue an active immigration policy. it is not certain that such a community agency would be a real added value compared to conventional intergovernmental cooperation, if one judges it, in another area, by the differences in efficiency and usefulness between europol and interpol. the agency's tasks seem to be becoming more numerous, more complex and, in fact, insurmountable until the root of the problem is tackled: on the one hand, despite the perils of the journey and the difficulties encountered on the ground, europe remains a social and financial eldorado for those seeking illegal immigration; on the other hand, the european union is a major source of funding for the european union's efforts to combat illegal immigration. on the other hand, the insufficient cooperation policy is endangered by the immigration of qualified professionals organized by the eu itself. the vacuum pumps of immigration and current policies must therefore be stopped. finally, i would like to stress that there are local associations which are fighting against illegal emigration, such as the alcec of mr emile bomba in cameroon, which deserve help and support.
in writing. recital b of this report states that 'illegal immigration is a common european challenge'. this is especially true when thousands of illegal immigrants are pouring into italian, greek and spanish coasts each month in search of european eldorado. in the face of this challenge, which, it should be recalled, has its main origin in the schengen agreements which abolished checks at the internal borders of the member states, the union's response has been the creation of a european agency for the management of external borders: frontex. yesterday, frontex was a mere gadget with no resources, staff or powers, but today it seems that its mandate allows it to support joint return operations and to make a small contribution to the daily fight against illegal immigration. but we must remember that it will be useless to close a few loopholes allowing illegal immigrants to cross if all the member states of the union do not react together to denounce the schengen agreements and re-establish real controls at all their land and sea borders.
in writing. counterfeiting is not just a problem of respect for intellectual property rights. as the rapporteur points out, this phenomenon kills the incentive to innovate, causes the disappearance of thousands of skilled and unskilled jobs in europe, and lays the foundations for a clandestine economy controlled by organised crime. such illegal practices may also endanger the safety and health of consumers or cause serious damage to the environment. the problem of the quality and hazard of imported products, whose counterfeiting only increases the risks by misleading consumers, is more general. the countries of origin are clearly identified, china being the most important. the union sometimes even agrees to open its markets to products which do not meet the standards it imposes on its own producers, such as chlorinated chicken, which is cheaper to produce than chickens subject to veterinary checks. in the arsenal of measures proposed by the rapporteur (bilateral or multilateral agreements, cooperation with the countries of origin, cooperation between the european services concerned, etc.), two are obviously missing: trade sanctions against the states which accept these practices; the establishment of a general national and european preference!
in writing. this report on cross-border use and the recognition of authentic instruments is likely to cause confusion in several respects. it should be noted, first and foremost, that the concept of an authentic instrument does not exist in common law systems. in england and wales, solicitors act as notaries. there are also professional notaries (scrivener notaries). they cannot issue authentic instruments and are only empowered to certify signatures. in its efforts to harmonize the legal professions, the commission has little regard for the differences in the very nature of the legal systems of the member states. unfortunately, this political will does not contribute to legal certainty as a whole. europe must preserve the identity of its peoples and the values and traditions of each of its states. the biggest mistake would be for it to build itself against its people.
